## C45. Final pre-Codex visual-resource approval board requirements

Before the exhaustive implementation prompt is issued, produce one compact approval board/document containing the following concrete choices. This board is a gate, not an optional moodboard.

| Gate | Approval artifact |
| --- | --- |
| Palette | Render the same candidate tokens on: hero architecture scene, populated dashboard charts, 390px assessment choice state. User approves exact HEX roles. |
| Typography | Render Mona Sans 2 actual strings: “Your work leaves evidence.”, Work Worlds names, one long adaptive question, dashboard labels/numerals, mobile navigation. Approve width/weight/optical ranges. |
| Hero media | Show retained architecture + retained laptop/human + 2–4 candidates for optional third process/code fragment. Approve exact crop/role. |
| Work Worlds | Show all six chosen photographs in their proposed active aspect/crop plus mobile crop. Reject any that feel generic/low-quality. |
| Career media | Profession-specific set for major public/demo careers. Avoid reusing developer image for every technical role. |
| Illustrations | Show 6–10 scenes from one coherent family (or custom set) including welcome, analytics empty, development/team, completion, report/privacy. Approve style first, then exact assets. |
| Charts | Show static visual mock/layout of Big Five lollipop, RIASEC radar+ranking, Work Values bars, trend line and career breakdown in the final palette. |
| Hero/Work Worlds mobile | Show 390px static frames before code: hero first viewport, first Work World active state, profile lens state, dashboard zero state. |

## C46. Closing principle — completeness without paralysis

The requirement to research at every step is not permission to browse forever. Research is attached to a decision and ends when the uncertainty relevant to that decision is sufficiently resolved. The project moves through explicit gates: understand → compare → decide → specify → implement → render → accept/reject → record learning. What Phase 3C forbids is skipping the first four steps and asking a coding agent to discover the design in CSS.

The best evidence that this Brain is working will not be the length of this file. It will be that the next implementation does **not** recreate any of the rejected visual fingerprints under a different class name, that its motion is visible and understandable at the center of the viewport, that mobile feels independently designed, that dashboard charts answer real questions, that images are sized/cropped as art direction, and that the resulting website could not plausibly be mistaken for an unrelated AI-generated SaaS template.


# C47. Phase 3C research-source interpretation archive — what each source changes in our decisions

## C47 — Lusion Oryzo BTS Part 1 — concept/creative direction

The important contribution is continuity. Lusion describes learning that a beautiful isolated section does not create a premium experience if the sections do not belong to the same world. They centered one protagonist and worked hard on transitions between substantially different scenes. For Personality Assessor this validates the evidence-as-protagonist model: architecture/professional evidence does not need to remain literally the same photograph everywhere, but the idea of evidence should survive its transformation into context, question, signal, profile and career relationship. The direct implementation consequence is that our flagship sequences require shared actors and scene handoffs rather than independent “finished sections.” It also reinforces that responsiveness is part of transition design; a scene transition that only works at 1440×900 is not a successful concept.

**Personality-specific decision:** This source is used only for the principle described above. Before any future implementation step, re-check the current version of the source if the technology, compatibility, license or live behavior could have changed.

## C47 — Lusion Oryzo BTS Part 2 — production pipeline

The key principle is that the pipeline follows the idea. Oryzo used heavy 3D/rendering/scanning experiments because its visual thesis required a physical-feeling product world. Personality does not inherit those technologies. Instead, we inherit the selection logic: first define what must be seen, then choose the cheapest medium that preserves it. A CV artifact and profile chart are better DOM/SVG than WebGL. A professional photograph is better served as responsive AVIF/WebP than a 3D reconstruction. A scroll carry is better owned by GSAP/DOM transforms than by a realtime renderer. This is how we can use fewer technologies while reaching a higher level of craft.

**Personality-specific decision:** This source is used only for the principle described above. Before any future implementation step, re-check the current version of the source if the technology, compatibility, license or live behavior could have changed.

## C47 — Lusion Oryzo BTS Part 3 — UX/UI/illustration

This source matters because Lusion explicitly rejected an early clean, abstract “Awwwards-like” direction as lifeless. The believable desk/world and protagonist made the site feel specific. They also describe “design without ego”: when imagery/world is rich, typography/UI can become restrained. This maps directly to our hero and color correction. We should not add five labels, a bright CTA, tinted badges and multiple border treatments around already-rich architecture photography. It also supports our illustration quality gate: illustration becomes a human layer integrated into a designed world, not a stock vector pasted into a card.

**Personality-specific decision:** This source is used only for the principle described above. Before any future implementation step, re-check the current version of the source if the technology, compatibility, license or live behavior could have changed.

## C47 — Dogstudio Zoox case study

Zoox is useful because the actual product form generated the site’s frames, borders and buttons. The transferable lesson is not rounded corners; it is that product truth can generate the shape grammar. Personality does not have a physical object, so its native geometry should come from evidence/artifacts, continuous dimensions, profiles and relationships. If a shape exists solely because it is fashionable, it should not survive the anti-copy test. This case also documents collaborative design/technical decision-making, reinforcing that feasibility should be discussed while the concept is being resolved rather than after static design is “finished.”

**Personality-specific decision:** This source is used only for the principle described above. Before any future implementation step, re-check the current version of the source if the technology, compatibility, license or live behavior could have changed.

## C47 — Dogstudio Virgin Galactic case study

This case is relevant to our scene architecture because it had to bridge heavy immersive sequences and content-dense sections while minimizing performance/loading impact. Dogstudio discusses multiple WebGL subscenes, a shared render architecture and transitions as a technical priority. Personality does not need WebGL, but it absolutely needs the same boundary discipline: when Work Worlds releases into Context, or Context carries into Living Profile, the transition must be planned as a first-class system. The case also shows that optimizing perception often means precomputing/using cheaper visual techniques rather than insisting on realtime fidelity—an important progressive-enhancement lesson.

**Personality-specific decision:** This source is used only for the principle described above. Before any future implementation step, re-check the current version of the source if the technology, compatibility, license or live behavior could have changed.

## C47 — Dogstudio Geske case study

Geske uses visualization to explain product features that would otherwise be difficult to understand. The transferable rule is that special effects earn their cost by explaining. Personality charts and scroll transitions should similarly make a relationship clearer: which evidence becomes a question, how one signal enters four readings, how career fit decomposes. If an animation only makes a panel feel “alive,” it does not meet this bar.

**Personality-specific decision:** This source is used only for the principle described above. Before any future implementation step, re-check the current version of the source if the technology, compatibility, license or live behavior could have changed.

## C47 — White Desert live/reference research

White Desert remains the strongest image-world reference because it lets the environment persist while foreground content changes. The visual lesson is not “use full-screen photos.” It is how image scale, sequence and environmental continuity reduce the feeling of disconnected sections. Personality can create a conceptual rather than literal persistent world: professional evidence keeps reappearing in different forms. White Desert also demonstrates that a restrained UI can let photography carry color, supporting the Phase 3C option to remove a dominant marketing accent.

**Personality-specific decision:** This source is used only for the principle described above. Before any future implementation step, re-check the current version of the source if the technology, compatibility, license or live behavior could have changed.

## C47 — GSAP ScrollTrigger official documentation

ScrollTrigger remains the strongest tool for precise pinned scenic timelines because pinning, scrubbed progress, labels/snap behavior, refresh mechanics and directional progress are first-class. The most important engineering note for our implementation is to pin a stable stage and animate its descendants rather than transforming the pinned root. We also need to avoid high-frequency layout reads in `onUpdate` where possible; timeline measurements should be prepared and refreshed. GSAP is the owner of flagship theatre, not a universal hover/reveal library.

**Personality-specific decision:** This source is used only for the principle described above. Before any future implementation step, re-check the current version of the source if the technology, compatibility, license or live behavior could have changed.

## C47 — Lenis official documentation

Lenis provides smooth interpolation while retaining native-scroll semantics and offers direct GSAP integration. For Personality it is a candidate replacement for ScrollSmoother on fine-pointer marketing routes, not a required brand feature. We must validate anchor links, focus, route restoration, pin behavior, nested scroll areas and low-powered devices. Touch stays native by default. If Lenis fails those tests, native scroll is preferable to a “smoother” experience with accessibility or control problems.

**Personality-specific decision:** This source is used only for the principle described above. Before any future implementation step, re-check the current version of the source if the technology, compatibility, license or live behavior could have changed.

## C47 — Anime.js v4 documentation

Anime.js has a real timeline and scroll observer/synchronization system and therefore deserves to be understood rather than ignored. However, knowing a tool is not the same as assigning it a job. Phase 3C does not currently identify a flagship sequence where Anime is clearly superior to existing GSAP. Its likely role is isolated SVG/typographic/illustration choreography where its API makes the local animation cleaner. It must never own the same transform/progress state as GSAP in one scene.

**Personality-specific decision:** This source is used only for the principle described above. Before any future implementation step, re-check the current version of the source if the technology, compatibility, license or live behavior could have changed.

## C47 — Motion for React documentation

Motion is much better aligned with authenticated UI state than with our pinned marketing theatre. Its layout/layoutId features can animate real React layout changes, remain interruptible and support shared-element continuity. That makes it ideal for career list→detail, active tabs/lenses, dashboard rearrangements, dialogs, accordions and selection states. This helps separate “product motion” from “narrative scroll motion,” reducing the temptation to run everything through ScrollTrigger.

**Personality-specific decision:** This source is used only for the principle described above. Before any future implementation step, re-check the current version of the source if the technology, compatibility, license or live behavior could have changed.

## C47 — Native View Transition API / React Router integration

View Transitions can create route/shared-element continuity with graceful fallback in unsupported environments. They are useful when old/new DOM differs significantly and a snapshot transition is acceptable, for example carrying a selected career thumbnail/title into detail. They are not a replacement for interruptible in-page layout animation or scroll theatre. Our architecture should prefer React Router’s own integration instead of layering Barba over the SPA.

**Personality-specific decision:** This source is used only for the principle described above. Before any future implementation step, re-check the current version of the source if the technology, compatibility, license or live behavior could have changed.

## C47 — CSS scroll-driven animations

Native scroll/view timelines are strategically useful for noncritical progressive effects, especially simple progress/opacity/translate relationships. Their existence does not justify moving core storytelling away from a well-tested JS owner before browser support and debugging behavior are sufficient. We can use them where failure means “the subtle effect does not run,” not where failure means “the visitor cannot understand the product sequence.”

**Personality-specific decision:** This source is used only for the principle described above. Before any future implementation step, re-check the current version of the source if the technology, compatibility, license or live behavior could have changed.

## C47 — Embla Carousel

Embla proves that a small carousel engine can support variable widths, horizontal/vertical axes, drag-free behavior, progress and accessibility plugins without requiring a giant UI framework. Our default remains native scroll snap because it is lighter and directly manipulable. Embla becomes justified only if Work Worlds mobile or another gallery requires coordinated selected state, progress, velocity or snapping that native CSS cannot deliver reliably enough.

**Personality-specific decision:** This source is used only for the principle described above. Before any future implementation step, re-check the current version of the source if the technology, compatibility, license or live behavior could have changed.

## C47 — Rive runtime/state-machine research

Rive can package vector art and state machines into an interactive illustration system and has official React runtimes. The tradeoff is meaningful runtime/WASM weight, especially for richer renderers. Personality should therefore use static SVG/DOM by default. Rive is interesting if we later commission an authored “evidence becomes profile” illustration whose states genuinely respond to product data or user interaction. It is not justified for looping character motion.

**Personality-specific decision:** This source is used only for the principle described above. Before any future implementation step, re-check the current version of the source if the technology, compatibility, license or live behavior could have changed.

## C47 — Apple HIG — charts/layout/color

Apple’s guidance reinforces three Phase 3C principles: information importance should influence space; chart type follows the comparison/trend/relationship question; and color should be used consistently and not carry multiple meanings. It also supports progressive disclosure on smaller screens. The relevant transfer is not Apple visual styling but task clarity: one mobile state should own attention, and a chart should communicate without forcing hover or deciphering a legend.

**Personality-specific decision:** This source is used only for the principle described above. Before any future implementation step, re-check the current version of the source if the technology, compatibility, license or live behavior could have changed.

## C47 — Carbon data visualization/dashboard guidance

Carbon is useful as a disciplined operational reference. It distinguishes lollipop/radar/line/bar/part-to-whole chart purposes and emphasizes dashboard hierarchy. This validates our representation map and the move away from six equal MetricCards. Carbon is not the target skin; its value is semantic chart selection, labeling, accessibility and dense information behavior.

**Personality-specific decision:** This source is used only for the principle described above. Before any future implementation step, re-check the current version of the source if the technology, compatibility, license or live behavior could have changed.

## C47 — Responsive image / picture guidance

The web platform explicitly supports art direction through `<picture>` and different sources/crops. This makes the “desktop image squeezed into phone” failure avoidable. Our existing ResponsiveImage component already moves in this direction; Phase 3C must enrich the media registry so mobile crop is a deliberate creative decision rather than a filename convention. Intrinsic dimensions and responsive sizes also protect layout stability.

**Personality-specific decision:** This source is used only for the principle described above. Before any future implementation step, re-check the current version of the source if the technology, compatibility, license or live behavior could have changed.

## C47 — Mona Sans variable typography research

Mona Sans provides weight, width and optical axes broad enough to create distinct marketing, reading, UI and data roles inside one family. The lesson is not that Mona Sans is universally premium; it is that we can author character through axis behavior rather than introducing multiple fashionable faces. The font still requires real-string testing, especially long adaptive questions and dense chart labels.

**Personality-specific decision:** This source is used only for the principle described above. Before any future implementation step, re-check the current version of the source if the technology, compatibility, license or live behavior could have changed.

## C47 — Pexels / illustration licensing research

The production media system must include rights/provenance rather than treating a URL as enough. Pexels broadly permits free commercial use and editing under its license, but recognizable people/property/trademarks can still raise context-specific issues and cannot imply endorsement. Illustration sources differ: DrawKit and ManyPixels are attractive for no-attribution commercial use, while Storyset’s free route typically requires attribution. Exact licensing is checked again at selection time because terms can change.

**Personality-specific decision:** This source is used only for the principle described above. Before any future implementation step, re-check the current version of the source if the technology, compatibility, license or live behavior could have changed.

# C48. Mobile composition micro-specifications — 390px primary canvas

### C48 — Opening viewport

Header height is compact; brand + Menu/Sign in action remains clear. Headline uses 2–4 authored lines depending final copy. Architecture crop occupies a meaningful visual block without pushing all CTA content beyond the first useful scroll. The human/laptop fragment is smaller and either overlaps the lower edge deliberately or appears as the next beat. No horizontal media carousel appears simply because desktop has multiple actors.

**Mobile rejection test:** Does this feel like an intentional app/page at 390px, or can the desktop layout be inferred as a stack underneath it? If the latter is true, redesign again.

### C48 — Work Worlds active state

One work photograph dominates, around 78–86vw depending crop, with a visible next peek. World name and one sentence are immediately adjacent. Swipe/drag has direct previous/next or accessible index. Momentum does not leave the user between two unreadable panels. The phone does not simulate a 4000px pinned desktop sequence.

**Mobile rejection test:** Does this feel like an intentional app/page at 390px, or can the desktop layout be inferred as a stack underneath it? If the latter is true, redesign again.

### C48 — Context intake

A compact document/evidence preview uses the full content width minus 18–20px gutters. Evidence groups are rows/tags only when semantically correct, with edit affordances. The user can proceed or change source without navigating a horizontal composition.

**Mobile rejection test:** Does this feel like an intentional app/page at 390px, or can the desktop layout be inferred as a stack underneath it? If the latter is true, redesign again.

### C48 — Assessment question

Question number/progress sits in a quiet header; question text begins near the top third rather than dead center if it is long. Answer choices are reachable without precision. Continue/Back respect the software keyboard and safe area. Save/Exit is available but visually subordinate.

**Mobile rejection test:** Does this feel like an intentional app/page at 390px, or can the desktop layout be inferred as a stack underneath it? If the latter is true, redesign again.

### C48 — Living Profile

A lens selector can be horizontally compact or a dropdown/segmented control depending width. One visualization owns the stage. Labels below the radar/lollipop are readable without pinch zoom. Swiping between lenses is optional; buttons always work.

**Mobile rejection test:** Does this feel like an intentional app/page at 390px, or can the desktop layout be inferred as a stack underneath it? If the latter is true, redesign again.

### C48 — Dashboard zero state

User/context name, active-session status or zero count, illustration and primary action appear before secondary explanation. The illustration is cropped/positioned as an editorial actor, not a huge image pushing the action below multiple screens.

**Mobile rejection test:** Does this feel like an intentional app/page at 390px, or can the desktop layout be inferred as a stack underneath it? If the latter is true, redesign again.

### C48 — Dashboard populated

Latest profile/next action first; one Big Five plot; one career direction summary. Secondary readings and history follow. The bottom nav stays visible but does not cover chart labels or buttons.

**Mobile rejection test:** Does this feel like an intentional app/page at 390px, or can the desktop layout be inferred as a stack underneath it? If the latter is true, redesign again.

### C48 — Analytics

Each visualization is a dedicated module with readable axes/labels. Multi-series trend may use a dimension selector or small multiples rather than forcing five colored lines into a 320px plot. A “View data” action exposes the accessible table.

**Mobile rejection test:** Does this feel like an intentional app/page at 390px, or can the desktop layout be inferred as a stack underneath it? If the latter is true, redesign again.

### C48 — Career Explorer

Role list is the first view. Each row provides role name, truthful fit/status and maybe one concise reason. Selecting opens detail; shared-element transition is optional. Back returns to the exact list position.

**Mobile rejection test:** Does this feel like an intentional app/page at 390px, or can the desktop layout be inferred as a stack underneath it? If the latter is true, redesign again.

### C48 — Privacy

Controls are grouped by consequence, with full-width buttons only where action deserves it. Destructive account deletion is separated and confirmed. Explanatory text is compact enough that controls remain discoverable.

**Mobile rejection test:** Does this feel like an intentional app/page at 390px, or can the desktop layout be inferred as a stack underneath it? If the latter is true, redesign again.

### C48 — Footer

Terminal phrase uses mobile-specific line breaks and perhaps reduced size. Links are grouped with 44px targets. Any giant desktop type treatment that would cause overflow is explicitly replaced rather than clipped.

**Mobile rejection test:** Does this feel like an intentional app/page at 390px, or can the desktop layout be inferred as a stack underneath it? If the latter is true, redesign again.

# C49. Dashboard information architecture — zero, one-result, and longitudinal maturity states

The dashboard should evolve with data maturity instead of rendering one fixed grid and replacing dashes with numbers. Three maturity modes are explicitly designed.

## C49.1 — Maturity 0: no completed assessments

The dashboard explains what the user can do now, not what the future data might look like. Show real account/CV/session state, a quality illustration, the first-assessment action and the four reading families as an educational preview. Do not show empty trait charts as if 0 were a score. If an active assessment exists, Resume becomes the primary action and the current progress can be shown truthfully.

## C49.2 — Maturity 1: one completed assessment

The page can now show a real current profile but cannot honestly imply trends. Big Five, RIASEC, Work Values, Career Signals, top career relationships and next roadmap action are useful. “Change over time” is replaced by an invitation/explanation that longitudinal comparison unlocks after a future valid assessment. The page should feel complete rather than like half of the dashboard is disabled.

## C49.3 — Maturity 2+: longitudinal history

Trend visualization becomes legitimate. The dashboard may show a compact change summary and the Analytics route becomes richer. Even here, avoid interpreting small score changes as psychological “growth” unless methodology supports that claim. Lines show recorded values and dates; explanatory text remains cautious. History, report generation and roadmap completion become meaningful secondary evidence.

## C49.4 — Maturity-sensitive composition rule

The number and type of visible dashboard regions can change by maturity state. This is preferable to preserving a template grid with empty placeholders. Layout continuity comes from typography, navigation, data visualization language and identity—not from forcing the same rectangles to remain forever.

# C50. Phase 3C “done enough to code” threshold

Phase 3C research is sufficiently mature for implementation **only after** the remaining visual-resource approvals are resolved. General research has reached diminishing returns; the remaining uncertainty is concrete: final palette, exact third hero fragment if any, final Work Worlds/career imagery, exact illustration family/scenes, and any copy/data source blockers such as retention/question count. Once those are approved, the implementation prompt should be generated immediately rather than returning to generic inspiration browsing.

The next Codex run should be a rebuild, not a sequence of patches. It should preserve product/backend logic and source integrity while replacing rejected macro composition. The brief should be long enough to remove ambiguity. The implementation agent should be forbidden to make convenience substitutions such as “if image unavailable use placeholder,” “if chart data missing render zero,” “if mobile difficult stack desktop cards,” or “if motion difficult fade between states.” A blocker must be reported, not cosmetically hidden.


# C51. Final implementation-authority checklist and ecosystem transfer notes

This final appendix exists to prevent the Phase 3C decisions from becoming another research document that implementation only partially follows. It defines the questions the design authority must answer immediately before issuing any new Codex instruction set, and the questions the reviewer must answer immediately after the rendered implementation returns.

## C51.1 — Before writing the Codex prompt

Confirm that the **current Master Brain has actually been reopened**, not merely remembered. Search the document for the route, interaction, image type, dashboard representation and mobile state involved. Re-read the newest rejection ledger entries. A previous decision can become stale when the user rejects its visible consequence; therefore “the Brain once said this was okay” is not sufficient if Phase 3C superseded it.

Confirm the **current repository state**. The prompt must name the branch/commit or at least state that Codex is to inspect current `main` before editing. If another agent has changed media files, route structure, data hooks, CSS ownership, backend contracts or dependencies since the last audit, the design brief must adapt to the source truth rather than assume the old file map is unchanged.

Confirm that every visible **number and claim has provenance**. A dashboard field can display `0` when zero is the actual value; it cannot display zero because a JavaScript fallback converted missing data to zero. Public illustrative values are clearly labelled illustrative. Career fit, evidence confidence, report availability, scoring validity, roadmap completion and assessment counts are all rendered from their actual contracts. Marketing copy does not imply diagnosis, scientific validation, certainty, hiring fitness or privacy guarantees that have not been verified.

Confirm that every **visual resource is in the correct approval state**. `APPROVED` assets can be implemented. `SHORTLISTED` assets can be shown for review but must not silently ship as final. `REJECTED` assets are forbidden. `PENDING` means the design brief must either stop at that resource gate or explicitly use a temporary local research frame that will not be mistaken for final art direction. Coding agents do not get to convert “pending” into “I chose something similar.”

Confirm the **actor budget** for every scene. A scene should name its protagonist, supporting actors and quiet information. If the list is too long to describe clearly, the composition is probably too crowded. Hero actor count, Work Worlds active/neighbor count, dashboard primary/secondary zones and mobile state ownership are all explicit.

Confirm **inline and block geometry**. Width alone is never enough for a pinned or media-dominant scene. State the intended width range, maximum viewport height, aspect/crop logic, position, surrounding text area and what should remain visible in the same viewport. Test the mental frame at 1366×768 before coding.

Confirm **mobile as an independent composition**. The prompt must not say only “on mobile stack the elements.” It states what remains, what disappears, what is reordered, what becomes a separate detail view, which image crop/source changes, what input mechanism replaces desktop scroll theatre, and how the bottom navigation/safe area behaves.

Confirm **motion ownership**. Each animated relationship has one owner. Lenis or native scroll handles scroll feel; GSAP owns flagship pinned timelines; Motion owns application layout/shared-element state; Anime can own a local animation if specifically chosen; CSS may own progressive noncritical effects; Rive can own a purpose-built vector state machine if approved. No two systems fight over the same transform/progress.

Confirm **reduced motion**. Describe the alternate composition, not merely a boolean that changes duration. The visitor must receive the entire semantic story without long pin distances or mandatory motion.

Confirm **error/loading/empty states**. Hero media failure leaves readable copy/action. Auth media failure leaves the form. Analytics loading uses a truthful skeleton/spinner with stable geometry. Empty dashboard does not invent chart values. AI report unavailability does not erase deterministic profile data. Career service errors do not destroy the rest of the result.

Confirm the **anti-template test**. Remove the words “Personality Assessor” mentally. Could the same scene be sold unchanged to a generic AI productivity tool? If yes, strengthen the relationship to professional evidence, adaptive questioning, independent profile readings, career relationships or longitudinal development before coding.

## C51.2 — While Codex is implementing

Codex is allowed to choose safe low-level implementation details when they do not alter the experience: exact helper-function decomposition, memoization strategy, CSS variable organization, test-file placement, small accessibility utilities, and equivalent browser APIs. It is not allowed to choose a different image, font, accent, chart type, hero layout, scene order, mobile composition, animation meaning or user-facing claim because that alternative is easier.

If a specified mechanism proves technically unstable, Codex should preserve the **semantic visual idea** and report the mechanism change. For example, if a shared-element transition fails across a route boundary, a simpler direct transition can be proposed while preserving list→detail continuity. If a complex clipping sequence is unreliable on Safari, the mobile/tablet fallback can simplify the mask while keeping the same state order. What cannot happen is replacing a difficult scene with a grid of cards without reporting a deviation.

Do not ask Codex to run broad Docker/full-regression loops after every visual edit. Use focused source tests and browser proof during implementation, then consolidated validation at a meaningful closure point. This protects development time and disk/cache resources while still requiring final build/test quality.

## C51.3 — Rendered-browser review after implementation

Review the **first viewport without scrolling**. Can the visitor identify one focal point? Is the architecture image still the dominant hero environment? Does the headline occupy intentional quiet space rather than colliding with important image detail? Is the CTA visually subordinate to the proposition rather than becoming the brand’s loudest object? Does the header belong to the opening composition?

Review the **first major scroll handoff**. Does the hero settle/resolve before Work Worlds pins? Is the direction change visually prepared? Does the user understand that continued vertical input is advancing horizontal content? Does a fast wheel burst skip every meaningful world, or do the timeline/snap/dwell rules preserve comprehension?

At every **pinned dwell state**, stop scrolling and take a screenshot. The active actor, title, supporting explanation and necessary navigation must be visible together. If the copy is below the fold while the media is pinned, the stage is oversized. If the actor is mostly offscreen when a state changes, the timeline begins too early/late.

Review **reverse scroll** with the same seriousness. Shared actors return to their origins, selected states do not flicker, directionality feels coherent, and the page does not jump when pins release. Reversibility is part of the design, not an engineering afterthought.

Review the **secondary routes as a family**. They share typography, product truth and quality, but their macro silhouettes must differ. If Methodology, Trust, Privacy and Progress all look like a headline followed by large white rounded sections, the rebuild has failed even if each section is individually clean.

Review the **dashboard at data maturity 0, 1 and 2+**. Zero state feels complete and useful. One-result state does not pretend trends exist. Longitudinal state introduces charts only where enough history supports them. Information hierarchy shifts with data maturity instead of preserving one template grid.

Review **chart truth and legibility**. Big Five position plots share a scale. RIASEC radar has precise accompanying labels/ranks. Work Values ranking is visually ordered. Career-fit breakdown reflects actual component data. Trend lines correspond to actual dates/results. Missing values are not zero. Every graphic has a readable text/data alternative.

Review **390px and 320px** independently. Do not compare only against desktop. Ask whether the phone experience has its own balance, image crop, line breaks, task priority and interaction mode. Check `scrollWidth` numerically. No global overflow clipping may hide defects.

Review **illustration integration**. Does the artwork feel like part of the scene, or could it be removed without changing the layout? If it simply occupies the right half of another text/card split, the integration is too shallow. Process/evidence/navigation should respond to the illustration’s silhouette or story when illustration is a major actor.

Review **auth routes with media blocked**. Login/signup must still render and work. Then review with media loaded; the image should add identity, not become a prerequisite for the form.

Review **reduced motion and keyboard use**. A keyboard user can reach every Work World/lens/career state. Focus indicators remain visible. Reduced motion contains no long empty pinned distances. Screen-reader landmarks and form labels remain correct after visual restructuring.

Finally, perform the **template-distance test**: compare the page mentally against ThemeForest/Webflow/Framer/AI-builder output. If the visible grammar is still “large centered heading + rounded container + cards + fade + repeat,” the implementation is rejected regardless of how clean the CSS is.

## C51.4 — Transfer to the rest of the Valtum ecosystem

Personality Assessor teaches the process; it does not become the template for other products. KT Courier should not inherit the architecture-photo hero, evidence constellation or Personality charts. Dubai Booking should not inherit the Personality neutral analytical palette by default. Math Intellect should not inherit a career-style dashboard. Aegis Senital should not inherit Work Worlds. Valtum Studio should not become a collage of Personality scenes.

What transfers is the **research discipline**: audit product truth, learn from references, define a native protagonist, choose correct representation, resolve media/type/color/motion/mobile, then give Codex exact instructions. What transfers is the **anti-template discipline**: cards only when semantic, mobile independently composed, images art-directed, motion visible and reversible, performance/accessibility built in, and the browser used as final authority.

For KT Courier, the protagonist may be a delivery moving through accountable operational states. For Dubai Booking, it may be a real place/experience moving from desire to confident transaction. For Math Intellect, it may be a mathematical relationship becoming manipulable. For Aegis, it may be evidence becoming contextualized into action. For Valtum, it may be the transformation of difficult product requirements into shipped engineered outcomes. Each of those truths should create its own composition grammar.

The final goal is not six award-style websites. It is six products whose visual worlds are so well matched to their subject that a user could remove the logos and still understand that each came from a different problem—while recognizing the same level of craft, restraint, engineering discipline and authorship behind all of them.

---

**END OF PHASE 3C EXPANDED MASTER BRAIN — 15 AUGUST 2026**

## Final size-independent note

Document length is not itself a quality metric. The reason this expanded Brain is intentionally exhaustive is to preserve decisions, rejections, evidence boundaries and implementation constraints that were repeatedly lost when a shorter handoff forced an implementation agent to fill visual gaps with defaults. Future versions may become shorter only if they preserve the same decision coverage through better structure. They may not become shorter by deleting negative evidence, mobile behavior, reduced-motion states, media provenance, chart semantics, crop decisions, source divergences, or authority boundaries.

Every future update should therefore distinguish three things: **standing doctrine**, which remains reusable across the ecosystem; **product-specific truth**, which belongs only to the current product; and **historical research evidence**, which explains why a rule exists but does not automatically remain a live visual direction. This prevents old palette candidates, old media selections, old class names or superseded implementation techniques from becoming accidental requirements simply because they remain in the archive.

The Master Brain is complete enough to guide implementation when it can answer the practical questions Codex would otherwise invent: what is shown, what is not shown, which actor dominates, where it sits, how large it is, what crop it uses, what the user reads, what changes, when it changes, how long the state remains visible, what happens in reverse, what mobile does instead, what reduced motion sees, what data can truthfully populate the view, and what the browser must prove before acceptance.

# C54 — Math Intellect Forensic Negative-Control Addendum
## Valtum UI/UX Brain Update — 15 August 2026

**Status:** Standing cross-ecosystem negative-design addendum derived from the current Math Intellect frontend and live-production route.  
**Scope:** Math Intellect first; every rule marked **CROSS-ECOSYSTEM** also applies to Valtum Studio, KT Courier, Dubai Booking Marketplace, Personality Assessor, Aegis Senital, and future Valtum products unless later product evidence explicitly overrides it.  
**Implementation status:** Research/diagnosis only. This is not the Math Intellect redesign specification and is not permission for Codex to begin redesigning production.

---

## C54.0 Evidence boundary

This addendum is based on:

- the current `analyticsmath/MathIntellect` `main` frontend source;
- the current public production route `https://math-intellect.vercel.app/`;
- the existing Valtum Master Brain/C53;
- the user’s direct negative observation of the rendered site;
- current primary-source research into dynamic mathematical interfaces such as Desmos, GeoGebra, Mathigon/Polypad, Observable Plot, and Wolfram Demonstrations.

The current tool environment verifies the production route and source structure, but does not provide a trustworthy visual screenshot of the SPA. Therefore rendered-pixel claims supplied by the user remain **USER-OBSERVED**; code structure/style/behavior claims below are **TECHNICALLY VERIFIED FROM SOURCE**.

---

# C54.1 The new product-truth correction

The older broad research sometimes described Math Intellect like a general interactive-learning site. The current product contracts show that this is incomplete.

Math Intellect is a **mathematical simulation and decision-intelligence workbench with adaptive learning/progression layers**.

The real product material includes:

- Monte Carlo simulations;
- game-theory simulations;
- market simulation;
- conflict/agent simulation;
- custom simulation;
- mean / variance / standard deviation / min / max / median / sample count;
- histograms;
- CDFs;
- box plots;
- time series;
- heatmaps;
- bar and pie data;
- 3D surfaces and scatter plots;
- behavioral signals such as parameter changes, hesitation, exploration, reruns and strategy changes;
- adaptive explanation/chart complexity;
- AI-assisted interpretation and decision support;
- saved models;
- progression/XP and social/forking features.

Therefore the native experience identity should not be:

> “AI intelligence command center”

and it should not be reduced to:

> “school mathematics learning website.”

The stronger product-specific transformation is:

> **scenario assumptions → mathematical model → simulation → distribution/equilibrium/relationship → interpretation → decision → changed assumptions → rerun**

The mathematical state itself must become the visual protagonist.

---

# C54.2 The current frontend is a canonical AI-template negative reference

The present interface combines almost every surface treatment that the Valtum doctrine has already rejected:

- deep navy/black canvas;
- cyan + blue + violet identity;
- multiple radial/linear gradients;
- glows;
- glassmorphism;
- rounded cards;
- rounded pills;
- generic “premium” shadows;
- Sora + Inter + JetBrains Mono technology typography;
- uppercase micro-labels with wide tracking;
- decorative line before section labels;
- generic “live” dots;
- AI orb / neural sphere;
- dot grid;
- cursor-follow glow;
- fade-up reveal on sections;
- card tilt;
- card lift;
- button ripple;
- scale-on-press;
- count-up metrics;
- shimmer;
- pulse;
- floating animation;
- pseudo-command-center language;
- fake-looking metric strips;
- dashboard widget grids.

**CROSS-ECOSYSTEM HARD RULE:** Never reproduce this cluster as a “premium technology” design language.

Individual primitives are not universally illegal. The failure is the combination being used as the identity.

---

# C54.3 Ban the “AI palette cluster”

Current code deliberately defines:

- dark navy page/base/card surfaces;
- indigo-violet brand family;
- electric cyan;
- blue/violet/cyan gradients;
- glow shadows;
- radial glow backgrounds;
- multi-color chart palette.

This is not product-generated color. It is category decoration.

**NEVER DO:**

- purple/blue/cyan because “AI”;
- a dark canvas merely because the product is technical;
- gradient text or gradient buttons to manufacture importance;
- blue/violet bloom around generic objects;
- glow as the active-state language everywhere;
- a branded color assigned to every engine simply to make a dashboard colorful.

For Math Intellect, future color must derive from mathematical reading, semantic state and visual hierarchy.

---

# C54.4 Ban the “technology font costume”

The current product combines:

- Sora for display;
- Inter for body/UI;
- JetBrains Mono for numbers/technical moments;
- uppercase tracked micro-labels.

None of those fonts is inherently forbidden. The **combination and role assignment** are the negative reference.

It creates the generic “AI/quant/crypto dashboard” voice when paired with dark gradients, glows and command-center copy.

**CROSS-ECOSYSTEM HARD RULE:** Never choose typography by category costume:

- mono ≠ mathematical;
- mono ≠ engineering;
- grotesk ≠ premium;
- wide uppercase ≠ technical;
- heavy 700/800 heading ≠ authority.

Typography must be selected after product-specific reading, notation, data-density, mobile and spatial requirements are resolved.

---

# C54.5 Ban the universal section-kicker formula

Current global CSS defines a reusable section kicker:

- tiny uppercase text;
- wide tracking;
- cyan;
- a decorative horizontal gradient line before the text.

This is exactly the pseudo-editorial grammar already rejected by the Master Brain.

**CROSS-ECOSYSTEM HARD RULE:**

Do not construct pages from:

`decorative line → tiny uppercase kicker → big heading → paragraph → cards`

Do not replace the line with a dot, dash, number or micro-icon and pretend the pattern is different.

If a label is real navigation, status, data category or chart annotation, it may exist. Decorative pre-heading labels used as layout filler are rejected.

---

# C54.6 TEXT–CONTAINER–CARD LOOP: Math Intellect is now a canonical example

The current homepage repeats:

- heading;
- paragraph;
- `premium-card`;
- nested glass cards;
- more heading;
- more paragraph;
- another card grid;
- another premium card;
- pricing cards;
- final CTA card.

Features, Pricing, Product, Dashboard, Profile, Analytics and Simulation repeat variations of the same syntax.

**CROSS-ECOSYSTEM HARD RULE:** Math Intellect joins the rejected Personality Assessor pass as permanent evidence for the **TEXT–CONTAINER–CARD LOOP** ban.

A page is not authored merely because:

- cards have different sizes;
- cards tilt;
- cards glow;
- cards have charts inside;
- cards have 3D inside;
- cards are dark rather than white;
- cards are called “panels,” “surfaces,” “missions,” or “scenes.”

---

# C54.7 Ban “premium-card” as a macro design strategy

The current code literally centralizes a `.premium-card` class and a `MarketingCard` abstraction, then uses it as the answer to many unrelated information problems.

**CROSS-ECOSYSTEM HARD RULE:**

Low-level component reuse is good.  
Macro-composition reuse is dangerous.

Do not create a universal:

- PremiumCard;
- FeatureCard;
- InsightCard;
- MissionCard;
- FrameworkCard;
- StatCard;
- StoryCard

and let that abstraction determine the visual language of an entire website.

Containers are allowed when the information itself is a bounded object. They are not allowed merely because the coding agent needs somewhere to put content.

---

# C54.8 Ban the generic split hero + AI orb

The current hero is structurally:

`left headline/copy/CTAs/metric cards | right rounded 3D intelligence card`

The right-side protagonist is a glowing WebGL sphere made from:

- glassy core sphere;
- cyan pulse sphere;
- halo;
- blue/cyan/violet nodes;
- connecting lines;
- particles;
- bloom;
- auto-rotation;
- pointer parallax;
- scroll-driven camera drift.

This is technically competent but semantically generic.

**CROSS-ECOSYSTEM HARD RULE:**

Never make a product-specific problem look intelligent by inserting:

- AI orb;
- glowing brain;
- neural sphere;
- particle globe;
- random network ball;
- generic 3D core;
- rotating chrome object

unless that object literally represents meaningful product data or behavior.

For Math Intellect, 3D earns its place only when the data itself needs 3D: e.g. a real surface, state space, payoff/risk landscape or multivariate relationship.

---

# C54.9 Preserve engineering quality; reject conceptual irrelevance

The current WebGL implementation contains useful engineering practices:

- quality tiers;
- device-memory checks;
- reduced-motion fallback;
- lower-power fallback;
- adaptive pixel ratio;
- FPS-based quality reduction;
- explicit disposal/cleanup;
- lazy loading;
- post-processing fallback.

These are **good technical patterns**.

The failure is not “Three.js is bad.”  
The failure is spending good engineering on a protagonist that does not explain Math Intellect.

**CROSS-ECOSYSTEM RULE:** Keep high-quality engineering patterns; replace conceptually generic visual systems.

---

# C54.10 Ban “simulation cosplay”

The marketing Features page contains visual previews such as:

- a decorative sine/cosine wave;
- a static payoff matrix;
- random animated market candles;
- a generic node network;
- an AI coach progress bar.

Some visuals are generated with arbitrary/random values rather than real product results.

For a mathematical product, this is especially damaging.

**HARD RULE:**

A visualization that looks quantitative must be one of:

1. real product data;
2. a deterministic illustrative model whose inputs/formula are explicitly defined;
3. clearly labeled illustrative/demo data.

Never animate arbitrary numbers/shapes merely to make the product look mathematical.

The visualization should let the user ask and answer a mathematical question.

---

# C54.11 Ban fake “Live” UI and status theater

Current source contains static/decorative states such as:

- “Live” hero badge;
- pulsing status dot;
- “System Health” copy;
- static “Engines available” presentation;
- “Live platform telemetry” marketing labels.

If those states are not backed by real runtime status, they are interface fiction.

**CROSS-ECOSYSTEM HARD RULE:**

Never render “Live”, “Online”, “Healthy”, “Synced”, “Available”, “Verified”, “Secure”, “AI active”, etc. as decoration.

A status indicator must have a source of truth and a defined unknown/error state.

---

# C54.12 Ban fabricated authority metrics

The current marketing frontend hardcodes values including:

- `12.4M+` simulations;
- `2,300+` teams;
- `+38%` confidence gain;
- `94.8%` recommendation precision;
- `1.4M/day` throughput;
- sample feed statistics;
- sample likes/scores;
- community counts.

These values are not fetched from telemetry in the inspected components.

**CROSS-ECOSYSTEM HARD RULE:**

Never use hardcoded authority metrics as if they are production facts.

If a number is illustrative:

- label it illustrative/demo;
- do not use it as social proof;
- do not place it in a “trusted metrics” strip.

A premium site becomes less credible when it invents evidence.

---

# C54.13 Ban synthetic community theater

The current feed surface includes seeded usernames and hardcoded community numbers/rankings.

**HARD RULE:**

Do not manufacture:

- fake community size;
- fake active users;
- fake leaderboard ranks;
- fake testimonials;
- fake likes;
- fake feed activity;
- fake “trending” states.

Demo fixtures may exist in development/testing, but production presentation must either be real or clearly identified as a demonstration.

---

# C54.14 Ban fake ROI calculators

The current pricing route computes ROI using hardcoded assumptions such as analyst hourly cost and an invented hours-saved formula.

A calculator is not credible merely because it outputs changing numbers.

**CROSS-ECOSYSTEM HARD RULE:**

Never create “ROI”, “savings”, “revenue uplift”, “time saved”, “confidence gain” or similar calculators from invented coefficients.

If a model is used:

- expose assumptions;
- cite/justify them;
- let the user edit meaningful assumptions;
- label the result as an estimate;
- never present it as measured product performance.

This rule is especially strict for Math Intellect because mathematical credibility is part of the product identity.

---

# C54.15 Ban random decision-impact previews

The current simulation launch flow creates frontend-only random preview values for XP impact and predicted skill gain.

It also creates synthetic progress when live progress is absent.

**CROSS-ECOSYSTEM HARD RULE:**

Never generate random or invented “intelligence” values to make a workflow feel dynamic.

No random:

- confidence;
- prediction;
- skill gain;
- success probability;
- risk;
- readiness;
- progress;
- completion estimate;
- system health.

When progress is unknown, use an honest indeterminate state.  
When a prediction is unavailable, show unavailable/unknown.  
When an estimate exists, show its source and uncertainty.

---

# C54.16 Ban “mission-control theater” unless product semantics earn it

Current product language includes:

- Intelligence Cockpit;
- Mission Command;
- Mission Launch;
- Strategic Level;
- Engine Fleet;
- Badge Vault;
- tunnel/rings launch animation;
- “Initializing Mission”;
- “Strategic Win”.

Some progression/gamification is real product functionality, so gamification itself is not banned.

The negative pattern is turning a mathematical workbench into a sci-fi operations game.

**HARD RULE:**

Gamification must support learning/progression, not replace mathematical understanding.

Do not make serious analysis look more advanced by using military/space/command-center metaphors.

---

# C54.17 Ban transition spectacle that delays the task

The current launch flow can place a full-screen “execution tunnel” between configuration and actual simulation execution.

It animates concentric rings, blur, scaling and gradient title treatment.

**CROSS-ECOSYSTEM HARD RULE:**

A task transition must earn its duration.

For repeated operational tasks:

- do not require cinematic transition before every run;
- do not hide actual progress behind decorative animation;
- do not block experts with the same spectacle repeatedly;
- respect reduced motion;
- allow the mathematical state/result to become the interesting transition.

---

# C54.18 Ban microinteraction soup

The current global interaction system includes:

- ripple on pointer down;
- button scaling;
- 3D card tilt;
- card lift;
- cursor-follow glow;
- generic IntersectionObserver fade-up;
- stagger by DOM index;
- pulsing dots;
- count-up numbers;
- shimmer;
- float;
- glow pulse.

**CROSS-ECOSYSTEM HARD RULE:**

Microinteractions do not become premium by quantity.

Use motion only when it:

- explains cause/effect;
- preserves identity;
- clarifies state;
- gives useful feedback;
- or improves orientation.

A whole site driven by `fade up + card tilt + button ripple + glow` is now a named rejection pattern.

---

# C54.19 Ban decorative scroll reveal as the primary motion language

The homepage applies essentially the same `y + opacity` reveal to many unrelated sections.

**HARD RULE:**

If every section enters the same way, motion is not expressing product logic.

Math Intellect motion must be causal:

`parameter changes → model changes → distribution/surface/strategy changes → interpretation changes`

That relationship should supply the motion grammar.

---

# C54.20 Ban page-level overflow concealment

Current global CSS applies horizontal overflow hiding at page level.

**CROSS-ECOSYSTEM HARD RULE:**

Never use broad `overflow-x: hidden/clip` to make a responsive defect disappear.

Fix the actor/component that overflows.

Local clipping is allowed when a visual stage genuinely requires it.

---

# C54.21 Ban “desktop cards stacked vertically” as mobile-first

The current How It Works desktop card row becomes a vertical stack of the same cards on mobile.

This is responsive CSS, not mobile product design.

**CROSS-ECOSYSTEM HARD RULE:**

Mobile must reconsider:

- order;
- task priority;
- direct manipulation;
- chart viewport;
- gestures;
- navigation;
- labels;
- density;
- what is hidden;
- what becomes full-screen;
- what becomes a sheet;
- what interaction changes.

For Math Intellect, mobile should feel like a real mathematical app: one current model/question/manipulation dominates the screen.

---

# C54.22 Keep safe-area awareness; reject floating glass as universal mobile identity

The current app correctly uses `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)` for the mobile dock.

That is worth preserving.

The visual surface, however, is another large rounded blurred glass container with a glowing gradient central action.

**RULE:**

Preserve:
- safe areas;
- persistent top-level navigation where useful;
- touch target discipline;
- route continuity.

Do not assume:
- floating glass dock;
- glowing central FAB;
- tinted active pills

are the only way to make a mobile app feel premium.

---

# C54.23 Ban dashboard inventory design

Current dashboard architecture repeatedly uses:

- hero card;
- stat cards;
- rank card;
- suggestion card;
- daily-mission card;
- badge card;
- trend card;
- simulation cards.

The result is an inventory of widgets rather than a hierarchy of decisions.

**HARD RULE:**

A dashboard should answer the user’s next important questions in order.

For Math Intellect these are likely closer to:

1. What am I working on / what changed?
2. What should I inspect?
3. What does the mathematics say?
4. What is uncertain?
5. What can I change or rerun?
6. What happened previously?

Do not begin by deciding how many cards fit in twelve columns.

---

# C54.24 Ban chart decoration that competes with the data

The current chart theme includes:

- dark surfaces;
- multi-hue brand palette;
- gradients;
- inner glow;
- glass overlay;
- bloom-like 3D colors;
- animated/spring tooltip movement.

Some of this code is technically thoughtful, but chart identity should come from the data and the analytical question.

**HARD RULE:**

Charts should optimize:

- comparison;
- exact reading;
- uncertainty;
- selection;
- state change;
- direct manipulation;
- annotations;
- accessible alternatives.

Do not make charts look “premium” with glow.

---

# C54.25 Ban generic tabbed analytics as the only information architecture

Current analytics groups content into `Overview / Charts / 3D`.

That is implementation-category navigation, not necessarily user-question navigation.

**HARD RULE:**

Organize analytics around what the user is trying to learn, for example:

- What happened?
- How uncertain is it?
- Which variable matters most?
- Where is equilibrium?
- What changes if I alter this assumption?
- Which scenario dominates?
- What should I rerun?

A 3D representation is a view, not a product goal.

---

# C54.26 Ban visualizing “AI” instead of visualizing mathematics

The current experience repeatedly emphasizes:

- AI Coach;
- Intelligence Core;
- AI Intelligence Layer;
- intelligence feed;
- intelligence cockpit;
- confidence and recommendations.

The risk is that the mathematical engines become supporting content to an AI brand costume.

**HARD RULE:**

Math Intellect should lead with mathematical causality and simulation evidence.

AI may interpret, summarize or suggest.  
AI is not the visual protagonist.

---

# C54.27 Ban copy that sounds generated from “premium AI SaaS” prompts

Current copy frequently uses phrases such as:

- premium decision system;
- modern strategic teams;
- intelligence core;
- decision-ready strategy;
- premium feed;
- strategic precision;
- simulation velocity;
- high-trust decision workflows;
- premium analytics;
- intelligence command.

The vocabulary is abstract and self-congratulatory.

**CROSS-ECOSYSTEM HARD RULE:**

Do not repeatedly tell visitors the product is:

- premium;
- intelligent;
- powerful;
- strategic;
- cutting-edge;
- high-trust;
- advanced.

Demonstrate the capability through the actual interface and mathematics.

Prefer precise nouns and verbs:

- change variance;
- compare payoff;
- inspect distribution;
- constrain scenario;
- rerun;
- isolate tail risk;
- compare strategies.

---

# C54.28 Ban fake contradiction copy

The Product route literally claims a “real product showcase” while much of the preview is hardcoded schematic content.

**CROSS-ECOSYSTEM HARD RULE:**

Never use copy that says:
- real;
- live;
- verified;
- production;
- actual;
- telemetry;
- proven

when the presented object is a mock/fixture.

If it is a demonstration, say demonstration.

---

# C54.29 Ban legal/trust as decoration

Current Pricing places Privacy, Compliance and Terms into small marketing cards with broad reassuring claims.

**HARD RULE:**

Legal/trust content is not conversion decoration.

A trust claim needs:
- product truth;
- real controls/policies;
- direct language;
- links to actual legal content where required.

Do not invent “audit-ready”, “isolated”, “compliant” or “enterprise secure” language without verified support.

---

# C54.30 What is worth preserving from the existing frontend

Complete visual redesign does **not** mean destroying good engineering.

Potentially valuable foundations include:

- React/Vite/TypeScript architecture;
- lazy route loading;
- typed simulation/chart/AI contracts;
- realtime socket integration;
- explicit pending/running/completed/failed simulation states;
- reusable chart geometry code;
- 3D surface/scatter data contracts;
- adaptive explanation/chart-complexity semantics;
- reduced-motion checks;
- device-capability checks;
- WebGL quality tiers;
- renderer cleanup/disposal;
- resize observers;
- safe-area-aware mobile navigation;
- error/loading boundaries;
- semantic form controls;
- code splitting of expensive visual modules.

The next redesign should first separate:
- **product logic to preserve**
from
- **visual grammar to remove**.

---

# C54.31 New Math Intellect north-star refinement

Earlier Brain direction remains useful:

> **The mathematical object/manipulation owns the space.**

The product audit refines the protagonist further:

> **A scenario becoming a mathematical consequence the user can manipulate, inspect and rerun.**

Possible visual materials, pending later research/approval:

- probability distributions;
- parameter sliders;
- confidence/uncertainty bands;
- payoff matrices;
- equilibrium fields;
- stochastic paths;
- sensitivity surfaces;
- agent networks;
- scenario branches;
- compare states;
- annotations;
- formulas;
- exact values;
- risk regions.

The key relationship is:

> **input changes → mathematics changes → interpretation changes → decision changes**

That is the source of future motion, composition and interaction.

---

# C54.32 Research implication from current mathematical tools

Primary-source research into Desmos, GeoGebra, Mathigon/Polypad, Observable Plot and Wolfram Demonstrations reinforces one central principle:

> mathematical interfaces become compelling when the user can directly manipulate meaningful variables and immediately see mathematical relationships change.

Transferable principles:

- direct manipulation;
- linked representations;
- sliders/variables;
- immediate visual response;
- exact-value inspection;
- geometry/data as interface material;
- progressive complexity;
- visual explanation before prose;
- mobile-capable mathematical workspaces.

Do **not** copy their branding or layouts.

Math Intellect is a different product and should remain a simulation/decision workbench rather than becoming a Desmos/GeoGebra clone.

---

# C54.33 Gate before any Math Intellect Codex redesign

Do not give Codex a redesign implementation brief until the design authority has separately resolved:

1. verified public product claims;
2. actual production pricing/billing truth;
3. which social/community data is real;
4. whether gamification remains central, supporting, or reduced;
5. final audience/business positioning;
6. information architecture;
7. hero mathematical system;
8. final typography candidates;
9. final palette candidates;
10. chart/data-vis language;
11. 3D role;
12. mobile app composition;
13. motion grammar;
14. public-page narrative;
15. product workspace hierarchy;
16. auth;
17. dashboard;
18. simulation setup;
19. running state;
20. results/analytics;
21. feed/community;
22. profile/progression;
23. accessibility;
24. performance/fallbacks.

**No lab phase is required. Research first, then one exact production reconstruction contract.**

---

# C54.34 Final cross-ecosystem test

If a future Valtum website contains most of these at once:

> dark navy + cyan/violet + gradients + glowing orb + uppercase micro-label + decorative line + glass card + card grid + fake metric + “Live” dot + card tilt + fade-up + cursor glow + generic AI copy

reject the direction before implementation.

If Math Intellect can be understood more clearly after removing the words “AI”, “premium”, “intelligence”, the decorative orb and the cards, the redesign is moving in the correct direction.

The goal is not to make mathematics look futuristic.

The goal is to make complex mathematical behavior **legible, manipulable and consequential**.

# Math Intellect — Complete Frontend Redesign Research Blueprint
## C55 Product-Specific Design Constitution — 15 August 2026

**Status:** Research and design-direction blueprint.  
**Scope:** Complete Math Intellect frontend: public marketing, authentication, application shell, dashboard, simulation/model builder, running state, analytics/results, AI interpretation, saved models, feed/community, profile/progression, responsive/mobile, accessibility, performance, media, typography, color, data visualization, motion, and frontend architecture.  
**Backend/database rule:** Preserve backend/database behavior and contracts. The redesign may adapt frontend representations around verified contracts, but it must not redefine backend semantics simply to make the UI easier to design.  
**Implementation rule:** This document is **not** permission for Codex to implement the redesign. Final typography, palette, image/media assets, pricing/community claims, information architecture, hero system, and major interaction decisions still require explicit design-authority approval.

---

# 0. Executive redesign thesis

Math Intellect should no longer look like software trying to *signal intelligence*.

It should look and behave like a mathematical instrument that allows a person to:

> **state assumptions → build a model → run a simulation → inspect mathematical consequence → understand uncertainty/strategy → interpret the result → compare alternatives → change assumptions → rerun**

The visual protagonist is therefore not an AI orb, a card, a dashboard, a dark technical world, or even “AI.”

The protagonist is:

> **a scenario becoming a mathematical consequence that the user can manipulate, inspect, compare and rerun.**

The premium quality target is not “Awwwards styling.” It is the level of resolution visible in excellent authored sites and tools:

- the opening scene has a unique reason to exist;
- media has a semantic job;
- state changes have causal motion;
- type creates hierarchy and geometry;
- charts optimize understanding before decoration;
- mobile is a deliberate app composition;
- the public narrative proves the product rather than listing features;
- the app prioritizes decisions rather than widgets;
- every visible number has provenance;
- every “live” state has a source of truth;
- every high-cost visual enhancement has a useful fallback.

---

The current frontend contracts establish a product substantially richer than a generic education website.

Verified product material includes:

## Simulation engines

- Monte Carlo
- Game Theory
- Market

- Custom

- pending

## Core numerical results

- mean
- variance

## Existing chart/data contracts

- histogram
- cumulative distribution function
- box plot
- time series
- heatmap

## Existing 3D contracts

- surface
- scatter 3D
- multi-trace scatter 3D

## Existing analytical/interpretive material

- severity-typed insights
- key metrics
- highlights
- AI summary
- risk analysis

- mathematical interpretation
- recommendation
- alternatives
- confidence
- explain steps/formula/interpretation
- comparison/ranking

## Existing adaptive/progression material

- parameter changes
- reruns
- exploration ratio
- hesitation
- strategy changes

- adaptive mode

- highlighted metrics
- behavior type/tag
- learning velocity
- difficulty
- XP/progression
- skill profile
- engagement signals
