## C45. Final pre-Codex visual-resource approval board requirements

Before the exhaustive implementation prompt is issued, produce one compact approval board/document containing the following concrete choices. This board is a gate, not an optional moodboard.

| Gate | Approval artifact |
| --- | --- |
| Palette | Render the same candidate tokens on: hero architecture scene, populated dashboard charts, 390px assessment choice state. User approves exact HEX roles. |
| Typography | Render Mona Sans 2 actual strings: “Your work leaves evidence.”, Work Worlds names, one long adaptive question, dashboard labels/numerals, mobile navigation. Approve width/weight/optical ranges. |
| Hero media | Show retained architecture + retained laptop/human + 2–4 candidates for optional third process/code fragment. Approve exact crop/role. |
| Work Worlds | Show all six chosen photographs in their proposed active aspect/crop plus mobile crop. Reject any that feel generic/low-quality. |
| Career media | Profession-specific set for major public/demo careers. Avoid reusing developer image for every technical role. |
| Illustrations | Show 6–10 scenes from one coherent family (or custom set) including welcome, analytics empty, development/team, completion, report/privacy. Approve style first, then exact assets. |
| Charts | Show static visual mock/layout of Big Five lollipop, RIASEC radar+ranking, Work Values bars, trend line and career breakdown in the final palette. |
| Hero/Work Worlds mobile | Show 390px static frames before code: hero first viewport, first Work World active state, profile lens state, dashboard zero state. |

## C46. Closing principle — completeness without paralysis

The requirement to research at every step is not permission to browse forever. Research is attached to a decision and ends when the uncertainty relevant to that decision is sufficiently resolved. The project moves through explicit gates: understand → compare → decide → specify → implement → render → accept/reject → record learning. What Phase 3C forbids is skipping the first four steps and asking a coding agent to discover the design in CSS.

The best evidence that this Brain is working will not be the length of this file. It will be that the next implementation does **not** recreate any of the rejected visual fingerprints under a different class name, that its motion is visible and understandable at the center of the viewport, that mobile feels independently designed, that dashboard charts answer real questions, that images are sized/cropped as art direction, and that the resulting website could not plausibly be mistaken for an unrelated AI-generated SaaS template.


# C47. Phase 3C research-source interpretation archive — what each source changes in our decisions

## C47 — Lusion Oryzo BTS Part 1 — concept/creative direction

The important contribution is continuity. Lusion describes learning that a beautiful isolated section does not create a premium experience if the sections do not belong to the same world. They centered one protagonist and worked hard on transitions between substantially different scenes. For Personality Assessor this validates the evidence-as-protagonist model: architecture/professional evidence does not need to remain literally the same photograph everywhere, but the idea of evidence should survive its transformation into context, question, signal, profile and career relationship. The direct implementation consequence is that our flagship sequences require shared actors and scene handoffs rather than independent “finished sections.” It also reinforces that responsiveness is part of transition design; a scene transition that only works at 1440×900 is not a successful concept.

**Personality-specific decision:** This source is used only for the principle described above. Before any future implementation step, re-check the current version of the source if the technology, compatibility, license or live behavior could have changed.

## C47 — Lusion Oryzo BTS Part 2 — production pipeline

The key principle is that the pipeline follows the idea. Oryzo used heavy 3D/rendering/scanning experiments because its visual thesis required a physical-feeling product world. Personality does not inherit those technologies. Instead, we inherit the selection logic: first define what must be seen, then choose the cheapest medium that preserves it. A CV artifact and profile chart are better DOM/SVG than WebGL. A professional photograph is better served as responsive AVIF/WebP than a 3D reconstruction. A scroll carry is better owned by GSAP/DOM transforms than by a realtime renderer. This is how we can use fewer technologies while reaching a higher level of craft.

**Personality-specific decision:** This source is used only for the principle described above. Before any future implementation step, re-check the current version of the source if the technology, compatibility, license or live behavior could have changed.

## C47 — Lusion Oryzo BTS Part 3 — UX/UI/illustration

This source matters because Lusion explicitly rejected an early clean, abstract “Awwwards-like” direction as lifeless. The believable desk/world and protagonist made the site feel specific. They also describe “design without ego”: when imagery/world is rich, typography/UI can become restrained. This maps directly to our hero and color correction. We should not add five labels, a bright CTA, tinted badges and multiple border treatments around already-rich architecture photography. It also supports our illustration quality gate: illustration becomes a human layer integrated into a designed world, not a stock vector pasted into a card.

**Personality-specific decision:** This source is used only for the principle described above. Before any future implementation step, re-check the current version of the source if the technology, compatibility, license or live behavior could have changed.

## C47 — Dogstudio Zoox case study

Zoox is useful because the actual product form generated the site’s frames, borders and buttons. The transferable lesson is not rounded corners; it is that product truth can generate the shape grammar. Personality does not have a physical object, so its native geometry should come from evidence/artifacts, continuous dimensions, profiles and relationships. If a shape exists solely because it is fashionable, it should not survive the anti-copy test. This case also documents collaborative design/technical decision-making, reinforcing that feasibility should be discussed while the concept is being resolved rather than after static design is “finished.”

**Personality-specific decision:** This source is used only for the principle described above. Before any future implementation step, re-check the current version of the source if the technology, compatibility, license or live behavior could have changed.

## C47 — Dogstudio Virgin Galactic case study

This case is relevant to our scene architecture because it had to bridge heavy immersive sequences and content-dense sections while minimizing performance/loading impact. Dogstudio discusses multiple WebGL subscenes, a shared render architecture and transitions as a technical priority. Personality does not need WebGL, but it absolutely needs the same boundary discipline: when Work Worlds releases into Context, or Context carries into Living Profile, the transition must be planned as a first-class system. The case also shows that optimizing perception often means precomputing/using cheaper visual techniques rather than insisting on realtime fidelity—an important progressive-enhancement lesson.

**Personality-specific decision:** This source is used only for the principle described above. Before any future implementation step, re-check the current version of the source if the technology, compatibility, license or live behavior could have changed.

## C47 — Dogstudio Geske case study

Geske uses visualization to explain product features that would otherwise be difficult to understand. The transferable rule is that special effects earn their cost by explaining. Personality charts and scroll transitions should similarly make a relationship clearer: which evidence becomes a question, how one signal enters four readings, how career fit decomposes. If an animation only makes a panel feel “alive,” it does not meet this bar.

**Personality-specific decision:** This source is used only for the principle described above. Before any future implementation step, re-check the current version of the source if the technology, compatibility, license or live behavior could have changed.

## C47 — White Desert live/reference research

White Desert remains the strongest image-world reference because it lets the environment persist while foreground content changes. The visual lesson is not “use full-screen photos.” It is how image scale, sequence and environmental continuity reduce the feeling of disconnected sections. Personality can create a conceptual rather than literal persistent world: professional evidence keeps reappearing in different forms. White Desert also demonstrates that a restrained UI can let photography carry color, supporting the Phase 3C option to remove a dominant marketing accent.

**Personality-specific decision:** This source is used only for the principle described above. Before any future implementation step, re-check the current version of the source if the technology, compatibility, license or live behavior could have changed.

## C47 — GSAP ScrollTrigger official documentation

ScrollTrigger remains the strongest tool for precise pinned scenic timelines because pinning, scrubbed progress, labels/snap behavior, refresh mechanics and directional progress are first-class. The most important engineering note for our implementation is to pin a stable stage and animate its descendants rather than transforming the pinned root. We also need to avoid high-frequency layout reads in `onUpdate` where possible; timeline measurements should be prepared and refreshed. GSAP is the owner of flagship theatre, not a universal hover/reveal library.

**Personality-specific decision:** This source is used only for the principle described above. Before any future implementation step, re-check the current version of the source if the technology, compatibility, license or live behavior could have changed.

## C47 — Lenis official documentation

Lenis provides smooth interpolation while retaining native-scroll semantics and offers direct GSAP integration. For Personality it is a candidate replacement for ScrollSmoother on fine-pointer marketing routes, not a required brand feature. We must validate anchor links, focus, route restoration, pin behavior, nested scroll areas and low-powered devices. Touch stays native by default. If Lenis fails those tests, native scroll is preferable to a “smoother” experience with accessibility or control problems.

**Personality-specific decision:** This source is used only for the principle described above. Before any future implementation step, re-check the current version of the source if the technology, compatibility, license or live behavior could have changed.

## C47 — Anime.js v4 documentation

Anime.js has a real timeline and scroll observer/synchronization system and therefore deserves to be understood rather than ignored. However, knowing a tool is not the same as assigning it a job. Phase 3C does not currently identify a flagship sequence where Anime is clearly superior to existing GSAP. Its likely role is isolated SVG/typographic/illustration choreography where its API makes the local animation cleaner. It must never own the same transform/progress state as GSAP in one scene.

**Personality-specific decision:** This source is used only for the principle described above. Before any future implementation step, re-check the current version of the source if the technology, compatibility, license or live behavior could have changed.

## C47 — Motion for React documentation

Motion is much better aligned with authenticated UI state than with our pinned marketing theatre. Its layout/layoutId features can animate real React layout changes, remain interruptible and support shared-element continuity. That makes it ideal for career list→detail, active tabs/lenses, dashboard rearrangements, dialogs, accordions and selection states. This helps separate “product motion” from “narrative scroll motion,” reducing the temptation to run everything through ScrollTrigger.

**Personality-specific decision:** This source is used only for the principle described above. Before any future implementation step, re-check the current version of the source if the technology, compatibility, license or live behavior could have changed.

## C47 — Native View Transition API / React Router integration

View Transitions can create route/shared-element continuity with graceful fallback in unsupported environments. They are useful when old/new DOM differs significantly and a snapshot transition is acceptable, for example carrying a selected career thumbnail/title into detail. They are not a replacement for interruptible in-page layout animation or scroll theatre. Our architecture should prefer React Router’s own integration instead of layering Barba over the SPA.

**Personality-specific decision:** This source is used only for the principle described above. Before any future implementation step, re-check the current version of the source if the technology, compatibility, license or live behavior could have changed.

## C47 — CSS scroll-driven animations

Native scroll/view timelines are strategically useful for noncritical progressive effects, especially simple progress/opacity/translate relationships. Their existence does not justify moving core storytelling away from a well-tested JS owner before browser support and debugging behavior are sufficient. We can use them where failure means “the subtle effect does not run,” not where failure means “the visitor cannot understand the product sequence.”

**Personality-specific decision:** This source is used only for the principle described above. Before any future implementation step, re-check the current version of the source if the technology, compatibility, license or live behavior could have changed.

## C47 — Embla Carousel

Embla proves that a small carousel engine can support variable widths, horizontal/vertical axes, drag-free behavior, progress and accessibility plugins without requiring a giant UI framework. Our default remains native scroll snap because it is lighter and directly manipulable. Embla becomes justified only if Work Worlds mobile or another gallery requires coordinated selected state, progress, velocity or snapping that native CSS cannot deliver reliably enough.

**Personality-specific decision:** This source is used only for the principle described above. Before any future implementation step, re-check the current version of the source if the technology, compatibility, license or live behavior could have changed.

## C47 — Rive runtime/state-machine research

Rive can package vector art and state machines into an interactive illustration system and has official React runtimes. The tradeoff is meaningful runtime/WASM weight, especially for richer renderers. Personality should therefore use static SVG/DOM by default. Rive is interesting if we later commission an authored “evidence becomes profile” illustration whose states genuinely respond to product data or user interaction. It is not justified for looping character motion.

**Personality-specific decision:** This source is used only for the principle described above. Before any future implementation step, re-check the current version of the source if the technology, compatibility, license or live behavior could have changed.

## C47 — Apple HIG — charts/layout/color

Apple’s guidance reinforces three Phase 3C principles: information importance should influence space; chart type follows the comparison/trend/relationship question; and color should be used consistently and not carry multiple meanings. It also supports progressive disclosure on smaller screens. The relevant transfer is not Apple visual styling but task clarity: one mobile state should own attention, and a chart should communicate without forcing hover or deciphering a legend.

**Personality-specific decision:** This source is used only for the principle described above. Before any future implementation step, re-check the current version of the source if the technology, compatibility, license or live behavior could have changed.

## C47 — Carbon data visualization/dashboard guidance

Carbon is useful as a disciplined operational reference. It distinguishes lollipop/radar/line/bar/part-to-whole chart purposes and emphasizes dashboard hierarchy. This validates our representation map and the move away from six equal MetricCards. Carbon is not the target skin; its value is semantic chart selection, labeling, accessibility and dense information behavior.

**Personality-specific decision:** This source is used only for the principle described above. Before any future implementation step, re-check the current version of the source if the technology, compatibility, license or live behavior could have changed.

## C47 — Responsive image / picture guidance

The web platform explicitly supports art direction through `<picture>` and different sources/crops. This makes the “desktop image squeezed into phone” failure avoidable. Our existing ResponsiveImage component already moves in this direction; Phase 3C must enrich the media registry so mobile crop is a deliberate creative decision rather than a filename convention. Intrinsic dimensions and responsive sizes also protect layout stability.

**Personality-specific decision:** This source is used only for the principle described above. Before any future implementation step, re-check the current version of the source if the technology, compatibility, license or live behavior could have changed.

## C47 — Mona Sans variable typography research

Mona Sans provides weight, width and optical axes broad enough to create distinct marketing, reading, UI and data roles inside one family. The lesson is not that Mona Sans is universally premium; it is that we can author character through axis behavior rather than introducing multiple fashionable faces. The font still requires real-string testing, especially long adaptive questions and dense chart labels.

**Personality-specific decision:** This source is used only for the principle described above. Before any future implementation step, re-check the current version of the source if the technology, compatibility, license or live behavior could have changed.

## C47 — Pexels / illustration licensing research

The production media system must include rights/provenance rather than treating a URL as enough. Pexels broadly permits free commercial use and editing under its license, but recognizable people/property/trademarks can still raise context-specific issues and cannot imply endorsement. Illustration sources differ: DrawKit and ManyPixels are attractive for no-attribution commercial use, while Storyset’s free route typically requires attribution. Exact licensing is checked again at selection time because terms can change.

**Personality-specific decision:** This source is used only for the principle described above. Before any future implementation step, re-check the current version of the source if the technology, compatibility, license or live behavior could have changed.

# C48. Mobile composition micro-specifications — 390px primary canvas

### C48 — Opening viewport

Header height is compact; brand + Menu/Sign in action remains clear. Headline uses 2–4 authored lines depending final copy. Architecture crop occupies a meaningful visual block without pushing all CTA content beyond the first useful scroll. The human/laptop fragment is smaller and either overlaps the lower edge deliberately or appears as the next beat. No horizontal media carousel appears simply because desktop has multiple actors.

**Mobile rejection test:** Does this feel like an intentional app/page at 390px, or can the desktop layout be inferred as a stack underneath it? If the latter is true, redesign again.

### C48 — Work Worlds active state

One work photograph dominates, around 78–86vw depending crop, with a visible next peek. World name and one sentence are immediately adjacent. Swipe/drag has direct previous/next or accessible index. Momentum does not leave the user between two unreadable panels. The phone does not simulate a 4000px pinned desktop sequence.

**Mobile rejection test:** Does this feel like an intentional app/page at 390px, or can the desktop layout be inferred as a stack underneath it? If the latter is true, redesign again.

### C48 — Context intake

A compact document/evidence preview uses the full content width minus 18–20px gutters. Evidence groups are rows/tags only when semantically correct, with edit affordances. The user can proceed or change source without navigating a horizontal composition.

**Mobile rejection test:** Does this feel like an intentional app/page at 390px, or can the desktop layout be inferred as a stack underneath it? If the latter is true, redesign again.

### C48 — Assessment question

Question number/progress sits in a quiet header; question text begins near the top third rather than dead center if it is long. Answer choices are reachable without precision. Continue/Back respect the software keyboard and safe area. Save/Exit is available but visually subordinate.

**Mobile rejection test:** Does this feel like an intentional app/page at 390px, or can the desktop layout be inferred as a stack underneath it? If the latter is true, redesign again.

### C48 — Living Profile

A lens selector can be horizontally compact or a dropdown/segmented control depending width. One visualization owns the stage. Labels below the radar/lollipop are readable without pinch zoom. Swiping between lenses is optional; buttons always work.

**Mobile rejection test:** Does this feel like an intentional app/page at 390px, or can the desktop layout be inferred as a stack underneath it? If the latter is true, redesign again.

### C48 — Dashboard zero state

User/context name, active-session status or zero count, illustration and primary action appear before secondary explanation. The illustration is cropped/positioned as an editorial actor, not a huge image pushing the action below multiple screens.

**Mobile rejection test:** Does this feel like an intentional app/page at 390px, or can the desktop layout be inferred as a stack underneath it? If the latter is true, redesign again.

### C48 — Dashboard populated

Latest profile/next action first; one Big Five plot; one career direction summary. Secondary readings and history follow. The bottom nav stays visible but does not cover chart labels or buttons.

**Mobile rejection test:** Does this feel like an intentional app/page at 390px, or can the desktop layout be inferred as a stack underneath it? If the latter is true, redesign again.

### C48 — Analytics

Each visualization is a dedicated module with readable axes/labels. Multi-series trend may use a dimension selector or small multiples rather than forcing five colored lines into a 320px plot. A “View data” action exposes the accessible table.

**Mobile rejection test:** Does this feel like an intentional app/page at 390px, or can the desktop layout be inferred as a stack underneath it? If the latter is true, redesign again.

### C48 — Career Explorer

Role list is the first view. Each row provides role name, truthful fit/status and maybe one concise reason. Selecting opens detail; shared-element transition is optional. Back returns to the exact list position.

**Mobile rejection test:** Does this feel like an intentional app/page at 390px, or can the desktop layout be inferred as a stack underneath it? If the latter is true, redesign again.

### C48 — Privacy

Controls are grouped by consequence, with full-width buttons only where action deserves it. Destructive account deletion is separated and confirmed. Explanatory text is compact enough that controls remain discoverable.

**Mobile rejection test:** Does this feel like an intentional app/page at 390px, or can the desktop layout be inferred as a stack underneath it? If the latter is true, redesign again.

### C48 — Footer

Terminal phrase uses mobile-specific line breaks and perhaps reduced size. Links are grouped with 44px targets. Any giant desktop type treatment that would cause overflow is explicitly replaced rather than clipped.

**Mobile rejection test:** Does this feel like an intentional app/page at 390px, or can the desktop layout be inferred as a stack underneath it? If the latter is true, redesign again.

# C49. Dashboard information architecture — zero, one-result, and longitudinal maturity states

The dashboard should evolve with data maturity instead of rendering one fixed grid and replacing dashes with numbers. Three maturity modes are explicitly designed.

## C49.1 — Maturity 0: no completed assessments

The dashboard explains what the user can do now, not what the future data might look like. Show real account/CV/session state, a quality illustration, the first-assessment action and the four reading families as an educational preview. Do not show empty trait charts as if 0 were a score. If an active assessment exists, Resume becomes the primary action and the current progress can be shown truthfully.

## C49.2 — Maturity 1: one completed assessment

The page can now show a real current profile but cannot honestly imply trends. Big Five, RIASEC, Work Values, Career Signals, top career relationships and next roadmap action are useful. “Change over time” is replaced by an invitation/explanation that longitudinal comparison unlocks after a future valid assessment. The page should feel complete rather than like half of the dashboard is disabled.

## C49.3 — Maturity 2+: longitudinal history

Trend visualization becomes legitimate. The dashboard may show a compact change summary and the Analytics route becomes richer. Even here, avoid interpreting small score changes as psychological “growth” unless methodology supports that claim. Lines show recorded values and dates; explanatory text remains cautious. History, report generation and roadmap completion become meaningful secondary evidence.

## C49.4 — Maturity-sensitive composition rule

The number and type of visible dashboard regions can change by maturity state. This is preferable to preserving a template grid with empty placeholders. Layout continuity comes from typography, navigation, data visualization language and identity—not from forcing the same rectangles to remain forever.

# C50. Phase 3C “done enough to code” threshold

Phase 3C research is sufficiently mature for implementation **only after** the remaining visual-resource approvals are resolved. General research has reached diminishing returns; the remaining uncertainty is concrete: final palette, exact third hero fragment if any, final Work Worlds/career imagery, exact illustration family/scenes, and any copy/data source blockers such as retention/question count. Once those are approved, the implementation prompt should be generated immediately rather than returning to generic inspiration browsing.

The next Codex run should be a rebuild, not a sequence of patches. It should preserve product/backend logic and source integrity while replacing rejected macro composition. The brief should be long enough to remove ambiguity. The implementation agent should be forbidden to make convenience substitutions such as “if image unavailable use placeholder,” “if chart data missing render zero,” “if mobile difficult stack desktop cards,” or “if motion difficult fade between states.” A blocker must be reported, not cosmetically hidden.


# C51. Final implementation-authority checklist and ecosystem transfer notes

This final appendix exists to prevent the Phase 3C decisions from becoming another research document that implementation only partially follows. It defines the questions the design authority must answer immediately before issuing any new Codex instruction set, and the questions the reviewer must answer immediately after the rendered implementation returns.

## C51.1 — Before writing the Codex prompt

Confirm that the **current Master Brain has actually been reopened**, not merely remembered. Search the document for the route, interaction, image type, dashboard representation and mobile state involved. Re-read the newest rejection ledger entries. A previous decision can become stale when the user rejects its visible consequence; therefore “the Brain once said this was okay” is not sufficient if Phase 3C superseded it.

Confirm the **current repository state**. The prompt must name the branch/commit or at least state that Codex is to inspect current `main` before editing. If another agent has changed media files, route structure, data hooks, CSS ownership, backend contracts or dependencies since the last audit, the design brief must adapt to the source truth rather than assume the old file map is unchanged.

Confirm that every visible **number and claim has provenance**. A dashboard field can display `0` when zero is the actual value; it cannot display zero because a JavaScript fallback converted missing data to zero. Public illustrative values are clearly labelled illustrative. Career fit, evidence confidence, report availability, scoring validity, roadmap completion and assessment counts are all rendered from their actual contracts. Marketing copy does not imply diagnosis, scientific validation, certainty, hiring fitness or privacy guarantees that have not been verified.

Confirm that every **visual resource is in the correct approval state**. `APPROVED` assets can be implemented. `SHORTLISTED` assets can be shown for review but must not silently ship as final. `REJECTED` assets are forbidden. `PENDING` means the design brief must either stop at that resource gate or explicitly use a temporary local research frame that will not be mistaken for final art direction. Coding agents do not get to convert “pending” into “I chose something similar.”

Confirm the **actor budget** for every scene. A scene should name its protagonist, supporting actors and quiet information. If the list is too long to describe clearly, the composition is probably too crowded. Hero actor count, Work Worlds active/neighbor count, dashboard primary/secondary zones and mobile state ownership are all explicit.

Confirm **inline and block geometry**. Width alone is never enough for a pinned or media-dominant scene. State the intended width range, maximum viewport height, aspect/crop logic, position, surrounding text area and what should remain visible in the same viewport. Test the mental frame at 1366×768 before coding.

Confirm **mobile as an independent composition**. The prompt must not say only “on mobile stack the elements.” It states what remains, what disappears, what is reordered, what becomes a separate detail view, which image crop/source changes, what input mechanism replaces desktop scroll theatre, and how the bottom navigation/safe area behaves.

Confirm **motion ownership**. Each animated relationship has one owner. Lenis or native scroll handles scroll feel; GSAP owns flagship pinned timelines; Motion owns application layout/shared-element state; Anime can own a local animation if specifically chosen; CSS may own progressive noncritical effects; Rive can own a purpose-built vector state machine if approved. No two systems fight over the same transform/progress.

Confirm **reduced motion**. Describe the alternate composition, not merely a boolean that changes duration. The visitor must receive the entire semantic story without long pin distances or mandatory motion.

Confirm **error/loading/empty states**. Hero media failure leaves readable copy/action. Auth media failure leaves the form. Analytics loading uses a truthful skeleton/spinner with stable geometry. Empty dashboard does not invent chart values. AI report unavailability does not erase deterministic profile data. Career service errors do not destroy the rest of the result.

Confirm the **anti-template test**. Remove the words “Personality Assessor” mentally. Could the same scene be sold unchanged to a generic AI productivity tool? If yes, strengthen the relationship to professional evidence, adaptive questioning, independent profile readings, career relationships or longitudinal development before coding.

## C51.2 — While Codex is implementing

Codex is allowed to choose safe low-level implementation details when they do not alter the experience: exact helper-function decomposition, memoization strategy, CSS variable organization, test-file placement, small accessibility utilities, and equivalent browser APIs. It is not allowed to choose a different image, font, accent, chart type, hero layout, scene order, mobile composition, animation meaning or user-facing claim because that alternative is easier.

If a specified mechanism proves technically unstable, Codex should preserve the **semantic visual idea** and report the mechanism change. For example, if a shared-element transition fails across a route boundary, a simpler direct transition can be proposed while preserving list→detail continuity. If a complex clipping sequence is unreliable on Safari, the mobile/tablet fallback can simplify the mask while keeping the same state order. What cannot happen is replacing a difficult scene with a grid of cards without reporting a deviation.

Do not ask Codex to run broad Docker/full-regression loops after every visual edit. Use focused source tests and browser proof during implementation, then consolidated validation at a meaningful closure point. This protects development time and disk/cache resources while still requiring final build/test quality.

## C51.3 — Rendered-browser review after implementation

Review the **first viewport without scrolling**. Can the visitor identify one focal point? Is the architecture image still the dominant hero environment? Does the headline occupy intentional quiet space rather than colliding with important image detail? Is the CTA visually subordinate to the proposition rather than becoming the brand’s loudest object? Does the header belong to the opening composition?

Review the **first major scroll handoff**. Does the hero settle/resolve before Work Worlds pins? Is the direction change visually prepared? Does the user understand that continued vertical input is advancing horizontal content? Does a fast wheel burst skip every meaningful world, or do the timeline/snap/dwell rules preserve comprehension?

At every **pinned dwell state**, stop scrolling and take a screenshot. The active actor, title, supporting explanation and necessary navigation must be visible together. If the copy is below the fold while the media is pinned, the stage is oversized. If the actor is mostly offscreen when a state changes, the timeline begins too early/late.

Review **reverse scroll** with the same seriousness. Shared actors return to their origins, selected states do not flicker, directionality feels coherent, and the page does not jump when pins release. Reversibility is part of the design, not an engineering afterthought.

Review the **secondary routes as a family**. They share typography, product truth and quality, but their macro silhouettes must differ. If Methodology, Trust, Privacy and Progress all look like a headline followed by large white rounded sections, the rebuild has failed even if each section is individually clean.

Review the **dashboard at data maturity 0, 1 and 2+**. Zero state feels complete and useful. One-result state does not pretend trends exist. Longitudinal state introduces charts only where enough history supports them. Information hierarchy shifts with data maturity instead of preserving one template grid.

Review **chart truth and legibility**. Big Five position plots share a scale. RIASEC radar has precise accompanying labels/ranks. Work Values ranking is visually ordered. Career-fit breakdown reflects actual component data. Trend lines correspond to actual dates/results. Missing values are not zero. Every graphic has a readable text/data alternative.

Review **390px and 320px** independently. Do not compare only against desktop. Ask whether the phone experience has its own balance, image crop, line breaks, task priority and interaction mode. Check `scrollWidth` numerically. No global overflow clipping may hide defects.

Review **illustration integration**. Does the artwork feel like part of the scene, or could it be removed without changing the layout? If it simply occupies the right half of another text/card split, the integration is too shallow. Process/evidence/navigation should respond to the illustration’s silhouette or story when illustration is a major actor.

Review **auth routes with media blocked**. Login/signup must still render and work. Then review with media loaded; the image should add identity, not become a prerequisite for the form.

Review **reduced motion and keyboard use**. A keyboard user can reach every Work World/lens/career state. Focus indicators remain visible. Reduced motion contains no long empty pinned distances. Screen-reader landmarks and form labels remain correct after visual restructuring.

Finally, perform the **template-distance test**: compare the page mentally against ThemeForest/Webflow/Framer/AI-builder output. If the visible grammar is still “large centered heading + rounded container + cards + fade + repeat,” the implementation is rejected regardless of how clean the CSS is.

## C51.4 — Transfer to the rest of the Valtum ecosystem

Personality Assessor teaches the process; it does not become the template for other products. KT Courier should not inherit the architecture-photo hero, evidence constellation or Personality charts. Dubai Booking should not inherit the Personality neutral analytical palette by default. Math Intellect should not inherit a career-style dashboard. Aegis Senital should not inherit Work Worlds. Valtum Studio should not become a collage of Personality scenes.

What transfers is the **research discipline**: audit product truth, learn from references, define a native protagonist, choose correct representation, resolve media/type/color/motion/mobile, then give Codex exact instructions. What transfers is the **anti-template discipline**: cards only when semantic, mobile independently composed, images art-directed, motion visible and reversible, performance/accessibility built in, and the browser used as final authority.

For KT Courier, the protagonist may be a delivery moving through accountable operational states. For Dubai Booking, it may be a real place/experience moving from desire to confident transaction. For Math Intellect, it may be a mathematical relationship becoming manipulable. For Aegis, it may be evidence becoming contextualized into action. For Valtum, it may be the transformation of difficult product requirements into shipped engineered outcomes. Each of those truths should create its own composition grammar.

The final goal is not six award-style websites. It is six products whose visual worlds are so well matched to their subject that a user could remove the logos and still understand that each came from a different problem—while recognizing the same level of craft, restraint, engineering discipline and authorship behind all of them.

---

**END OF PHASE 3C EXPANDED MASTER BRAIN — 15 AUGUST 2026**

## Final size-independent note

Document length is not itself a quality metric. The reason this expanded Brain is intentionally exhaustive is to preserve decisions, rejections, evidence boundaries and implementation constraints that were repeatedly lost when a shorter handoff forced an implementation agent to fill visual gaps with defaults. Future versions may become shorter only if they preserve the same decision coverage through better structure. They may not become shorter by deleting negative evidence, mobile behavior, reduced-motion states, media provenance, chart semantics, crop decisions, source divergences, or authority boundaries.

Every future update should therefore distinguish three things: **standing doctrine**, which remains reusable across the ecosystem; **product-specific truth**, which belongs only to the current product; and **historical research evidence**, which explains why a rule exists but does not automatically remain a live visual direction. This prevents old palette candidates, old media selections, old class names or superseded implementation techniques from becoming accidental requirements simply because they remain in the archive.

The Master Brain is complete enough to guide implementation when it can answer the practical questions Codex would otherwise invent: what is shown, what is not shown, which actor dominates, where it sits, how large it is, what crop it uses, what the user reads, what changes, when it changes, how long the state remains visible, what happens in reverse, what mobile does instead, what reduced motion sees, what data can truthfully populate the view, and what the browser must prove before acceptance.

# Valtum Studio — Master UI/UX, Product Design, Visual Design, Content, Motion & Creative Frontend Engineering Brain

**Status:** Authoritative master doctrine + complete research archive  
**Date:** 13 August 2026  
**Scope:** Valtum Studio flagship website and the five core portfolio/product websites: KT Courier, Dubai Booking Marketplace, Math Intellect, Personality Assessor, and Aegis Senital.  
**Audience:** Senior UI/UX lead, product designer, visual/graphic designer, brand designer, art director, content designer/copywriter, motion designer, senior frontend engineer, creative developer, 2D/3D/WebGL engineer, accessibility/performance lead, and Codex implementation agent.  
**Purpose:** Preserve the full working design brain developed through this project: user feedback, visual references, direct live-browser inspections, deep-research passes, mobile/product research, typography and color research, image-specific research, creative-frontend engineering research, negative-reference analysis, screenshots, recordings, implementation lessons, and hard rules.

---

## 0. How to use this document

This file is not a moodboard and it is not a collection of fashionable effects. It is a **decision system**. Future project-specific briefs may refine values, assets, copy, timing, or product behavior, but they must not silently violate the reasoning model in this document.

The central rule is:

> **Valtum is authored, not templated.**

That does **not** mean every Valtum-owned site should look the same. The six sites should share standards of craft, product truth, responsive discipline, accessibility, media quality, engineering quality, and intentionality. They should not share one reskinned hero, one repeated card grammar, one universal palette, one font recipe, one animation preset, or one page silhouette.

The governing workflow is:

**product truth → audience objective → business objective → emotional objective → native concept → protagonist → information architecture → composition grammar → media grammar → typography grammar → color logic → motion grammar → interaction grammar → mobile recomposition → accessibility states → performance strategy → exact implementation specification → rendered-browser art-direction review.**

Codex is the implementation agent. Codex is not allowed to become the designer by filling ambiguity with generic frontend habits. Before Codex writes a public experience, the design authority must know what is shown, why it is shown, where it sits, what it says, how it moves, how it reverses, how it behaves at each viewport, what reduced motion sees, what happens when assets or WebGL fail, and which real product data or media proves the claim.

Never give Codex instructions such as:

- make it premium;
- make it cinematic;
- add smooth animations;
- use a modern font;
- make it like Oryzo;
- add a beautiful carousel;
- make the dashboard cool;
- use an Awwwards-style hero.

Those phrases surrender design authority. Replace them with exact composition, content, state, media, timing, fallback, and acceptance instructions.

### Evidence taxonomy

This master preserves the evidence discipline developed during the live-inspection program:

- **DIRECTLY OBSERVED:** seen in a rendered browser or in a user-provided recording/screenshot.
- **TECHNICALLY VERIFIED:** established from exposed DOM/runtime/resource information or official technical material.
- **DOCUMENTED:** stated by the product/site/studio itself or by a primary source.
- **USER-OBSERVED:** directly reported by the user from their own live browser; treated as authoritative preference/negative evidence, but not falsely relabeled as our own direct observation.
- **INFERRED:** a design/engineering conclusion derived from evidence.
- **NOT VERIFIED:** not safely established; never promoted to fact.

The most important epistemic rule is simple: **never fill a gap because the answer would be aesthetically convenient.**

---

# PART I — THE GOVERNING PHILOSOPHY

## 1. Premium means resolution

“Premium” is not a color. It is not a dark theme, a luxury serif, giant text, smooth scrolling, a WebGL scene, a rounded card, a grain layer, a glowing cursor, or an expensive photograph.

For this ecosystem:

> **Premium means every visible decision feels resolved.**

A resolved design has intentional crop, focal point, line break, paragraph measure, font width, weight, optical size, tracking, leading, whitespace, hierarchy, z-order, image order, active state, disabled state, error state, table density, chart encoding, scroll distance, transition boundary, reverse behavior, mobile composition, touch behavior, fallback, reduced-motion state, loading behavior, and footer resolution.

A mediocre site can contain sophisticated libraries. A sophisticated site can be almost motionless. The distinction is whether the experience feels **authored for its subject**.

### Resolution questions

Before approval, every major decision must survive:

1. Why is this here?
2. Why this size?
3. Why this crop?
4. Why this type behavior?
5. Why this direction of movement?
6. Why this image before the next one?
7. What happens if the user stops halfway?
8. What happens if they reverse?
9. What happens at 390 px?
10. What happens with touch instead of hover?
11. What happens with reduced motion?
12. What happens on a slow connection?
13. What happens if JavaScript or WebGL fails?
14. Can the visible claim be proved?
15. Could another unrelated company replace the logo and keep the same design?

If the last answer is yes, authorship is weak.

## 2. Product truth generates visual truth

The strongest recurring lesson from Oryzo, White Desert, Lando Norris, Inversa, Glyphic, CargoKite, top Behance/Dribbble work, and the better product interfaces is that **design should emerge from something native to the subject**.

This does not mean literal visual metaphors everywhere. It means the information, material, environment, object, action, evidence, or workflow that makes the product itself distinctive should influence the site’s visual system.

Examples:

- White Desert earns ice, location, atmospheric scale, route movement, wildlife and camp imagery because Antarctica is the product world.
- Lando Norris earns the helmet and signature as recurring actors because they are identity material, not generic motorsport decoration.
- Oryzo earns an absurdly over-engineered physical protagonist because the entire concept is one object being treated with excessive technical seriousness.
- Inversa earns field footage, prediction maps, body-camera evidence and operational states because the service is ecological field operations.
- Math Intellect should earn graphs, equations, geometric relationships and manipulable mathematical state because mathematics is the product material.
- Aegis should earn evidence, location, event history and contextual signals because situational understanding is the product problem.

A generic visual can be beautiful and still be wrong.

## 3. The protagonist comes before the hero layout

Do not begin a homepage with “left image or right image?” Begin with:

> **What should the visitor remember after the first ten seconds?**

Then decide what actor can carry that meaning.

Possible protagonists include:

- a physical product;
- a real environment;
- a stateful workflow;
- one piece of evidence;
- a mathematical relationship;
- a living profile;
- an incident becoming understandable;
- selected work transforming from artifact into case study;
- typography itself, if it truly carries identity and composition.

The hero is a **thesis**, not a template.

## 4. The anti-copy test

Every reference is decomposed into **principle** and **surface**.

The principle may transfer. The surface usually should not.

Ask:

> **If the reference disappeared tomorrow, would this decision still make sense because of our product itself?**

If yes, we learned.

If no, we copied.

A second test is even stricter:

> **Could this hero or section be moved to another one of our six websites by changing only the logo, accent color and words?**

If yes, the design is not product-specific enough.

## 5. Shared craft, different identities

The ecosystem should share:

- high-resolution art direction;
- strong responsive behavior;
- truthful copy;
- semantic HTML and accessible interaction;
- intentional type systems;
- meaningful motion;
- explicit fallbacks;
- high-quality loading behavior;
- correct data representations;
- excellent mobile composition;
- authored endings;
- exact Codex specifications.

It should **not** share:

- one hero layout;
- one global “premium” color palette;
- one repeated image rail;
- one universal giant font;
- one macro component template;
- one motion timeline applied everywhere;
- one style of cards;
- one footer arrangement;
- one dashboard skin.

---

# PART II — HARD NEGATIVE CONTROLS: VANTUM STUDIO AND VANTUM WORKS

## 6. Why negative controls matter

Most design research asks “what should we emulate?” This project also needs clear answers to “what must we never drift toward?” The two Vantum sites are useful because the user has designated them as **hard anti-references**: not because every functional choice is inherently invalid, but because their overall combination represents exactly the visual, structural, copywriting, and frontend-default behavior that must not enter the Valtum ecosystem.

The correct use of a negative reference is not mockery. It is forensic diagnosis.

For these two sites, separate three evidence layers:

1. **Current indexed/accessible site structure and copy** — independently inspectable.
2. **User-observed live visual behavior** — including the gray/AI-template feeling, cheap microanimation language, punctuation/cadence, and family resemblance across product sites.
3. **Inferred code smells** — patterns to search for in our own implementation. These are not claims that the proprietary source literally contains a given component name.

That distinction prevents the anti-reference itself from lowering our evidence standard.

## 7. Vantum Studio — structural audit

The currently indexed Vantum Studio homepage follows an extremely recognizable marketing sequence:

**navigation → hero → quick metrics → trade/category list → “why us” → problem → numbered process → featured project → CTA → services → included extras → CTA → pricing → FAQ → about/story → values → CTA → contact → standard footer.**

None of those modules is forbidden in isolation. The problem is the **accumulation of familiar modules with almost no product-specific spatial logic between them**.

The page repeatedly introduces a small section label before a larger heading. Examples of the hierarchy include labels equivalent to “why,” “problem,” “how it works,” “featured project,” “services,” “included,” “pricing,” “about,” “values,” and “contact.” That is precisely the eyebrow/kicker grammar this project has banned.

The site also repeatedly uses:

- numbered steps and service units;
- check/cross icon lists;
- benefit cards;
- stat fragments;
- “Most Popular” pricing treatment;
- FAQ accordion grammar;
- repeated conversion CTAs;
- feature lists under feature headings;
- conventional trust/guarantee panels;
- standard contact form and utility footer.

The result is not necessarily unusable. It is **predictable before the user has finished scrolling**. Predictability is the central negative lesson.

### Hard transfer rule

For Valtum and its products, section order must come from the product story rather than the standard landing-page inventory. If a draft can be described as:

**hero → benefits → features → steps → testimonials → pricing → FAQ → CTA**, reject the macro architecture before styling it.

## 8. Vantum Studio — copy and AI-cadence audit

The site demonstrates multiple writing habits the user specifically rejects:

- short slogan fragments used as a substitute for a sentence;
- repeated contrast pairs;
- repeated “no X, no Y” reassurance patterns;
- frequent dash-led interruptions;
- sentence fragments separated into pseudo-dramatic lines;
- repeated “fast / simple / premium / results” vocabulary;
- broad claims that could belong to hundreds of agencies;
- pain → fear → reassurance → CTA repeated in multiple chapters;
- faux-conversational statements that sound engineered to mimic directness;
- headings whose rhythm is more important than their information.

A few short phrases on the live page make the pattern obvious: the process is described with a “simple/zero-stress” slogan, and pricing is framed with a “straight-up/no-bull” slogan. The issue is not that those individual lines are illegal. The issue is **detectable synthetic cadence across the entire page**.

The about copy uses another common pattern: a normal sentence is interrupted, then a two-word declaration is given its own sentence for emphasis, then another certainty statement follows. Repeated enough, this begins to sound like copy generated from a prompt such as “make it punchy, direct and conversion focused.”

### Our content-writing rule

We do not ban punctuation. We ban **habitual, machine-detectable rhythm**.

A human premium writer should vary:

- sentence length;
- syntax;
- paragraph length;
- rhetorical intensity;
- specificity;
- emotional temperature;
- use of punctuation;
- degree of compression.

The website should sound as though somebody understood the actual product and wrote for that exact moment, not as though every section was asked to “sound punchy.”

### Never-do content patterns

Reject pages where multiple sections contain variations of:

```text
Short noun phrase.
Short contrast phrase.
Another certainty.
CTA.
```

Reject repeated constructions such as:

```text
No X. No Y. Just Z.
```

or:

```text
Simple X. Powerful Y. Built for Z.
```

or:

```text
You do A. We handle B.
```

if they become the voice of the entire website.

Those devices can occur once when naturally deserved. They cannot become the writing engine.

## 9. Vantum Studio — visual grammar as a negative control

The user’s live observation identifies the site as a strong example of the visual family we reject: gray/neutral agency styling, generic card/modular composition, so-called microanimations, and a visibly AI-generated/site-builder quality.

Because the current research environment did not provide a direct rendered animation replay of this site, the exact easing curves, CSS values, hover transforms and framework are **not claimed here**. The live-user judgment remains authoritative as a preference constraint; the accessible page structure explains why that judgment is plausible.

The hard rule is not “gray is forbidden.” Gray can be excellent. The hard rule is:

> **Do not use neutrality as a substitute for art direction.**

A gray background, dark text, rounded feature cards, little icons, subtle translate-on-hover behavior, and modern sans type are all ordinary primitives. If the subject has not generated any additional visual logic, the result feels generated even when it is professionally assembled.

### Cheap microinteraction signatures to reject

A site should fail art-direction review when most of its interaction language consists of:

- card rises 4–8 px on hover;
- border becomes slightly brighter;
- shadow increases;
- icon rotates a few degrees;
- CTA arrow slides 3–6 px;
- button scales to 1.02 or 0.98;
- section fades upward when entering viewport;
- heading words stagger in because a library makes it easy;
- number counts up for no narrative reason;
- generic spring/bounce on every click;
- cursor-triggered parallax that communicates nothing;
- a glowing accent follows pointer movement with no product meaning.

These are not “premium microinteractions.” They are implementation defaults unless the state change has semantic value.

For operational UI, a row highlighting because it is selected is meaningful. A delivery status changing because data changed is meaningful. A card rising because it is hoverable may be acceptable. What we reject is using such tiny effects as **the complete creative language of a marketing experience**.

## 10. Vantum Studio — over-modularization and visual sameness

The accessible structure demonstrates a deeper risk: the page can easily be implemented as a collection of reusable marketing modules. That is attractive to a coding agent because it is fast, maintainable and visually safe. It is exactly why the result can look generic.

The anti-pattern is not component reuse itself. Low-level reuse is desirable. The anti-pattern is **macro-composition reuse**.

Good shared primitives:

- accessible button;
- link;
- responsive image;
- typography token;
- focus treatment;
- menu logic;
- media loader;
- data table primitive;
- modal/dialog;
- motion hook;
- page-transition infrastructure;
- spacing tokens;
- color tokens;
- form field;
- reusable chart foundations.

Dangerous shared macro patterns:

- one universal hero with props;
- one universal section intro with eyebrow/title/body;
- one universal feature card used for everything;
- one universal 3-column “benefits” grid;
- one universal numbered process component;
- one universal testimonial card;
- one universal CTA band;
- one universal black footer;
- one universal “premium” reveal wrapper.

Our codebase can be systematic without our pages having the same silhouette.

## 11. Vantum Studio — claim discipline

The current page contains multiple numerical or performance-oriented claims: percentages, lead/result language, turnaround guarantees, search/mobile behavior, hosting guarantees, and SEO expectations.

The negative lesson is not “never show metrics.” Real metrics are powerful. The rule is:

> **No visible proof object without provenance.**

Before a Codex brief places a statistic in the interface, it must know:

- source;
- time period;
- sample population;
- whether it describes the product or an industry;
- whether it is still current;
- whether marketing has permission to publish it.

If that cannot be answered, use a truthful qualitative statement or omit the claim.

## 12. Vantum Works — evidence boundary

The current Vantum Works main domain identifies itself as an independent software studio spanning B2B SaaS, consumer utilities and games. The main product presentation is dynamic enough that the current text environment does not reliably expose the complete visual family or all nine-to-eleven products.

The final doctrine therefore does **not** pretend to have independently replayed every product website.

What is independently available:

- **Link Shrink**, which identifies itself as a Vantum Works product and exposes a detailed public marketing surface.
- **Scout**, whose public metadata describes structured recruiter screening/intake work.
- **Piper**, whose subdomain has appeared in indexing evidence, but whose full experience is not sufficiently verified here.

What is also binding:

- The user has directly inspected the broader Vantum Works product family and explicitly designated the main site plus the entire product portfolio as a **hard negative reference**.

That user-observed designation is authoritative for future Valtum art direction even when a specific product cannot be replayed by this research environment.

## 13. Link Shrink — why the product page is a useful anti-template study

Link Shrink’s current public structure is a familiar SaaS marketing stack:

**hero promise → QR capability → link capability → switching reasons → analytics sample → use cases → pricing tiers → plan comparison → reliability bullets → final CTA → standard product/resources footer.**

Again, the information itself may be legitimate. The negative lesson concerns **presentation grammar**.

### What to reject

#### 13.1 Capability checklist as narrative

A homepage becomes documentation when most of its story is expressed as capability lists. A visitor understands what features exist but does not necessarily experience why the product is distinctive.

Our product pages should show the transformation or decision the product enables:

- KT: one delivery moving from uncertainty to accountable completion;
- Dubai: desire becoming a confident booking;
- Math: an abstract relationship becoming understandable through manipulation;
- Personality: professional evidence becoming a nuanced profile and explainable career relationship;
- Aegis: an event becoming contextualized and actionable;
- Valtum: a difficult product requirement becoming a real engineered outcome.

#### 13.2 Placeholder-looking analytics proof

A compact set of sample KPIs can be useful in a dashboard. It becomes generic marketing decoration when the only reason it appears is to make the product look “data-driven.”

When we show product UI as marketing proof, it should show a **decision or relationship**, not just four numbers.

#### 13.3 Universal pricing-card grammar

Pricing cards are correct when plan comparison is the task. They are not a visual identity. A product family should not acquire its personality from three equal cards and a highlighted middle tier.

#### 13.4 Repeated numbered use cases

Numbering can communicate order. It should not be added simply to make a list feel designed. If five use cases are not sequential, visual numbering should not pretend they are a process.

#### 13.5 Generic slogan compression

The product uses concise contrastive marketing language. The user specifically wants to avoid this becoming a family-wide voice. Our copy should carry more concrete subject matter and less templated slogan rhythm.

## 14. Vantum Works family — the largest negative lesson

The user’s strongest criticism is not one button or one color. It is that the studio plus its many products feel as though **the same AI/site-generator brain authored every one of them**.

That creates the most important portfolio rule in this document:

> **Shared quality is desirable. Shared macro-design identity across unrelated products is not.**

A studio portfolio is supposed to prove range, judgment and the ability to discover what is native to each problem. If every product shares the same gray field, card system, type scale, rounded corners, subtle hover lift, feature sequence, fragment copy and pricing shape, the portfolio proves that the studio can reproduce one template efficiently. It does not prove art direction.

Valtum must do the opposite.

Each portfolio site gets a different creative thesis:

- KT = movement and accountability;
- Dubai = place, desire, trust and transaction;
- Math = understanding made manipulable;
- Personality = humane interpretation of complexity;
- Aegis = evidence, context and action;
- Valtum = authored product-building credibility.

The six products may share internal engineering primitives. They may not share one visible generator fingerprint.

## 15. Anti-template code blacklist

The following examples are **review signatures**, not allegations about the exact proprietary source of Vantum Studio/Works. Search for these patterns in our code because they often produce the aesthetic we are trying to avoid.

### 15.1 Universal section intro

```tsx
<SectionIntro
  eyebrow="The Problem"
  title="..."
  description="..."
/>
```

Default verdict: reject. Eyebrows are banned, and the abstraction encourages every chapter to begin with the same hierarchy.

### 15.2 Universal feature card

```tsx
<FeatureCard icon={icon} title={title} description={copy} />
```

If the same component is used for services, benefits, proof, process, methodology, testimonials, “why us,” product capabilities and values, the code has become an aesthetic generator.

Cards are acceptable only when the information actually behaves like independent cards.

### 15.3 Universal section shell

```tsx
<section className="mx-auto max-w-7xl px-6 py-24 lg:py-32">
```

A common content container is fine. A whole authored homepage repeating the same max-width/padding silhouette is not.

### 15.4 Layout from item count

```tsx
<div className="grid md:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-4">
```

because there happen to be four ideas.

The number of data records should not automatically determine art direction.

### 15.5 Generic reveal wrapper

```tsx
<Reveal>
  {children}
</Reveal>
```

where every instance means opacity 0 → 1 and translateY 24 → 0.

A single reveal primitive can exist, but it cannot become the page’s motion grammar.

### 15.6 Motion-library autopilot

```tsx
<motion.div
  initial={{ opacity: 0, y: 24 }}
  whileInView={{ opacity: 1, y: 0 }}
  transition={{ duration: 0.6 }}
/>
```

repeated on most sections.

This is the exact kind of code that creates a technically animated but creatively inert site.

### 15.7 Generic hover animation

```tsx
whileHover={{ y: -6, scale: 1.01 }}
whileTap={{ scale: 0.98 }}
```

on every card and CTA.

Do not confuse response feedback with art direction.

### 15.8 Generic naming

Review abstractions named:

- `PremiumSection`;
- `PremiumCard`;
- `PremiumHero`;
- `FancyReveal`;
- `GlassCard`;
- `ModernGrid`;
- `AnimatedSection`;
- `FeatureBento`.

Names like these often reveal that styling was generalized before meaning was understood.

### 15.9 Universal marketing data schema

```ts
{
  hero,
  stats,
  features,
  benefits,
  testimonials,
  pricing,
  faqs,
  cta
}
```

rendered by one generic page template for every product.

This may be convenient for a page builder. It is unacceptable as the visible architecture of our six flagship experiences.

### 15.10 Reusable macro silhouettes

Do not build a `ProductMarketingPage` whose main layout is fixed and only content props change. Reuse implementation infrastructure; author composition at the page/scene level.

## 16. Code review anti-slop search list

When reviewing a PR, inspect for concentration of:

```text
eyebrow
kicker
badge
pill
glass
bento
premium
feature-grid
stats-grid
cta-band
section-intro
animated-section
fade-up
hover:-translate-y
hover:scale
transition-all
duration-300
rounded-3xl
backdrop-blur
shadow-xl
gradient
from-
to-
via-
```

None is automatically illegal in source code. The point is to detect **clusters of default styling** before they become a page-wide fingerprint.

Also inspect:

- repeated `py-24`, `py-32`, `gap-8`, `max-w-7xl` section shells;
- repeated four-column grids;
- repeated centered H2 + paragraph + cards;
- repeated Framer Motion `whileInView` blocks;
- repeated tiny icon + title + two-line body cards;
- repeated rounded containers around media;
- repeated CTA rows after every two sections;
- duplicated macro components across unrelated product websites.

---

# PART III — THE HARD GLOBAL “NEVER DO” LIST

## 17. Permanent visual prohibitions

Unless a future product-specific exception is explicitly justified and approved, never introduce:

- eyebrow/kicker/pre-title text;
- decorative horizontal divider rules as page grammar;
- “micro-label + line + oversized heading” editorial cliché;
- gradients;
- default ivory, cream, beige or warm luxury off-white systems;
- generic blue/purple/cyan “AI” identity;
- green-led “premium tech” identity by reflex;
- black/gold “Dubai luxury” cliché;
- cyberpunk neon security styling;
- a differently colored word inside the hero headline as a gimmick;
- generic left-copy/right-image hero;
- detached floating pill/capsule navbar at the opening;
- glassmorphism as default hierarchy;
- giant extra-bold sans as the definition of quality;
- giant serif-led editorial magazine identity by reflex;
- numbered decorative chapters (`01`, `02`, `03`) unless real sequence needs it;
- decorative status pills such as “AI powered,” “Live,” “New” without task value;
- card grids simply because cards are easy to code;
- Bento composition unless the content genuinely behaves as a Bento-like set of independent modules;
- rainbow KPI cards;
- charts with no question;
- fake dashboards built only for marketing aesthetics;
- stock photography used to fill empty space;
- dark overlays used only to manufacture “cinematic” feeling;
- random orb/blob/particle/brain 3D objects;
- WebGL merely because Three.js is available;
- page loaders with fake counters or artificial minimum time;
- repeated fade-up section entrances;
- bounce, pop, spring, elastic or overshoot as generic marketing motion;
- custom scroll inside operational workspaces merely for smoothness;
- horizontal scrolling without semantic horizontal logic;
- carousels with no orientation or direct control;
- hover-only essential information;
- desktop choreography squeezed onto mobile;
- one visual template reused for all five portfolio products;
- invented testimonials, metrics, awards, users, results, confidence percentages, science claims or product capabilities;
- copy whose voice is obviously constructed from repetitive AI marketing patterns.

## 18. Permanent content prohibitions

Do not write:

- generic agency filler about “crafting digital experiences at the intersection of design and technology”;
- inflated AI language when AI is infrastructure rather than proposition;
- fake scientific authority;
- promises the product cannot prove;
- paragraphs full of unnecessary em dashes;
- every sentence as a fragment;
- every heading as two punchy fragments;
- repetitive “No X. No Y. Just Z.” cadence;
- repetitive “Simple X. Powerful Y.” cadence;
- repetitive “Built for X. Designed for Y.” cadence;
- text that could be moved to an unrelated SaaS product unchanged.

No punctuation mark is banned. **Patterned artificiality is banned.**

---

# PART IV — REFERENCE INTELLIGENCE: WHAT EACH SITE ACTUALLY TAUGHT US

## 19. Reference hierarchy by design problem

No single reference owns a future Valtum website. The research is deliberately problem-based.

| Design problem | Highest-value reference intelligence | Principle to transfer | Surface not to transfer |
|---|---|---|---|
| Image-led world building | White Desert | Environment can persist while foreground meaning changes; media sequence controls scale and emotion | Antarctica, ice palette, camp cards, coordinates |
| Strong identity continuity | Lando Norris | Repeated symbolic actors/motifs can connect distant chapters | Lime, helmets, signature, motorsport language |
| Protagonist transformation | Oryzo | One central idea can change media representation without losing identity | Coaster, fake research satire, olive world |
| Branded loading | Outfit | Loading can be the first authored state and hand directly into product/brand | Numeric `000`, exact red/cream system, wordmark choreography |
| Complex service explanation | Inversa | A complicated operation becomes memorable through a few named, evidence-backed states | Lime/black ecology styling, field graphics |
| Portfolio credibility | Jasmine Gunarto | Show process, role, tools, context, credits, reflection and artifacts, not only final screenshots | Exact editorial layout and type language |
| Motion-system thinking | Osmo | Name interaction primitives and build reusable mechanics | Radial carousel, black navigation, resource-library skin |
| Experimental studio authorship | Studio K95 | Portfolio indexing and project presentation can feel strongly authored | Rings/Spiral, royal blue field, split-letter treatment |
| Progressive enhancement warning | Igloo | Renderer failure must not erase the product/company story | All-or-nothing WebGL gate |
| Persistent motif → proof | Aether | Carry identity from emotional scene into specifications/information | Blue rings, fictional audio-product surface |
| Serious atmospheric pacing | Darknode | Intensity can alternate with structured information and chapter resets | Military/tactical visual language |
| Physical → digital operational proof | Terminal Industries | Show the physical system and interactive consequence; use real calculators/data when meaningful | Lime enterprise surface, floating rounded header, generic cards |
| Header/hero integration | White Desert, Lando, Glyphic | Navigation belongs to the opening composition | Exact header placements |
| Mobile product thinking | Apple/platform research + Behance/Dribbble | Recompose priorities and inputs; do not only reduce width | Static presentation-board layouts |
| Dashboard hierarchy | Operational SaaS/product research | Attention/action first, correct data structures, restrained state color | Fashionable dashboard skins |
| Creative frontend architecture | Lusion, Dogstudio, Unseen, GSAP/browser platform | Layer semantics, state, motion, rendering, fallbacks and performance | Any studio’s internal framework |

The matrix is a guardrail. Before saying “we should do this like X,” identify **which problem** X solved and whether our product has the same problem.

## 20. White Desert — the image-led benchmark

White Desert is one of the deepest references in the brain because it proves that a website can be cinematic while remaining bright, editorial and specific to its subject.

### 20.1 Header and hero as one composition

The opening navigation does not sit in a detached bar. It occupies the Antarctic visual field alongside the huge location word, moving media, short proposition and film action. The page therefore begins as one authored scene.

This permanently reinforces the header doctrine:

> **At first viewport, navigation is a layer of the hero/world.**

Later transformations are allowed when contrast or task changes, but they must be scene-driven rather than “after 100 px turn the navbar into a blurred white pill.”

### 20.2 Images are structural

The site is not text plus photography. Photography establishes environment, scale, wildlife, camps, human vulnerability, route and operational reality.

The most useful image rhythm is:

**wide environment → close subject → human scale → detail → another environment → visual release.**

This is now a default sequencing question whenever we art-direct a long image-led page.

### 20.3 Persistent worlds

The famous camp sequence teaches a deeper rule than “horizontal scrolling.” The cracked-ice environment becomes a long-lived substrate while different camp cards move through it. The background/world persists longer than individual content.

This creates continuity because the visitor is not constantly asked to rebuild a mental model from a completely new section background.

### 20.4 Directional priming

The landscape fractures into vertical slices before the lateral camp movement fully begins. The next spatial logic is prepared before it is demanded from the user.

That produces the concept of **directional priming**:

> A major change of movement direction should be visually motivated before the new interaction is in full force.

### 20.5 Movement inheritance

One scene can hand direction, background, velocity, object, scale, color or alignment to the next. The site does not always “finish a component” and start another.

For our future scenes, explicitly ask:

- what survives the transition?
- what enters before the old state is gone?
- what movement does the new scene inherit?
- can the page feel like one system changing state instead of stacked modules?

### 20.6 Cinematic does not mean dark

White snow, bright daylight, pale blues and huge open fields still feel cinematic because the site controls attention, scale, image timing, perspective, crop and silence.

Permanent definition:

> **Cinematic = authored attention over time.**

It is not a black overlay preset.

### 20.7 White space as rhythm

The page alternates visual density with editorial rest. A quiet quote or wide white text field makes the next visual scene stronger.

Image-led does not mean image-everywhere.

### 20.8 Footer as a final scene

The final grid, utility information and enormous brand name resolve the journey. The site has an ending, not merely a copyright block.

This is the standard for Valtum footers: **utility must remain useful, but the final viewport should feel intentionally concluded.**

## 21. Lando Norris — identity as a recurring actor

Lando’s site is useful because it does not rely on one consistent background or one consistent section shape. Identity persists through symbols.

### 21.1 Helmet as protagonist and archive object

The helmet appears as racing equipment, personal object, edge-cropped composition, archive/grid material and footer protagonist. That creates continuity over a very long page.

The lesson is not “repeat one image.” It is:

> **An identity object can change role while remaining recognizable.**

### 21.2 Signature as motion/graphic token

The lime handwritten mark moves from loader/identity moment into typography overlays and other chapters. A brand-motion token can connect different content states without forcing every section to share the same layout.

### 21.3 Chapter contrast

The page can move dark → light → dark without losing identity because the symbolic actors, typography behavior and chrome remain coherent.

This is why our sites do not need one monotonous background to feel consistent.

### 21.4 Editorial collage

Personal images are allowed to be asymmetrical, edge-cropped and differently scaled when the composition has enough negative space and metadata to keep them intentional.

A collage is not automatically a random masonry grid.

## 22. Oryzo / Lusion — the most important concept-to-engineering reference

Oryzo remains one of the most important references, not because we want a 3D product gimmick, but because it demonstrates **design method**.

### 22.1 Four high-value principles

The documented Oryzo direction can be reduced to:

- realistic imagery;
- product/protagonist at the center;
- seamless transitions;
- humor or human character.

Our products will translate those principles differently.

### 22.2 Design without ego

When renders, props, photography, scan material, illustration and the protagonist are already rich, the UI should often become quieter.

The lesson is crucial:

> **Do not make every layer compete to prove that it was designed.**

Typography, palette and UI complexity can reduce when the world itself carries identity.

### 22.3 Typography as a physical actor

A headline can behave spatially:

- pass behind/around a protagonist;
- become an environmental plane;
- change width/scale with scene state;
- transition from display object into interface label;
- be partially occluded if legibility remains intentionally managed.

This is more sophisticated than merely increasing `font-size`.

### 22.4 Human irregularity
