---

# 20. PHOTO ART DIRECTION

All selected images need one common treatment.

Not a filter preset.

A controlled editorial grade.

## Grade goals

- natural skin;
- restrained saturation;
- strong blacks but preserved shadow detail;
- consistent white balance;
- modest highlight rolloff;
- no fake teal/orange cinema grade;
- no purple AI lighting;
- no heavy blue night coding scenes as hero imagery;
- subtle film grain only if it genuinely unifies the set;
- preserve material realism.

## Cropping

Every image must have:

- desktop hero crop;
- desktop crawler crop;
- tablet crop;
- mobile crop where required;
- focal point metadata.

Do not let CSS `object-fit: cover` make every final art-direction decision.

---

# 21. PALETTE — FINAL METHOD

The biggest mistake in prior passes was choosing an accent before the visual world existed.

Therefore:

# THE BODY HAS NO ARBITRARY IDENTITY ACCENT.

## Locked base

- Pure white
- near-black / carbon
- graphite
- cool neutral gray
- image color

These are structural colors only.

## Scene color

Individual scenes may borrow a solid tone sampled from their own imagery when that tone:

- supports the media;
- passes contrast;
- does not read as blue-purple AI;
- does not become an app-wide accent;
- is not cream/beige/ivory;
- is not yellow highlighter;
- is not generic green;
- is not orange crypto;
- is not decorative gradient.

## Footer color

The footer **must** have a distinct full-bleed color field.

But the exact color is intentionally **not selected until the final hero/media board exists**.

This is a deliberate art-direction gate.

The footer color must be chosen by:

1. placing the final 12–16 primary images on one board;
2. extracting 6–10 candidate deep/saturated tones;
3. removing disallowed families;
4. testing huge Instrument Sans in white/black on each tone;
5. testing adjacent transition from the preceding scene;
6. testing mobile OLED / ordinary laptop brightness;
7. choosing the tone that feels inevitable with the media.

No more arbitrary “oxblood because it sounds premium.”

---

# 22. TYPOGRAPHY

## Family

Instrument Sans remains the primary candidate and should stay unless the final media prototype proves it wrong.

The latest screenshots show that the family itself is not the primary problem.

The use of it is.

## Hero

Do not place a giant paragraph inside a white rectangle.

Hero display typography should:

- live in the same field as imagery;
- remain readable without creating a card;
- sometimes allow image overlap / occlusion;
- have an intentional 2–4 line break;
- use width axis for character;
- avoid excessive weight.

## Major scene copy

A major scene does not automatically get a 90px H2.

Some scenes may use:

- 38–52px;
- a large image;
- minimal copy.

Other scenes may use:

- 80–110px;
- almost no imagery.

Rhythm matters more than consistency of size.

## Microtype

Delete the pseudo-editorial system:

- no `02`;
- no `04`;
- no `Review`;
- no `Lenses`;
- no tiny pre-title labels;
- no eyebrow copy.

Functional UI labels are allowed only inside actual product interaction.

---

# 23. FINAL HOMEPAGE MOVIE

The homepage is designed as a film with connected scenes.

It is **not** a stack of sections.

---

# SCENE 00 — COLD ARRIVAL

## Purpose

Establish craft immediately without a fake loader.

## Behavior

If critical hero media is not decoded:

- show Personality Assessor identity on a clean field;
- actual load progress determines duration;
- no fake percentage;
- no decorative counter;
- transition begins as soon as hero is ready.

On warm revisit:

- skip almost entirely.

## Handoff

The identity settles into the real header as the hero media becomes visible.

This must feel like one object changing scale/position.

---

# SCENE 01 — HERO: MANY WORLDS, ONE PERSON

## Composition

One full-screen visual field.

No white card.

No copy container pasted over an image.

Desktop contains:

- one dominant 55–65vw environmental photograph;
- one tall human/detail crop;
- one macro work-detail crop;
- one partially offscreen image;
- headline;
- concise supporting copy;
- two actions;
- integrated header.

Media overlaps in depth.

Some images may extend outside viewport edges.

No visible borders.

No uniform radii.

No card shadows.

## Header

Header belongs to this field.

It may sit directly over white negative space or image depending crop.

No separate white strip.

## Type

Headline is large but not the entire page.

It can cross a media boundary when the crop allows.

No text over faces.

## Motion

On arrival:

- media reveals at slightly different timings;
- not every image fades;
- dominant image can reveal through crop/mask;
- secondary images slide from actual spatial edges;
- title settles with a small width / tracking adjustment.

On scroll:

the hero media pieces **become the next scene's Work Worlds media stream**.

This is the first major continuity requirement.

---

# SCENE 02 — WORK WORLDS

## Purpose

Show the variety of professional contexts without explaining it through cards.

## Content

Use approximately 9–12 worlds.

Candidate sequence:

- student research;
- software development;
- UX research;
- data / analytics;
- electronics;
- hands-on prototyping;
- collaboration;
- workstation / operations;
- field engineering;
- product planning;
- solo research;
- project delivery.

## Desktop geometry

Mixed aspect ratios.

No identical slides.

At any moment the viewport should contain:

- one dominant image;
- parts of 2–4 neighboring images;
- no blank rail;
- no uniform card captions.

The rail should feel editorial, not e-commerce.

## Scroll

One bounded horizontal travel chapter.

Vertical scroll drives horizontal movement.

The distance is derived from actual rail travel, not a fixed 200svh guess.

Velocity may subtly affect:

- crop lag;
- nearby image offset;
- text inertia.

Do not skew the whole page.

## Captions

Use one active description area or sparse image captions.

Do not print labels under every item like a portfolio grid.

## Handoff

As the rail ends, one active image becomes the selected context.

Other images leave.

The selected image stays.

This is not optional.

---

# SCENE 03 — SELECTED WORLD / FOCUS

The selected world now fills most of the viewport.

The user should feel:

“we stopped moving across worlds; now we are looking more closely at this one.”

## Visual transformation

The active image:

- expands;
- crop changes;
- background clears;
- macro detail or document fragment appears;
- the scene becomes quieter.

No hard section cut.

---

# SCENE 04 — CONTEXT BECOMES ASSESSMENT

This is the product's key demonstration.

## Input material

Use a first-party designed CV / professional-context artifact.

Not tags.

Not:

`Stage Graduate`
`Field Software`
`Skills JavaScript`

as a permanent marketing layout.

Those values can exist inside the real product interaction, but the public story should first show something closer to real input:

- CV fragment;
- project description;
- degree title;
- portfolio image;
- short work-history line;
- relevant skill excerpt.

## Transformation

The selected image and document artifact reorganize.

The system visually identifies useful contextual material.

Do not highlight with yellow boxes.

Possible techniques:

- text crop moves closer;
- irrelevant text reduces in opacity;
- selected phrases become larger;
- document fragments physically regroup;
- image and document share a moving mask.

The user then sees a question that clearly relates to that context.

## Key rule

Do not show all context columns and question UI at once.

The visitor should *experience the translation*.

---

# SCENE 05 — ADAPTIVE QUESTION

## Purpose

Let the visitor feel the assessment is context-sensitive.

The same viewport can switch between:

- Student / research;
- Software / systems;
- Engineering.

But switching is not a row of generic tabs at the top.

Use the media itself as the switch.

Examples:

- swipe between three contextual images;
- select one of three environment thumbnails integrated into the scene;
- image changes → document changes → question changes.

The question is the visual consequence.

---

# SCENE 06 — ANSWER → PROFILE EMERGENCE

The user's answer should not simply toggle a black button.

A response should trigger a subtle structural change.

For example:

- question field compresses;
- media crop recedes;
- first profile mass appears;
- the scene opens into interpretation.

The next scene feels earned.

---

# SCENE 07 — ONE PROFILE, FOUR READINGS

## Rebuild from zero

No horizontal bars.

No five primitive rectangles sitting on an empty field.

The system needs a **custom analytical visual language**.

## Principle

Each reading is a different way to view the same profile.

The content changes.

The world should still feel connected.

---

## BIG FIVE / OCEAN

Recommended direction:

Five tall vertical **portrait apertures / masses**.

Each one contains:

- label;
- value;
- a cropped fragment of the selected professional image or a neutral material field.

The value changes:

- visible aperture height;
- crop position;
- density.

This makes the visualization visually related to the user's work world.

It is not a generic bar chart.

---

## RIASEC

Six spatial territories around a central field.

No radar polygon.

No classic hexagon chart.

Use six moving zones with:

- varying scale;
- distance from center;
- typographic emphasis.

---

## WORK VALUES

Use a dynamic editorial ranking.

High-value dimensions occupy more visual space.

Words become spatial material.

No card grid.

---

## CAREER SIGNALS

Use four large directional fields.

Each signal can control:

- scale;
- depth;
- crop;
- typographic position.

---

## TRANSITIONS BETWEEN READINGS

Use Flip only when the same elements actually move.

Avoid applying Flip to unrelated replacement trees.

The user should perceive one profile reorganizing itself.

---

# SCENE 08 — CAREER WORLDS

The world opens back into photography.

This should feel like a return to the real world after interpretation.

## Gallery

Use 6–8 career environments.

Desktop:

- draggable / scrollable editorial gallery;
- true pointer drag;
- inertia;
- active item can temporarily dominate the viewport;
- adjacent worlds remain visible.

Mobile:

- native swipe / snap.

## Careers

Use verified / curated role families.

Do not imply exhaustive matching.

## Image treatment

Active career environment can become nearly full-height.

Career title integrates with image.

No small caption card.

No black rectangle label.

---

# SCENE 09 — RELATIONSHIP, NOT SCORE

After selecting a career, the photo remains.

The career relationship appears **inside the same scene**.

Avoid:

- three-column data panel;
- comparison table;
- ruled rows;
- low-contrast navy on black;
- percentage “match score” if methodology does not support it.

## Composition

One side remains visual.

The other becomes:

- “why it relates”;
- “what differs”;
- “what to develop.”

This can be a large typographic composition with selective product UI.

The image is still part of the reasoning.

---

# SCENE 10 — DEVELOPMENT LOOP

The relationship does not end with a recommendation.

It becomes work.

## Visual language

A cinematic filmstrip / editorial sequence.

Use 4–6 images:

- gap / unfamiliar task;
- deliberate practice;
- project output;
- review;
- new evidence;
- return.

No numbered process.

No horizontal line.

No three cards.

## Motion

The selected career image can break into the first development frame.

Then the filmstrip carries the visitor forward.

---

# SCENE 11 — TRUST / HUMAN LAYER

After heavy media and motion, the site becomes calmer.

This is where bespoke illustration enters.

Not a crude SVG line diagram.

## Illustration concept

A hand-drawn / vector hybrid showing:

- person;
- work artifacts;
- profile layers;
- boundaries between scoring, AI interpretation and career exploration.

The illustration must be professionally composed.

No puzzle pieces.

No brain.

No AI network.

No smiling corporate mascot.

---

# SCENE 12 — FINAL FUTURE / FOOTER

## Purpose

End as an experience, not a sitemap.

## Color

A distinct full-bleed field chosen only after the final media board is complete.

## Typography

Very large statement.

Potential copy direction:

**Your work will change.  
Your profile should keep up.**

or

**Build a profile that changes with your work.**

Final copy should be selected after composition testing.

## Media

Optional one quiet final image or moving image fragment.

Do not let the footer become another gallery.

## Utility

Product / Trust / Privacy / Account links arrive later and smaller.

No line separating creative ending from utility.

No black four-column footer.

---

# 24. HEADER — ONE ACTOR ACROSS THE SITE

The header must be part of the scene.

## Initial

Integrated into hero.

No background strip.

No border.

No glass.

No rounded floating container.

## During image-heavy scenes

Tone can adapt automatically to underlying image / scene.

## During light analytical scene

Simple transparent or lightly solid state.

## During dark career scene

White foreground.

## During footer

Footer-compatible tone.

## Motion

Do not simply toggle a white rectangle after `80px`.

State changes are scene-driven.

---

# 25. SMOOTH SCROLL — TARGET FEEL

The user asked for premium smooth scrolling across the entire public marketing ecosystem.

This is valid.

But “smooth” is not a number.

The motion must feel:

- responsive;
- weighted;
- reversible;
- never rubbery;
- never delayed;
- never disconnected from wheel/trackpad input.

## Desktop

Use one global smooth-scroll system on marketing routes.

Preferred implementation choices:

### Option A
Existing GSAP ScrollSmoother, correctly scene-owned.

### Option B
Lenis + GSAP ScrollTrigger if velocity / custom scheduling is easier.

The final choice should be based on browser feel, not reference-site imitation.

## Touch

Native.

## Reduced motion

Native.

---

# 26. PAGE-LEVEL MOTION CONDUCTOR

Every cinematic page should have one page-level motion controller.

Do not attach unrelated scroll listeners to every section.

The controller owns:

- hero release;
- Work Worlds;
- selected-world handoff;
- profile scene;
- career scene;
- footer arrival.

Local components can own:

- hover;
- drag;
- small state transitions.

---

# 27. MOTION PHYSICS

## Scroll-linked

Use direct / near-direct progress mapping.

No elastic ease.

No bounce.

No overshoot on scroll.

## Discrete interactions

Use controlled easing.

Target families:

- power2;
- power3;
- expo only for rare large scene shifts;
- custom cubic when browser testing proves it.

## Velocity

Use subtly for:

- image-crawler crop lag;
- filmstrip micro-offset;
- direction-aware captions.

Never make text unreadable.

---

# 28. REVERSAL RULE

Every important transition must work in reverse.

Test:

- 0%;
- 25%;
- 50%;
- 75%;
- 100%.

At every point:

- composition is valid;
- no blank viewport;
- no overlapping scene ownership;
- no incoming headline underneath an outgoing pinned layer;
- image masks remain coherent;
- header tone remains correct.

---

# 29. IMAGE CRAWLERS — THREE DIFFERENT SYSTEMS

The user specifically wants rich image scrollers.

Use three systems with different narrative roles.

---

## CRAWLER A — WORK WORLDS

Purpose: breadth.

Motion: scroll-driven horizontal journey.

Character:

- mixed sizes;
- editorial spacing;
- some edge crops;
- one dominant active world;
- vertical scroll → horizontal travel.

Not infinite.

Not autoplay.

---

## CRAWLER B — CAREER WORLDS

Purpose: choice.

Motion:

- drag;
- inertia;
- snap;
- active expansion.

Different from Work Worlds.

Not the same component restyled.

---

## CRAWLER C — DEVELOPMENT REEL

Purpose: return / evolution.

Motion:

- slower;
- film-like;
- can continue with native horizontal movement;
- alternating image heights allowed;
- less interactive than Career Worlds.

---

# 30. ROUTE TRANSITIONS

Public marketing pages should feel like one ecosystem.

Use the Living Frame as transition logic.

Examples:

- clicked image expands;
- page content moves behind it;
- destination scene opens from the same frame.

For text-only navigation:

- short solid-field wipe or media-mask transition;
- 450–700ms;
- no fake loader.

Reduced motion:

- immediate or tiny opacity transition.

---

# 31. HOW IT WORKS — UNIQUE PAGE LANGUAGE

The current numbered pseudo-editorial structure is rejected.

## New page

The page is one continuous transformation.

Use one persistent media frame.

Sequence:

1. real professional input;
2. CV / context capture;
3. system interpretation;
4. adaptive question;
5. multiple readings;
6. career exploration.

The same selected media actor changes role as the page progresses.

No `01 / 02 / 03`.

No tiny `Review / Lenses`.

No decorative image slivers.

---

# 32. CAREER INTELLIGENCE — UNIQUE PAGE LANGUAGE

Start with work-world imagery, not an information panel.

Hero:

- career environments dominate;
- title integrates with imagery;
- visitor can drag/scroll between worlds.

Then:

profile → career relationship is demonstrated.

No generic left-copy/right-photo.

No static three-column relationship panel.

No horizontal rules.

---

# 33. PROGRESS — UNIQUE PAGE LANGUAGE

The page should visually feel like **time and work evolving**.

Use:

- before / later work photography;
- project images;
- changing crops;
- profile visual snapshots;
- development reel.

The page can return to the same person/work environment at different stages.

No giant decorative `42 / 56 / 51 / 69`.

---

# 34. METHODOLOGY — QUIET BUT DEEPLY DESIGNED

Not every page should be cinematic.

Methodology needs authority.

Use:

- custom illustrations;
- annotated product visuals;
- interactive construct explanations;
- accessible textual definitions;
- one or two sticky visual moments.

No crude line illustration.

No generic chart.

No numbered editorial sequence.

---

# 35. TRUST — HUMAN CLARITY

Quiet page.

One major custom illustration.

Short sections.

Clear boundaries.

Primary goals:

- AI role;
- scoring role;
- limitations;
- privacy;
- data ownership;
- non-clinical framing.

Motion should be very restrained.

---

# 36. PRIVACY — CONTROL, NOT MARKETING

Use actual control concepts:

- export;
- deletion;
- account deletion;
- transparency.

Illustration can explain control.

No dramatic generic marketing hero.

---

# 37. LOGIN / SIGNUP

The current split-screen composition is rejected.

Auth must remain task-first.

## New concept

One strong immersive media field forms the outer environment.

The form sits in a quiet area created by the composition.

Not:

heading left;
random image middle;
form right.

Possible arrangement:

- one large environmental image partially occupies background;
- a calm solid area hosts the form;
- Personality Assessor identity integrates in upper area;
- media moves only slightly on arrival.

No smooth-scroll spectacle.

---

# 38. ILLUSTRATION SYSTEM — PUBLIC + FUTURE DASHBOARD

The user explicitly wants the category of illustrated content shown in the supplied reference.

The future system should be substantially more authored than generic stock vector art.

## Style

Hybrid editorial / product illustration.

Combine:

- clean vector geometry;
- human figures;
- work objects;
- document fragments;
- expressive hands;
- simple spatial perspective;
- occasional hand-drawn texture.

## Avoid

- gradients;
- purple AI palettes;
- generic blue SaaS;
- puzzle pieces;
- brains;
- network nodes;
- robots;
- floating icons;
- corporate Memphis blobs;
- fake 3D clay people.

## Motion

Rive or SVG/GSAP for:

- eye movement;
- small hand movement;
- page/document change;
- object position change;
- tiny responsive state.

No looping bounce.

---

# 39. DASHBOARD CONTINUATION — FUTURE PRINCIPLE

The authenticated dashboard should not visually become another product.

Carry forward:

- Instrument Sans;
- the media/illustration language;
- strong product-specific visual hierarchy;
- calm surfaces;
- sparse structural separators;
- intentional data visualization.

Illustration is appropriate for:

- no assessment yet;
- CV upload;
- first profile;
- no career comparison;
- roadmap empty state;
- progress milestone;
- privacy actions.

---

# 40. COLOR IN DASHBOARD

Public-site image color does not mean the dashboard becomes colorful.

Dashboard remains controlled.

Use:

- neutral foundation;
- semantic status colors;
- one limited brand event color after the public palette is finalized;
- separate chart palette only when data needs it.

---

# 41. MEDIA ENGINEERING

Every final raster asset needs:

- original master;
- optimized JPEG fallback;
- AVIF;
- WebP;
- intrinsic dimensions;
- focal point;
- mobile crop if needed;
- provenance.

Widths:

- 640;
- 960;
- 1440;
- 1920;
- 2560 only for true hero assets that need it.

Do not upscale.

---

# 42. PERFORMANCE BUDGET

## Initial hero

Only preload:

- one dominant hero image;
- necessary font subset;
- essential CSS/JS.

Secondary hero fragments may preload only if measurement proves they are needed for first-frame composition.

## Crawlers

Do not preload 12 images at page start.

Use:

- near-viewport prefetch;
- first-next / previous asset warmup;
- lazy decode.

## Mobile

Use distinct smaller crops/assets where needed.

The reference research repeatedly shows device-specific media budgets are legitimate.

---

# 43. LCP / MEDIA PRIORITY

The hero must have one clear LCP candidate.

Avoid making 5 simultaneous hero images all priority-loaded.

The dominant image is priority.

Secondary visual fragments can appear milliseconds later.

---

# 44. PRODUCT UI AS MEDIA

Do not recreate fake UI for marketing once real product UI exists.

Capture real:

- CV review;
- question;
- result;
- career comparison;
- progress.

Use exact controlled demo data.

Never leak private user data.

---

# 45. RESPONSIVE CHOREOGRAPHY

Mobile is redesigned, not stacked.

## Hero

2–3 media actors maximum.

Own line breaks.

Headline remains strong but not overwhelming.

## Work Worlds

Native horizontal swipe / snap.

No pin.

## Context scene

Vertical transformation.

## Profile

Tap-driven readings.

## Career Worlds

Native swipe.

## Footer

Huge final typography survives with intentional reflow.

---

# 46. REDUCED MOTION

Reduced motion must preserve:

- scene hierarchy;
- selected context;
- media relationships;
- career selection;
- profile readability.

Remove:

- pinned travel;
- large transforms;
- inertia;
- masking sequences.

Do not simply disable CSS and expose broken intermediate states.

---

# 47. PREVIS REQUIREMENT

Before implementation, the next coding brief must include a timing storyboard for at least:

1. hero → Work Worlds;
2. Work Worlds → selected context;
3. context → question;
4. question → profile;
5. career selection → relationship;
6. development → footer.

Each storyboard states:

- actor A;
- actor B;
- start state;
- end state;
- scroll duration;
- reverse behavior;
- mobile replacement;
- reduced-motion replacement.

---

# 48. BROWSER ART-DIRECTION LOOP

The next implementation is not approved by:

- tests;
- lint;
- build;
- screenshot at one breakpoint.

It must be reviewed in a rendered browser.

## Desktop

- 1920×1080
- 1440×900
- 1366×768

## Tablet

- 1024×768
- 768×1024

## Mobile

- 430×932
- 390×844

---

# 49. MOTION QA

Record the complete homepage.

Test:

- cold load;
- slow scroll;
- normal scroll;
- fast wheel;
- rapid reversal;
- pause mid-transition;
- trackpad;
- drag;
- resize after load;
- route transition;
- reduced motion.

---

# 50. TEMPLATE-DISTANCE TEST

At final review ask:

Could this composition be reused unchanged for:

- a CRM;
- an AI chatbot;
- a fintech startup;
- a consulting agency?

If yes, reject it.

---

# 51. REFERENCE-SUBSTITUTION TEST

Replace all Personality Assessor content mentally with a different brand.

If the site still makes equal visual sense, it is too generic.

The world of professional context must be structurally necessary.

---

# 52. MEDIA-SUBSTITUTION TEST

Replace all work imagery with random architecture photographs.

If the site still works, the media is decorative.

Reject it.

---

# 53. SILHOUETTE TEST

Blur the page.

Major scenes should still have recognizable silhouettes:

- hero collage;
- horizontal Work Worlds;
- selected-world focus;
- profile interpretation;
- career world;
- development filmstrip;
- large final footer.

If everything becomes equal rectangles, reject it.

---

# 54. ANTI-LINE RULE

Public marketing structure may not use decorative horizontal rules.

Functional exceptions:

- input boundaries;
- actual data-table separators;
- accessible focus states;
- chart axes when analytically necessary.

No rule as decoration.

No heading + line.

No footer separator.

No active-tab underline as the primary state.

---

# 55. ANTI-LABEL RULE

Never reintroduce:

- `01`;
- `02`;
- `03`;
- `Review`;
- `Lenses`;
- `Current profile` as a tiny editorial marker above a marketing block;
- pseudo-instrument readouts unless the product genuinely produces them.

Product UI labels inside actual UI are different.

---

# 56. ANTI-CARD RULE

A content item is not automatically a card.

Prefer:

- composition;
- image mass;
- whitespace;
- scale;
- overlap;
- grouping;
- typography.

Cards are permitted only when semantic containment is necessary.

---

# 57. ANTI-AI-AESTHETIC RULE

No:

- blue/purple/cyan gradient;
- neon orb;
- glass panels;
- glowing neural network;
- circuit background;
- abstract particle brain;
- prompt box as hero;
- floating chatbot bubble as identity.

---

# 58. TECHNOLOGY PER ACTOR

## Header / type / copy
DOM + CSS + GSAP.

## Photography
Responsive image pipeline.

## Hero masks
CSS clip-path / mask or GSAP transforms.

## Work Worlds
DOM + GSAP ScrollTrigger.

## Context → question
DOM + GSAP / Flip.

## Profile visuals
SVG + DOM, optionally Canvas 2D only if SVG becomes limiting.

## Career gallery
DOM + pointer events / Draggable / native scroll fallback.

## Illustrations
SVG / Rive.

## Page transitions
DOM/CSS/GSAP.

## WebGL
No default role.

Only introduce if a later approved visual actor cannot be delivered with high quality another way.

---

# 59. WHY WEBGL IS NOT THE ANSWER

Oryzo and Igloo use WebGL because their subjects demand real-time 3D / shader behavior.

Personality Assessor currently does not.

Adding WebGL without a product-specific reason would create:

- complexity;
- load cost;
- GPU risk;
- generic spectacle.

Our premium quality should come first from:

- media;
- art direction;
- motion;
- compositional continuity.

---

# 60. MOTION PERFORMANCE

Avoid:

- React state updates on every scroll tick;
- forced layout in scroll callbacks;
- repeated DOM querying inside update loops;
- animation of width/height when transform can express the state;
- excessive blur;
- continuous filter changes.

Use:

- refs;
- cached nodes;
- GSAP contexts;
- CSS transforms;
- requestAnimationFrame where appropriate;
- state updates only when semantic state changes.

---

# 61. COPY PRINCIPLE

Copy is not the visual protagonist.

Use less.

Make it more specific.

The public page should not need paragraphs to explain every feature because the motion demonstrates the product.

---

# 62. HERO COPY DIRECTION

Do not reuse current white-card composition.

# Personality Assessor — Final Public Experience Art-Direction Lock

**Status:** Design/research lock before the next Codex implementation brief  
**Scope:** Public marketing experience, public internal pages, header, footer, marketing motion, media system, and visual direction that must later continue into onboarding/dashboard.  
**Core principle:** Do not build a generic SaaS site. Build an authored, image-led, motion-led product experience.

---

# 1. Why the previous directions failed

The previous public designs failed because they treated “premium” as one or more of the following:

- oversized editorial typography;
- arbitrary accent colors;
- horizontal rules and pseudo-editorial dividers;
- isolated stock photographs inside rectangles;
- section-by-section layouts;
- long pinned states that overlap the next section;
- data presented as simple ruled bars;
- dark backgrounds with insufficient text contrast;
- duplicated “evidence” tags pretending to be a persistent visual actor;
- generic product-marketing composition.

Those patterns are explicitly retired.

The next public experience must be designed around **media, spatial transformation, rhythm, and narrative continuity**.

---

# 2. Final creative thesis

## Working Worlds → Living Profile

The visual story begins with **many real ways of working** and gradually resolves them into **one evolving professional profile**.

The user should feel this progression:

**many work contexts → one selected context → context becomes assessment → assessment becomes multiple readings → readings become career relationships → relationships become development → profile remains useful over time**

The site does not need a decorative “AI object,” orb, brain, avatar, network, or floating tag system.

The real visual protagonist is the transformation between:

- real professional worlds;
- captured evidence;
- question logic;
- profile interpretation;
- career relationships;
- development.

The website should feel as if the product is progressively making a person's work legible.

---

# 3. Non-negotiable visual rules

## Permanently prohibited

- No decorative horizontal divider rules across public marketing pages.
- No “heading + hairline + content” section pattern.
- No horizontal chart-track aesthetic as the dominant data language.
- No giant editorial serif.
- No serif-led identity.
- No yellow highlighter system.
- No orange/vermilion identity system.
- No generic blue/purple/cyan AI identity.
- No green premium-tech identity.
- No pink identity.
- No beige/cream/ivory luxury palette.
- No gradients.
- No floating AI/SaaS pills.
- No eyebrow text.
- No micro-label + line + oversized heading editorial cliché.
- No generic left-copy/right-image hero.
- No repeated cards simply to create structure.
- No bento layout unless the information genuinely requires it.
- No image inserted into a random rectangle simply because the section needs media.
- No stock image whose only role is “person with laptop.”
- No repeated fade-up section animation.
- No long scroll pin that allows the next scene to collide with the current scene.
- No cheap bounce, zoom, spring, elastic motion, or decorative parallax.
- No WebGL because Three.js already exists.
- No fake loading counter.
- No illustration that looks like generic corporate Memphis, generic AI art, or stock “business illustration.”

---

# 4. Research-derived design principles

## Oryzo principle

A compelling experience can keep the core idea continuous while changing media language. Richness should come from the world, imagery, material, motion, humor/human detail, and transformation—not from stacking more UI decoration.

For Personality Assessor:

- product logic remains consistent;
- media language is allowed to change;
- the same context can appear as photography, document evidence, question context, data interpretation, and career comparison;
- UI supports the story rather than competing with it.

## White Desert principle

Horizontal or spatial motion earns its place when it has semantic meaning.

For Personality Assessor, horizontal travel is justified when moving through **different professional contexts** or **different possible career worlds**.

## Outfit principle

Craft is visible in type, photography, navigation, timing, breakpoints, and tiny interaction pauses.

For Personality Assessor:

- typography must lock precisely at every viewport;
- images must have deliberate crops;
- navigation belongs to the experience;
- media reveals should have intentional timing;
- route transitions should feel designed.

## Osmo principle

Premium motion is made from reusable mechanics—scroll-linked galleries, looping sliders, momentum, image reveals, page transitions, Flip, and controlled inertia—but those mechanics only work when the product story justifies them.

## Inversa principle

The product's own operational vocabulary should generate visual language.

For Personality Assessor, the visual language must come from:

- context;
- questions;
- interpretation;
- profile dimensions;
- comparison;
- development;
- progress.

## Igloo principle

High-quality imagery can coexist with fast performance when the image-loading architecture is treated as a first-class engineering system.

---

# 5. Final color system

The website must no longer be a pure monochrome utility page, but color must remain disciplined.

## Core

| Role | Value | Usage |
|---|---:|---|
| Clean White | `#FFFFFF` | Primary light canvas |
| Cool Paper | `#F2F4F3` | Localized secondary surface only |
| Ink | `#111311` | Primary text / dark controls |
| Graphite | `#303532` | Secondary dark text |
| Quiet Gray | `#7A817D` | Secondary copy |
| Mist | `#E6E9E7` | Subtle structural surfaces |
| Deep Night | `#0C0F0D` | Controlled dark narrative scenes |
| Oxblood | `#9B2F35` | Signature event color |

## Oxblood rules

Oxblood is **not** the page's everyday highlight color.

It may be used for:

- the final footer scene;
- selected route-transition moments;
- one or two high-value interactive states;
- a single meaningful data emphasis when needed;
- small brand punctuation.

It must **not** be used to:

- color words inside the hero headline;
- create tags;
- color every button;
- create colored cards;
- replace semantic status colors;
- turn the site into a red website.

Photography supplies most of the visual color.

## Dark scenes

Dark sections use:

- Deep Night `#0C0F0D`;
- true white or very light gray for primary text;
- clearly legible muted text;
- no navy-on-black;
- no “almost invisible premium” typography.

Any dark scene that cannot remain clearly readable at ordinary laptop brightness fails QA.

---

# 6. Typography

## Family

Retain **Instrument Sans Variable**.

The latest direction is materially stronger with this family and should not be reopened without a demonstrated failure in the browser.

## Typography philosophy

Hierarchy should come from:

- width axis;
- scale;
- line breaking;
- spatial placement;
- image interaction;
- controlled contrast;
- rhythm.

Not from:

- heavy `800` weights;
- serif/sans novelty pairing;
- uppercase micro-labels;
- colored words;
- huge headings everywhere.

## Roles

### Hero display
- Weight: ~500
- Width: ~86–92
- Tight but readable tracking
- Desktop target: approximately 86–116px depending viewport/composition
- Never allow the hero type to become the only visual event.

### Major scene title
- Approximately 56–82px desktop
- Width axis may change subtly between scenes
- Must be composed with media, not isolated above content.

### Internal-page display
- Approximately 64–96px desktop
- Every page gets its own composition, not the same hero template.

### Body
- 16–19px desktop
- Comfortable line length
- High readability
- Fewer marketing paragraphs; stronger editorial pacing.

### Data / product UI
- 13–18px
- Tabular numerals where useful
- Precise hierarchy
- No fake micro-editorial labels.

---

# 7. Media strategy

The next version needs **far more imagery**, but not filler.

## Target media inventory

The public marketing ecosystem should eventually contain approximately:

- 10–12 high-quality professional-context photographs for the homepage;
- 5–6 career-context photographs;
- 4–6 progress/development images;
- 3–5 document/product-evidence visuals;
- 3–5 bespoke illustrations or illustrated states;
- real UI/product visuals once the authenticated experience is redesigned.

Reuse is allowed only when the crop and narrative role genuinely change.

## Professional worlds to cover

Media should include several of these contexts:

- student / academic research;
- software engineering;
- UX / product design;
- electrical / electronics engineering;
- data / analytics;
- cybersecurity / monitoring where appropriate;
- collaborative planning;
- solo analysis;
- prototyping / maker work;
- professional document review;
- technical workshop;
- project delivery / team discussion.

## Current researched candidate image IDs

These are candidates, not automatic final selections:

- `NASjMHJ9OhI` — focused student studying at a library table.
- `TI_IwVpN_qE` — students working in a modern library.
- `lAbYmLWrT9o` — engineer working on a circuit board with a magnifying glass.
- `R-9lrQEb_Hg` — professional inspecting electronic equipment.
- `WN1ZZaWY2fU` — professional at a computer workstation.
- `U-Werwf32CM` — professional at a laptop.
- `w00FkE6e8zE` — UX team collaborating with sticky-note research.
- `hlFB4he18Fc` — UX practitioner working with an affinity diagram.
- `-7oi_5uJPC4` — person designing on a laptop.
- `n7tKiugbzaM` — team brainstorming on a glass wall.
- `qwtCeJ5cLYs` — real dashboard/data context.
- `vDHEsIu69Lk` — field engineering / solar context.
- existing professionally licensed repository images may remain only if they pass the new art-direction review.

## Media selection criteria

Every selected photograph must answer:

1. What exact professional context does this communicate?
2. What does this image add that copy cannot?
3. Does it create useful negative space or spatial composition?
4. Does it survive aggressive desktop/mobile crops?
5. Can it participate in motion?
6. Is it visually distinct from the other selected images?
7. Does it avoid implying that pictured people are users, assessment participants, or career-match recipients?

If an image cannot answer those questions, remove it.

---

# 8. Image processing and engineering

Codex must eventually:

- download only appropriately licensed sources;
- store original source locally;
- preserve provenance;
- generate AVIF and WebP;
- generate at least 640, 960, 1440, 1920 widths;
- add 2560 only when the original and hero role justify it;
- generate optimized JPEG fallback rather than serving a 5–8MB source JPEG;
- record intrinsic width/height;
- record focal point;
- support route-specific and mobile-specific crops where necessary;
- preload only the actual LCP media;
- lazy-load the rest;
- use correct `sizes`;
- decode lower-priority media asynchronously.

Performance is part of art direction.

---

# 9. Homepage hero — final direction

## Goal

The first viewport must immediately feel like a crafted experiential site, not a SaaS landing page.

## Composition

The hero is one integrated world containing:

- header;
- headline;
- multiple professional-context images;
- one concise support statement;
- primary/secondary action;
- the beginning of the work-world narrative.

Do **not** render:

`headline left | photograph right`.

## Media composition

Use approximately 3–5 visible media fragments at desktop:

- one large dominant professional-context image;
- one tall secondary crop;
- one or two edge fragments partially outside the viewport;
- optional small document/product evidence fragment.

The image shapes should be asymmetrical and composed as one spatial field.

No border around every image.

No card container around every image.

No decorative lines.

## Type and media interaction

The headline may sit partly behind or in front of a media edge when the composition remains readable.

No type over faces.

No arbitrary word highlighting.

## Header integration

At arrival:

- header has no detached bar;
- header shares hero background/visual world;
- no shadow;
- no border;
- no floating rounded container;
- no glassmorphism.

As the user leaves the opening world:

- header may transform into a simpler persistent state;
- the change should be tied to scene ownership;
- it may become solid white/black depending the scene;
- it must never feel like a separate website pasted on top.

## Arrival animation

No fake loader.

On first cold load only, if critical media is genuinely decoding:

- show a brief non-blocking arrival treatment;
- Personality Assessor identity can appear large for a moment and settle into the header;
- hero media reveals as soon as ready;
- maximum blocking time should remain short;
- cached/revisit loads should skip or materially shorten it.

---

# 10. Work Worlds crawler — major homepage actor

This is the first major image-scroller.

## Purpose

Demonstrate that the product adapts to different professional contexts.

## Content

Approximately 8–10 media items:

- Student / research
- Graduate / project work
- Software
- UX / product
- Electronics / engineering
- Analytics
- Cyber / operations
- Collaborative planning
- Maker / prototyping
- Optional additional role world

## Desktop behavior

- horizontal narrative justified by movement across professional worlds;
- one brief pinned interval, not an endless pin;
- variable image aspect ratios;
- images partly overlap the typographic field;
- scroll controls horizontal travel;
- motion is reversible;
- velocity can subtly influence travel/inertia;
- scrolling fast must not expose blank areas;
- no autoplay carousel controls;
- no visible horizontal scrollbar;
- no rule line beneath the rail.

## Mobile behavior

- native horizontal overflow / snap;
- explicit Previous / Next controls;
- no desktop pin;
- no fake smooth-scroll hijacking;
- image captions available to screen readers.

## Handoff

The crawler must not simply end.

One selected professional world becomes the context used in the next scene.

A photograph/crop should visually carry forward so the user perceives a transformation rather than a new section.

---

# 11. Context → assessment transformation

The selected professional world becomes structured assessment context.

The sequence should visually communicate:

**real work → captured evidence → structured context → question relevance**

Use:

- real image crop;
- document/CV fragment;
- compact structured fields;
- question UI.

Do not use:

- floating tags;
- ruled tables;
- yellow markers;
- duplicate “evidence pieces” that fade between separate components.

The same actor(s) should move/recompose when possible.

Use GSAP Flip when actual shared DOM identity changes layout.

---

# 12. Adaptive question scene

The question scene should demonstrate real product behavior.

A context switch can be interactive:

- Student
- Software / systems
- Engineering

Changing context should change:

- supporting media;
- structured context;
- question phrasing;
- visible relevant evidence.

This demonstrates personalization more powerfully than marketing copy.

The transition should be spatial and calm.

---

# 13. Profile lenses — replace horizontal bars

The current ruled horizontal-bar presentation is retired.

## Heading

**One profile, four lenses.**

## Four visual modes

### Big Five / OCEAN
Use five vertical forms/columns with different heights or masses. No horizontal tracks.

### RIASEC
Use six spatial cells or a radial/arc composition. Avoid radar-chart cliché if possible.

### Work Values
Use a ranked typographic composition or modular spatial arrangement.

### Career Signals
Use four clear large measures in a strong spatial composition.

The same underlying data items should reposition/recompose across lenses.

Use Flip for continuity.

Every view needs a textual accessible equivalent.

---

# 14. Career gallery + relationship scene

This route/section needs a second premium image system.

## Career gallery

Use 5–6 role-context images in a horizontal draggable/scrollable editorial gallery.

Possible careers:

- Software Engineer
- UX Designer
- Data Analyst
- Product Manager
- Cybersecurity Analyst
- one additional curated role if product truth supports it.

On desktop:

- image rail has controlled inertia;
- active career image can expand or move forward in z-order;
- title becomes part of the image composition;
- no thumbnail-card strip;
- no horizontal rule.

On mobile:

- native swipe/snap;
- strong focal crop;
- text below or over safe negative space.

## Relationship scene

After selection:

- no ruled comparison table;
- no three bordered columns;
- no navy-on-black;
- no yellow “Strong alignment.”

Use one authored dark scene.

The selected career image may remain partially visible or become a cropped background actor.

The relationship must expose:

- current profile;
- why it relates;
- what differs;
- what to develop.

Use composition, scale, grouping, and whitespace rather than divider lines.

---

# 15. Development / progress scene

Development should feel like work continuing, not a three-step UI component.

Use:

- 3–5 high-quality images;
- filmstrip/editorial sequence;
- contextual work imagery;
- one visual transformation from “difference” to “deliberate work” to “new evidence.”

No numbered timeline.

No horizontal process line.

No three identical cards.

---

# 16. Trust and methodology

These sections intentionally become calmer.

Use one bespoke illustration or technical editorial visual.

The purpose is clarity:

- AI can assist context interpretation, adaptive questions, narrative/coaching;
- structured scoring calculates core assessment outputs;
- results are for reflection/career exploration;
- not diagnosis;
- not hiring decision;
- not guaranteed success.

Illustration should support comprehension, not decorate.

---

# 17. Illustration system

The last user-provided reference is best described as **editorial product illustration / vector spot illustration**.

The project should develop its own illustration language.

## Visual qualities

- clean flat vector forms;
- human figures when context requires them;
- professional objects and tools;
- restrained geometry;
- no gradients;
- no generic purple/blue AI palette;
- no brain icon;
- no neural network motif;
- no robot;
- no corporate Memphis blobs;
- no stock puzzle-piece cliché unless semantically unavoidable;
- no smiling corporate mascot aesthetic.

## Palette

Illustrations should primarily use:

- Ink;
- white;
- cool gray;
- oxblood;
- natural secondary object colors only where useful.

## Uses

Public site:
- How It Works
- Trust / methodology
- occasional empty/transition moment

Future authenticated surfaces:
- dashboard empty states;
- onboarding;
- CV-processing/waiting states;
- first-assessment states;
- report explanations;
- privacy/data-control education;
- milestones;
- no-data analytics states.

## Motion

Illustrations may later use:

- Rive;
- SVG/GSAP;
- tiny stateful motion.

No looping cartoon bounce.

# 18. Smooth scrolling and motion system

## Public marketing routes

Premium smooth scrolling should be shared across:

- `/`
- `/how-it-works`
- `/career-intelligence`
- `/progress`
- `/methodology`
- `/trust`
- `/privacy`

Auth pages should remain native/task-first unless a later browser test proves otherwise.

## ScrollSmoother

Desktop/fine pointer only.

Starting tuning target:

- `smooth` approximately `0.70–0.80`;
- `effects: false`;
- `smoothTouch: false`;
- `normalizeScroll: false`.

The exact value must be tuned in browser, not treated as a magic number.

## Touch

Native.

## Reduced motion

Native.

## Motion vocabulary

Use:

- shared-element movement;
- image crop changes;
- masking;
- scale changes;
- z-order shifts;
- controlled horizontal translation;
- subtle velocity response;
- Flip-based layout transitions;
- route transitions;
- scene overlap only when both states remain compositionally valid.

Avoid:

- generic fade-up;
- repeated `y: 30`;
- bouncing;
- elastic easing;
- excessive opacity-only transitions;
- decorative motion on every card;
- parallax on everything.

---

# 19. Motion physics

Premium feel depends on interruption and reversal.

Every scroll-linked timeline must be tested at:

- 0%;
- 25%;
- 50%;
- 75%;
- 100%.

At every intermediate point:

- composition must remain valid;
- no blank viewport;
- no text collision;
- no incoming scene underneath a still-pinned outgoing scene;
- scrolling backward reconstructs the prior state;
- fast-wheel input does not break ownership.

Use one page-level conductor for major homepage scenes.

Do not scatter independent ScrollTriggers across every paragraph.

---

# 20. Route transitions

Marketing pages should feel like one ecosystem.

Use a restrained page transition:

- a full-viewport solid-color or media-mask transition;
- approximately 450–700ms total;
- transition should react to current/next page tone;
- no fake loading state;
- no page-long animation;
- reduced-motion = immediate or tiny crossfade.

A controlled oxblood transition may be used selectively to make the signature color feel intentional.

---

# 21. Internal page direction

## How It Works

Opening composition uses student/context media and product transformation.

Main body uses:

- sticky media window;
- changing professional imagery;
- context → review → questions → lenses → direction.

No horizontal rules.

No numbered pseudo-editorial list.

## Career Intelligence

The page opens with:

- career imagery/crawler;
- comparison interaction;
- large typographic relationship statement.

Absolutely no generic left-copy/right-photo hero.

No ruled comparison table.

## Progress

Use:

- visual history;
- 4–6 images;
- changing work context;
- trend/profile visual;
- filmstrip or editorial crawler.

No `42 / 56 / 51 / 69` floating as a decorative number line.

## Methodology

More structured, but still designed.

Use:

- diagrams;
- illustration;
- interactive construct explanations;
- methodology cards only when semantic;
- no decorative rules.

## Trust

Quiet visual chapter with one strong illustration.

## Privacy

Task/control-driven visual design.

Use illustrations only when they explain user control.

# 22. Premium footer — major signature scene

The footer is no longer black utility columns appended to the end.

Primary recommendation:

**Oxblood `#9B2F35`**

This is the main chromatic brand event.

Use one very large statement, approximately 9–13vw desktop.

Recommended direction:

**Your work will change.

No highlighted word.

As the preceding scene resolves:

# 23. Header behavior

The header must feel native to every scene.

## Hero

Transparent/integrated.

## Light scenes

Ink text; no background until needed for readability.

## Dark scenes

White text.

## Oxblood footer

White text.

## Sticky behavior

As the user scrolls:

- reduce spacing/height slightly;
- keep motion calm;
- no floating pill;
- no border line;
- no glass background;
- no huge sticky header.

Navigation should remain stable enough that users do not lose orientation.

# 24. Image-crawler engineering

At least two distinct image systems must exist.

## Crawler A — Work Worlds

Scroll-driven horizontal editorial rail.

## Crawler B — Career Worlds

Interactive/draggable career imagery.

## Optional Crawler C — Progress Filmstrip

Slow contextual sequence showing work evolving over time.

Do not use the same component with different content for all three.

Each should have a different narrative purpose and motion feel.

---

# 25. Performance budget

The site can be image-rich without becoming slow.

## LCP

- one hero media source only;
- eager/high priority;
- responsive source;
- correct dimensions;
- optimized fallback;
- composition chosen with performance in mind.

## Crawlers

- lazy-load offscreen media;
- first 1–2 upcoming crawler assets may be prefetched as the crawler approaches;
- do not preload 20 photographs on page start.

## Motion

- primarily transform/opacity;
- minimize expensive filter/blur;
- avoid layout reads inside scroll loops;
- use GSAP quick setters or cached references where useful;
- no continuous React state updates for scroll position.

## 3D

No WebGL for public marketing unless a later concept explicitly requires it.

---

# 26. Responsive choreography

Mobile is not desktop stacked vertically.

## Hero

- own image crop;
- fewer visible media fragments;
- own line breaks;
- header simplified;
- no cramped collage.

## Crawlers

Native horizontal snap.

## Context transformation

Vertical sequence.

## Profile lenses

Tap-first.

## Career

# 2. RESEARCH BASIS — WHAT TO TRANSFER, WHAT NOT TO COPY

This pass incorporates the final engineering research across Oryzo AI, White Desert, Lando Norris / OFF+BRAND, Aether1, Outfit, Osmo and related award-caliber productions.

Do **not** imitate their surface design. Transfer the engineering/design logic only.

## 2.1 Oryzo AI / Lusion — strongest engineering lesson

Official Lusion BTS material documents these principles:

- the pipeline follows the idea rather than allegiance to one technology;
- Oryzo tested image sequences, video and realtime PBR before choosing a hybrid solution;
- Gaussian splatting was used only where it improved the result;
- simpler texture mapping was used where it was visually stronger and cheaper;
- the scene dropped from roughly 900k attempted splats to about 78k desktop / 45k mobile when representation was chosen per actor;
- texture resolution was concentrated where the camera actually looks;
- UI was intentionally restrained because the visual world was already expressive;
- roughly 99% of type uses one family;
- the site intentionally uses very few colors;
- seamless transitions matter more than animation quantity;
- realistic imagery, a clear protagonist and scene continuity provide the authored quality.

### Transfer into Personality Assessor

- choose DOM/SVG/GSAP for actors that are fundamentally text/data/UI;
- do not use Three.js/WebGL merely because it exists in the repository;
- keep UI color restrained because photography and product data already supply visual information;
- create a small number of meaningful transformations instead of dozens of entrances;
- keep one dominant type family and create hierarchy through width, size, placement and rhythm;
- spend rendering/media budget where the user looks;
- mobile receives a reduced actor/motion budget, not a shrunken desktop scene.

### Do not copy

- Oryzo's coaster premise;
- desk world;
- cream/olive/orange palette;
- satire;
- Gaussian-splat aesthetic;
- fashion-magazine transition styling;
- hand/prop jokes.

## 2.2 White Desert / Malvah — semantic geometry

White Desert's live content makes geography, coordinates, route distance, runway, camps, aircraft and Antarctic landscape the narrative material. Horizontal/directional progression works because the journey itself is directional.

### Transfer

- spatial behavior must follow product meaning;
- media is authored around story states, not inserted into generic image cards;
- first-party/product-specific evidence is more valuable than interchangeable stock photography;
- transition direction should be semantically defensible.

### Do not copy

- Antarctic palette;
- coordinate styling;
- expedition-map visual language;
- horizontal travel merely because the reference uses it.

## 2.3 Lando Norris / OFF+BRAND — identity continuity + responsive reduction

Documented Webflow material shows that the Lando site uses identity-specific media and interaction, a brief load state for rich assets, and responsive behavior that becomes less condensed/more interactive on larger screens. Mobile is treated as its own interaction context.

### Transfer

- use assets that are genuinely tied to the subject;
- do not force desktop spectacle onto mobile;
- richer motion is allowed only where device capability and space support it;
- navigation belongs to the same opening identity world.

### Do not copy

- F1/helmet language;
- lime signature styling;
- loader just because Lando has one;
- mandatory orientation guard.

## 2.4 Aether1 / OFF+BRAND — hybrid rendering

Webflow documents Aether1 as GSAP-powered and combining baked 3D choreography with realtime generative effects.

### Transfer

- bake/static-render deterministic content where realtime rendering adds no value;
- reserve interactive runtime work for elements whose state actually responds to user input;
- performance strategy is part of art direction.

### Personality decision

No WebGL/Three/R3F is required for Pass 3 marketing. Product evidence, document transformation and analytical geometry are better represented with semantic DOM + SVG + GSAP.

## 2.5 Osmo — interaction mechanics, not aesthetic

Osmo exposes reusable mechanics such as GSAP Flip, ScrollTrigger, Lenis setups, momentum interactions, path animation, image-to-background transforms and Barba transitions.

### Transfer

- use Flip only when the same visual actor genuinely changes layout/state;
- use one motion system consistently;
- write explicit lifecycle/cleanup code;
- interaction must preserve keyboard/touch alternatives.

### Do not copy

- gimmicks;
- magnetic/cursor effects without product meaning;
- marquees;
- physics toys;
- unnecessary page-transition spectacle.

## 2.6 GSAP implementation facts to respect

From GSAP's official documentation:

- create `ScrollSmoother` before page ScrollTriggers;
- ScrollSmoother keeps native scroll semantics and should not smooth touch by default;
- numeric `scrub` creates controlled catch-up between native scroll and timeline progress;
- `anticipatePin: 1` is useful for large pinned panels where fast scrolling can reveal a pin flash;
- `invalidateOnRefresh: true` recalculates values after refresh/resize;
- `gsap.matchMedia()` automatically manages responsive setup/reversion;
- Flip is appropriate for state/layout transitions and can match separate targets by `data-flip-id` when necessary.

### Personality policy

- use ScrollSmoother on **homepage desktop/fine-pointer only**;
- internal marketing pages use native scrolling unless a specific interaction requires ScrollTrigger;
- auth pages use native scrolling;
- touch always uses native scroll;
- no Lenis/Locomotive/new scroll dependency;
- no snap;
- no fake scrollbar.

- therapy-brand-like;
- HR surveillance-like;
- crypto/cyberpunk;
- blue/purple AI SaaS;
- editorial fashion magazine;
- monochrome luxury perfume brand;

- generic SaaS with a radar chart;
- Awwwards-template poster with scroll effects.

# 5. TYPOGRAPHY — FINAL PASS 3 LOCK

## 5.1 Single dominant family

Use **Instrument Sans Variable** as the sole public marketing/auth type family in Pass 3.

Reason:

- open-source OFL family;
- supports `wdth` 75–100 and `wght` 400–700;
- enough personality to avoid system-font blandness;
- width axis lets us author display proportions without giant bold text;
- one-family discipline follows the strongest Oryzo design lesson: expressive composition with restrained typographic inventory.

Remove Source Serif 4 and Source Sans 3 from public usage and package dependencies when no protected code depends on them.

### Package

Use:

`@fontsource-variable/instrument-sans@^5.3.0`

Import the variable file that includes width + weight support (`wdth.css` or the appropriate Fontsource standard variant after verifying local package contents). Do not import unnecessary italic/full variants.

## 5.2 Font roles

### Brand / header / UI

- width: 96–100
- weight: 500–600
- tracking: `-0.01em` to `-0.025em`

### Display

- width: 84–90
- weight: 480–520 (CSS may use 500 if browser/package only exposes conventional values while variable axis remains set)
- no weight above 600 in a marketing H1/H2
- tracking: `-0.035em` to `-0.055em`
- never use `font-weight: 700` as a shortcut for impact.

### Body

- width: 98–100
- weight: 400–450
- line-height: 1.5–1.62
- max readable measure: approximately 55–68 characters depending context.

### Data

- width: 96–100
- weight: 500
- tabular numerals where supported/appropriate.

## 5.3 Exact type scale

### Hero H1

Desktop ≥1280:

```css
font-size: clamp(64px, 6.3vw, 112px);
line-height: .90;
font-weight: 500;
font-variation-settings: "wdth" 86, "wght" 500;
letter-spacing: -.048em;
```

At 1440px, the visual result should land around 88–94px, **not** 130–160px.

Tablet 768–1279:

```css
font-size: clamp(56px, 7.7vw, 82px);
line-height: .92;
font-variation-settings: "wdth" 88, "wght" 500;
letter-spacing: -.042em;
```

Mobile <768:

```css
font-size: clamp(46px, 12.5vw, 64px);
line-height: .94;
font-variation-settings: "wdth" 90, "wght" 500;
letter-spacing: -.038em;
```

### Major H2

Desktop:

```css
font-size: clamp(48px, 4.8vw, 76px);
line-height: .96;
font-variation-settings: "wdth" 88, "wght" 500;
letter-spacing: -.04em;
```

Mobile:

```css
font-size: clamp(36px, 9.5vw, 52px);
line-height: 1;
```

### H3 / interaction title

- desktop 26–36px;
- mobile 24–30px;
- weight 500–550;
- line-height 1.05–1.15.

### Body

- primary marketing body: 17–20px desktop, 16–18px mobile;
- UI/form body: 15–17px;
- metadata/captions: 13–14px.

## 5.4 Type prohibitions

- no serif anywhere on public marketing/auth Pass 3;
- no 120–160px headline at 1440px;
- no ultra-tight `.82` line height;
- no giant heading consuming >55% of viewport height;
- no text opacity below WCAG-readable contrast just to create atmosphere;
- no dark-navy text on near-black;
- no headings positioned underneath active header controls;
- no decorative italics;
- no monospace as an aesthetic device;
- no eyebrow/kicker text above headings.

- inner visual stage is `100svh`;
- one master timeline;
- `start: "top top"`;
- `end: () => "+=" + window.innerHeight * 1.8` (tune within 1.6–2.0 after visual testing; do not exceed 2.2 without evidence);
- `pin: stage`;
- `pinSpacing: true`;
- `scrub: 0.35`;
- `anticipatePin: 1`;
- `invalidateOnRefresh: true`;
- no snap.

The following section must physically begin **after** the pin spacing. It may not enter under the pinned stage.

## 11.2 Persistent actor

Render one semantic/visual `ContextTrace` actor inside this stage.

Do not render separate copies of `EvidencePieces` in each state.

The actor contains real demo content in two representations:

### Raw representation

Use 4–5 short source lines resembling parsed professional background, for example:

- `BSc Computer Science — final semester`
- `Built web applications with JavaScript and React`
- `Worked through debugging, analysis and project delivery`
- `Interested in learning, product building and technology`

This is clearly a demonstration of how context can be structured. It is not claimed to be a real person's CV.

### Structured representation

The same information resolves into:

- Stage
- Field
- Skills
- Interests

Use the same DOM nodes where practical. Where separate elements are required, pair them with matching `data-flip-id` and use Flip only for the state change, not as decorative animation.

## 11.3 Context media

Use one media frame that can exchange content between:

- professional context;
- engineering context;
- optionally student context.

It is **not a horizontal carousel**.

At different scroll intervals, the same media frame changes source/crop while the context trace changes field assumptions. This is the product lesson: different work context leads to different questioning.

Image transitions:

- no crossfade longer than ~280ms;
- preferably use an overflow-hidden frame with a controlled incoming/outgoing translation of 8–14% plus opacity;
- do not stack several full images visibly at once;
- no parallax for decoration.

## 11.4 Exact copy

### Stage heading

`The questions should change when the context changes.`

### Supporting copy

`A student, recent graduate and working professional should not begin from the same assumptions. Field, skills, subjects and interests help shape what the assessment asks next.`

Do not repeat this heading after the next state enters.

## 11.5 Timeline states

Author these normalized states and inspect all intermediate compositions:

### 0.00–0.18 — raw context

- media + raw background excerpt visible;
- structured rows not yet dominant;
- heading readable.

### 0.18–0.42 — organization

- raw lines physically reorganize into structured Stage/Field/Skills/Interests positions;
- heading remains but reduces prominence;
- media source can exchange once to demonstrate different field context;
- no duplicate label cloud.

### 0.42–0.68 — question relevance

- only the structured fields relevant to the question remain visually close to the question area;
- question UI enters within the same stage;
- old heading exits before question heading becomes dominant.

### 0.68–0.90 — question

Question copy:

`When a project changes direction, what do you do first?`

Choices:

1. `Clarify the changed constraint, then test the revised path.`
2. `Gather input before choosing the next step.`

The demo may show a sample selected state as scroll advances, but clearly keep this a product demonstration and do not imply the visitor answered.

### 0.90–1.00 — handoff

- question settles;
- structured context condenses to a compact source block;
- stage prepares the analytical interpretation section;
- the stage fully unpins before the next section becomes visible.

## 11.6 Intermediate-state acceptance

At progress 0.00 / 0.25 / 0.50 / 0.75 / 1.00:

- there must be no text collision;
- no two major headings can occupy the same reading area;
- no body copy may sit under another scene's UI;
- no blank >35% viewport region caused by missing actor positioning;
- no element may be clipped unintentionally by the header;
- reversing from any point must reconstruct the previous state.

# 20. MOTION ARCHITECTURE — IMPLEMENTATION REQUIREMENTS

## 20.1 PublicMotionRoot

Refactor current motion root.

### Smoother scope

Create ScrollSmoother only when all are true:

- pathname is `/`;
- `(min-width: 1024px)`;
- `(pointer: fine)`;
- reduced motion is false.

Do not smooth internal marketing routes or auth.

### Smoother config starting point

```js
ScrollSmoother.create({
  wrapper: '#smooth-wrapper',
  content: '#smooth-content',
  smooth: 0.45,
  effects: false,
  smoothTouch: false,
  normalizeScroll: false,
});
```

Tune between 0.38 and 0.52 only after real browser testing. Do not exceed 0.55 without explicit visual evidence; the current experience already feels disconnected/slow.

### Lifecycle

- create smoother before homepage ScrollTriggers;
- expose `motionReady` only after smoother/native mode is established;
- wait for critical fonts/media layout, then one `ScrollTrigger.refresh()`;
- do **not** globally kill every ScrollTrigger in the application via `ScrollTrigger.getAll().forEach(...)`;
- own triggers via `gsap.context()` / `gsap.matchMedia()` and revert only what this public route created;
- kill the smoother instance on route exit;
- clean up listeners/RAF.

## 20.2 Home motion controller

Create one top-level controller for homepage scroll choreography.

Possible structure:

- `HomeNarrativeV3.jsx`
- `HomeMotionController` hook or effect inside it;
- child refs for Hero, ContextQuestionStage, Interpretation, Career, Development.

Do not attach unrelated ScrollTriggers in every child component.

## 20.3 Motion vocabulary

Use these primitives intentionally:

### Carry
The same context actor remains while position/structure changes.

### Exchange
One media source/representation becomes another in the same spatial role.

### Resolve
Complexity settles into a structured state.

### Inspect
Click/tap exposes a different lens/career.

### Release
A pinned stage relinquishes ownership fully before next scene starts.

Do not add decorative “reveal” motion to everything.

## 20.4 Scroll stress

The implementation is not complete until visually tested for:

- slow forward scroll;
- fast forward wheel/trackpad fling;
- slow reverse;
- fast reverse;
- small up/down oscillation near pin boundaries;
- resize at beginning/middle/end of a pin;
- reload at mid-scroll where browser restores scroll position;
- browser Back from an internal route;
- keyboard focus into controls near pinned scenes.

No state may leave orphaned opacity/transforms after interruption.

# 35. FINAL IMPLEMENTATION PRINCIPLE

Do not try to make Personality Assessor look like Oryzo, White Desert, Lando, Aether, Outfit or Osmo.

Use what those projects demonstrate at the engineering level:

- a clear subject;
- a small number of strong visual rules;
- purpose-built media;
- technology selected per actor;
- meaningful state continuity;
- responsive simplification;
- controlled typography;
- performance-aware asset production;
- motion that explains change rather than advertises itself.

For Personality Assessor, the authored experience must come specifically from:

**professional context becoming structured interpretation.**

If the result could be reskinned into an unrelated SaaS product by changing the copy and logo, the pass has failed.

If the result needs yellow, a giant serif, floating tags, or a random 3D object to feel designed, the pass has failed.

If the result feels calm and precise when still, and then becomes clearer rather than noisier when it moves, the implementation is moving in the correct direction.

# Personality Assessor — Codex Pass 2
## Marketing + Auth Art-Direction Reconstruction

**Status:** implementation specification — authoritative for this pass  
**Repository:** `analyticsmath/PersonalityAnalysis`  
**Local target:** the currently open local repository  
**Role:** Codex is implementation-only. Do not redesign, reinterpret, or rewrite the specification.  
**Scope:** public marketing pages + public chrome + login/signup + marketing media + public motion architecture.  
**Out of scope:** dashboard, assessment engine, scoring, CV parser, question-generation backend, authenticated result/dashboard UI, APIs, models, database, auth contracts.

---

# 0. Why this pass exists

Pass 1 is not to be polished incrementally. Its product truth and accessibility foundations are useful, but its art direction is too conventional for the target quality.

The following Pass 1 choices are explicitly retired:

- Vermilion/orange identity palette (`#C84A2D`).
- Instrument Sans as the dominant visual voice.
- A full-screen workplace photograph as the homepage protagonist.
- The five-photo `pa-work-rail` as the main narrative device.
- One single 480svh pinned slideshow-like journey.
- A white rectangular `Profile Plane` that remains essentially the same container while content changes.
- Fade/translate being the dominant scene-change language.
- Generic split-screen auth pages.
- Giant tightly tracked sans-serif headings as the default “premium” treatment.

The product truth remains unchanged:

**professional context → CV/manual-profile evidence → adaptive questions → Big Five/OCEAN + RIASEC + work values + career signals → explainable career relationships → development → progress.**

The new art direction must make that causal chain visible.

---

# 1. Governing creative thesis

## The Evidence Portrait

The website should feel as though professional evidence is being organized into something increasingly useful.

At the opening, the person is represented by fragments:

- current stage;
- field;
- skills;
- interests;
- CV/context;
- work/study imagery;
- question evidence.

Those fragments do **not** disappear and get replaced by unrelated sections. They progressively reorganize into structured context, then assessment, then multidimensional interpretation, then career/development direction.

The visitor should be able to understand the product from the transformations even before reading every paragraph.

**Do not create an AI brain, neural network, orb, particle face, glowing mesh, abstract 3D blob, cyber interface, or personality-logo object.**

---

# 2. Hard visual constraints

These are non-negotiable.

- No gradients anywhere.
- No blue/purple/cyan AI aesthetic.
- No beige, cream, ivory, or warm luxury off-white.
- No green-led premium palette.
- No differently colored phrase inside the hero headline.
- No eyebrow/kicker/pre-title text anywhere.
- No generic left-copy/right-image hero.
- No floating-card navbar.
- Header belongs to the opening composition.
- No decorative horizontal divider rules.
- No numbered editorial chapters (`01`, `02`, etc.) as visual decoration.
- No fake AI pills or labels such as “AI powered”, “Live”, “New”.
- No generic glassmorphism.
- No arbitrary WebGL object.
- No bounce, elastic, springy, or playful motion for marketing choreography.
- No scroll hijacking on touch devices.
- No design that depends on a GPU/WebGL context.
- No fake scientific accuracy, match percentages, or claims not present in product truth.
- Do not imply photographed people took the assessment, received a personality result, received a career match, or endorse the product.

# 3. Final typography system

Replace the current public typography system with **Source Serif 4 Variable + Source Sans 3 Variable**.

Both families are open-source and appropriate for production self-hosting. Use Fontsource variable packages so the repository owns the WOFF2 delivery instead of depending on Google Fonts at runtime.

## Required frontend dependencies

Add to `frontend/package.json`:

```json
"@fontsource-variable/source-sans-3": "5.3.0",
"@fontsource-variable/source-serif-4": "5.3.0"
```

Do not silently run a broad install if the environment is network constrained. If dependencies are absent locally, still edit `package.json` and source imports and report the exact install command required by the user.

Expected user command:

```powershell
npm install --prefix frontend @fontsource-variable/source-sans-3@5.3.0 @fontsource-variable/source-serif-4@5.3.0
```

## Imports

At the public frontend entry point used by all public/auth routes, import only what is required:

```js
import '@fontsource-variable/source-sans-3/wght.css';
import '@fontsource-variable/source-serif-4/full.css';
```

Do not import every language subset. Use the default Latin payload unless existing internationalization requires more.

## Font roles

### Source Serif 4 Variable
Use for:

- homepage hero H1;
- major interpretive statements;
- selected internal-page H1/H2 statements;
- career-resolution headline;
- trust quotation/statement;
- closing scene.

It represents **interpretation/human meaning**.

### Source Sans 3 Variable
Use for:

- navigation;
- brand wordmark;
- body copy;
- buttons;
- evidence fragments;
- question UI;
- data visualizations;
- labels;
- form UI;
- captions;
- numbers.

It represents **evidence/system/interaction**.

## Exact type tokens

```css
--pa-font-system: "Source Sans 3 Variable", "Segoe UI", Arial, sans-serif;
--pa-font-human: "Source Serif 4 Variable", Georgia, serif;

--pa-copy-xs: 0.8125rem;   /* 13 */
--pa-copy-sm: 0.9375rem;   /* 15 */
--pa-copy-md: 1.0625rem;   /* 17 */
--pa-copy-lg: 1.1875rem;   /* 19 */
```

### Hero H1

```css
font-size: clamp(4.5rem, 7.3vw, 7.75rem);
font-weight: 450;
font-optical-sizing: auto;
line-height: .91;
letter-spacing: -.038em;
```

# 4. Final color system

Retire the Pass 1 vermilion tokens.

Use a neutral editorial foundation with **signal yellow used as evidence annotation**, not as a full-site brand wash.

```css
--pa-ink: #0B0C0C;
--pa-paper: #F7F8F7;
--pa-white: #FFFFFF;
--pa-fog: #EEF1F0;
--pa-structure: #D9DEDC;
--pa-muted: #5C6461;
--pa-signal: #F0E84A;
--pa-signal-pressed: #D9D12F;
--pa-success: #0D7254;
--pa-warning: #8A6200;
--pa-danger: #A72A24;
```

## Rules

- `--pa-paper` is the default marketing background.
- `--pa-white` is used for local high-clarity surfaces/forms where needed.
- `--pa-ink` is the main text and one deliberate dark chapter.
- `--pa-signal` is an annotation/select/focus/highlight color only.
- Black text may sit on signal yellow.
- Do not use signal yellow as body text on white/paper.
- Primary CTA may remain ink/white instead of making every CTA yellow.
- Signal yellow can be used for selected question state, active lens marker, evidence highlight, focus indicator, small directional control, and one closing accent.
- Data dimensions are not rainbow-colored. Distinguish by hierarchy, shape, marker position, opacity, label, and layout.
- Semantic success/warning/error remain independent of brand/evidence color.

# 8. Public motion foundation

## Plugins

Use existing GSAP 3.15.0.

Required:

```js
import { gsap } from 'gsap';
import { ScrollTrigger } from 'gsap/ScrollTrigger';
import { ScrollSmoother } from 'gsap/ScrollSmoother';
import { Flip } from 'gsap/Flip';
```

Register once.

Do not add Lenis, Locomotive, another smooth-scroll package, or a custom RAF scroll engine.

## ScrollSmoother lifecycle fix

The current dynamic import can allow child ScrollTriggers to measure before ScrollSmoother exists. Replace that architecture.

Create a small public motion context, e.g.:

```text
PublicMotionProvider
  provides { motionReady, smoother, reducedMotion, finePointer }
```

Rules:

1. Public content renders immediately for accessibility/SEO.
2. On desktop/fine-pointer/non-reduced-motion, initialize ScrollSmoother first.
3. Only set `motionReady=true` after Smoother exists.
4. Homepage chapter ScrollTriggers must not initialize until `motionReady` is true.
5. On touch or reduced-motion, set `motionReady=true` without ScrollSmoother.
6. After fonts are ready (`document.fonts.ready`) and motion is ready, call one `ScrollTrigger.refresh()`.
7. Kill/revert on route change/unmount.

Desktop smoother:

```js
ScrollSmoother.create({
  wrapper: '#smooth-wrapper',
  content: '#smooth-content',
  smooth: 0.62,
  effects: false,
  smoothTouch: false,
  normalizeScroll: false,
});
```

The purpose is controlled catch-up, not floaty lag.

## Responsive motion API

Use `gsap.matchMedia()` rather than one-time `window.innerWidth` branches.

Conditions should include:

```js
{
  desktop: '(min-width: 1024px) and (pointer: fine)',
  tablet: '(min-width: 768px) and (max-width: 1023px)',
  mobile: '(max-width: 767px)',
  reduceMotion: '(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)'
}
```

Do not create desktop pins when `reduceMotion` is true.

## Motion rules

Allowed primary easing:

- `power2.inOut`
- `power3.out`
- `sine.inOut`
- `none` for direct scrubbed positional relationships.

Do not use:

- elastic;
- bounce;
- back overshoot;
- springy card behavior.

All major scroll transformations must be reversible.

Intermediate progress must remain compositionally valid. Do not build an effect that only looks correct at 0% and 100%.
