# 11. Context + evidence assembly chapter

## Purpose

Show that different professional contexts should not produce the same generic assessment.

## Exact chapter copy

H2:

```text
Different work should lead to different questions.
```

Body:

```text
A student, a recent graduate and an experienced professional should not begin from the same assumptions. Field, skills, subjects and interests help shape what comes next.
```

## Desktop choreography

Create one focused chapter around `260–300svh` with a sticky 100svh canvas.

### Phase A — 0% to 34%

- Incoming context photography crosses horizontally behind/around the evidence field.
- Do **not** recreate the old five-card rail.
- Use 3 main media actors with different sizes and vertical positions.
- Suggested order: student → engineering → professional/documents.
- Approx widths: 54vw, 42vw, 48vw.
- Approx heights: 68vh, 52vh, 61vh.
- Keep 8–12vw negative space between major media so the composition breathes.
- The track moves using direct scrub, no snap.
- Captions should sit beside/below each media and identify context (`Student`, `Engineering`, `Professional`) without numbered labels.

### Phase B — 34% to 70%

- Photography recedes in scale/opacity but does not pop away.
- The persistent evidence fragments from the opening move toward meaningful groups.
- `Graduate` becomes the stage/context anchor.
- `Software / systems` becomes field.
- `Problem solving · JavaScript · Analysis` become skills.
- `Learning · Product building · Technology` become interests.
- The transformation should be accomplished with the **same DOM actors whenever practical**, not by cross-fading duplicates.

### Phase C — 70% to 100%

The grouped evidence resolves into a structured context composition occupying roughly 58–70% of the viewport width.

It must **not** be a white card.

Use typography, spacing and background contrast to create hierarchy.

Exact supporting statement:

```text
Context is the starting point, not the result.
```

Keep the resolved context visible into the next scene for continuity.

# 20. Mobile homepage choreography

Desktop spectacle must not be mechanically stacked.

## Context media

Use native horizontal scroll only if the context images remain useful on mobile.

If horizontal:

No 200+svh mobile pin.

## Lenses

Tap controls + stable visualization region.

No automatic horizontal scroll of data labels.

## Career

Stack comparison semantically:

user profile → career model → why it relates → development difference.

Maintain clear reading order.

# 21. Reduced motion

When `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`:

- no ScrollSmoother;
- no pinned scrub chapters;
- no large horizontal auto movement;
- no scale-based cinematic media motion;
- show the same semantic states in normal document order;
- evidence appears already grouped by the time its chapter begins;
- lens changes can crossfade instantly or use ≤120ms opacity;
- focus/hover state changes remain;
- all information remains available.

Reduced motion is a designed composition, not `animation-duration: .01ms`.

---

# 22. Interaction states

## Buttons

Primary CTA default:

- ink background;
- white text;
- 46px minimum height;
- small radius 2–4px.

Hover:

- no bounce;
- translate Y maximum -1px;
- background may move toward graphite;
- duration 160–200ms.

Signal-yellow buttons should be rare and use ink text.

## Links

Avoid default decorative animated underline sweeps across every link.

Use clear text color/opacity changes and visible focus state.

## Lens/career selectors

- `aria-pressed`;
- selected state uses both color and another cue (position, weight, marker, background).

# 25. Performance requirements

Targets:

- LCP ≤ 2.5s at p75;
- INP ≤ 200ms at p75;
- CLS ≤ 0.1 at p75.

Implementation rules:

- only the opening critical image eager/high priority;
- no eager-loading the entire context stream;
- declare image dimensions;
- use existing responsive `<picture>` primitive or improve it without breaking contracts;
- transform/opacity for high-frequency motion;
- avoid animating layout properties continuously during scrub where transform can represent the same movement;
- `will-change` only on actors actively participating in motion, not globally;
- remove `will-change` after expensive temporary transitions when practical;
- do not add canvas/WebGL cost;
- do not animate filter blur continuously;
- do not preload every font file/weight.

- `aria-pressed` where appropriate;
- DOM/text equivalents for visual data;
- 44×44px preferred interactive targets;
- no meaning by color alone;
- logical DOM reading order independent of visual positioning;
- reduced-motion variant;
- captions/alt text that describe work context without implying endorsement or assessment outcome.

Decorative evidence actors that duplicate nearby text should be `aria-hidden="true"` to avoid screen-reader repetition.

# D. TECHNICAL IMPLEMENTATION CONTRACT

## D1 — Motion ownership

- The public homepage must have one clear motion conductor.
- Do not scatter page-wide independent `ScrollTrigger` instances across individual atoms.
- Route/unmount cleanup is mandatory.
- Use `gsap.context()` or an equivalent scoped cleanup strategy.
- Do not use Barba to take over React Router navigation.
- Existing React Router + React lifecycle remain authoritative.

## D2 — Smooth scroll eligibility

Enable the specified smooth-scrolling treatment only when all of these are true:

- public marketing route where the specification permits it
- viewport at least 1024px
- fine pointer
- reduced motion is **not** requested

Do not enable it for auth pages, touch-only mobile devices, or reduced-motion mode.

If ScrollSmoother is not actually importable from the installed GSAP package in this local project, do not install another package. Use native scrolling plus the master ScrollTrigger sequence and report `ScrollSmoother unavailable in local GSAP distribution` as a deviation. Do not build a homemade smooth-scroll hijacker.

## D3 — Responsive architecture

Use semantic breakpoints and CSS that supports at least:

- large desktop: 1440–1920
- laptop: 1280/1366
- tablet: approximately 768–1023
- mobile: 360–767

The exact optical layout must remain fluid between those ranges. Do not hard-code the experience only for 1440×900.

## D4 — Performance

- Hero must be an intentional LCP candidate and stay eager/high-priority.
- Below-fold media lazy-loads.
- Do not preload the entire media rail.
- Keep transforms/opacity as the main animation properties.
- Avoid animating layout properties continuously where transforms can represent the same state.
- Avoid unnecessary React re-renders on scroll; animation progress should live in GSAP/DOM rather than React state when possible.
- Keep `will-change` scoped and temporary/limited.

## D5 — Accessibility

- Preserve semantic headings/order even though visual layers overlap.
- Interactive demo controls must be keyboard focusable.
- Drag/swipe content must also have Previous/Next or direct controls.
- Mobile menu must lock background scroll, support Escape and restore focus.
- Reduced-motion users receive the alternate composition, not the same sequence at 0.01ms.
- Do not rely on color alone to communicate selected/status state.
- Minimum preferred interactive target is 44×44px; menu trigger 48×48px.

## 0. Authority and operating rule

This document is the design authority for the first implementation pass. Codex is the implementation agent, not the art director. If an instruction conflicts with current code or creates a technical impossibility, Codex must report the conflict rather than silently redesign, rewrite copy, substitute a template pattern, remove behavior, or invent new visual language.

The redesign preserves verified product functionality and public-route behavior while replacing the current public visual architecture. Backend contracts, authentication behavior, protected routes, assessment logic, scoring logic and data models are out of scope for this pass unless a frontend integration bug makes a minimal compatibility change strictly necessary.

### Evidence labels used in this document

- **VERIFIED PRODUCT TRUTH** — directly confirmed in the current repository.
- **DESIGN LOCK** — final creative/UX decision for implementation.
- **LIVE-QA PENDING** — implementation value is specified, but final optical tuning must be checked in the rendered browser because pixel-level source imagery/real font rendering cannot be perfectly judged from repository metadata alone.

# 1. Verified product truth that the marketing experience must communicate

## 1.1 Core journey

**VERIFIED PRODUCT TRUTH**

The current product supports this chain:

1. Account creation / sign in.
2. User chooses professional state: Student, Graduate, or Professional.
3. User supplies professional context through CV upload or manual profile entry.
4. CV/profile information is analyzed into structured professional context.
5. The adaptive assessment is built around that context.
6. Normal question target is 22, with extension possible up to 26.
7. Questions can use MCQ, Likert, slider/scale and text interaction forms.
8. Result generation includes Big Five / OCEAN, RIASEC, work values, career signals, confidence/evidence information and career intelligence.
9. Career comparison uses a curated catalog of 17 roles and exposes reasons, differences/gaps and roadmap-oriented development.
10. The product stores assessment history and supports longitudinal analytics/progress.

## 1.2 AI position

**VERIFIED PRODUCT TRUTH**

AI can participate in CV intelligence, adaptive question generation and written/narrative assistance when configured. Core scoring is not a free-form model opinion: structured scoring and deterministic career logic remain foundational. Adaptive question generation includes deterministic/contextual fallbacks when the AI service is unavailable.

**DESIGN LOCK — public wording:**

> AI helps adapt questions to your professional context and can support written interpretation. Core assessment scores are calculated through structured scoring logic.

Do not advertise OpenAI, Groq, a particular model, or “machine learning prediction” in headline marketing. Provider names are infrastructure, not the user proposition. Do not claim clinically validated, scientifically proven career prediction, guaranteed employability, diagnostic validity, or a numerical accuracy percentage.

## 1.3 Scientific framing

**DESIGN LOCK**

Permitted language:

- “Built around established personality and vocational frameworks.”
- “Big Five / OCEAN.”
- “RIASEC vocational interests.”
- “Continuous dimensions rather than a single personality box.”
- “Professional reflection and career exploration.”

Prohibited without a future validation study:

- “Clinically validated.”
- “Scientifically proves your ideal career.”
- “98% accurate.”
- “Predicts career success.”
- “Diagnoses personality or mental health.”

---

# 2. Final brand / experience concept

## 2.1 Creative concept: **The Portrait in Motion**

**DESIGN LOCK**

The persistent protagonist is not a literal face, avatar, brain, neural-network sphere or AI object. It is the user’s **professional evidence becoming legible**.

At the beginning, professional identity is unresolved:

- field
- education
- skills
- projects
- experience
- interests
- work context

As the story progresses, the same evidence changes state:

**work context → structured evidence → adaptive question → multidimensional profile → career relationship → development direction**

The page must feel like one idea transforming, not a collection of independent sections.

## 2.2 Emotional target

The experience should feel:

- intelligent
- composed
- human
- analytical without being clinical
- confident without claiming certainty
- premium without luxury clichés
- technological without looking like an “AI template”

It must not feel:

- mystical
- horoscope-like
- cyberpunk
- HR surveillance-like
- therapy-like
- generic SaaS
- purple/blue AI
- stock-market dashboard-like

## 2.3 Visual ownership test

If “Personality Assessor” is replaced with a random SaaS name and the page still makes complete sense, the design has failed. Every major visual state must derive from one of these product-specific truths:

- professional context
- CV/profile evidence
- adaptive questioning
- multidimensional interpretation
- explainable career relationship
- development over time

---

# 3. Hard visual rules for this implementation

1. No gradients anywhere.
2. No ivory, cream, beige, warm luxury off-white.
3. No purple/blue/cyan AI aesthetic.
4. No eyebrow/kicker text anywhere.
5. No visible editorial scene numbering (`01`, `02`, etc.).
6. No decorative horizontal hairlines/dividers as a visual motif.
7. No split-color hero headline.
8. No left-copy/right-image hero.
9. No floating rounded navbar capsule.
10. No “AI Powered”, “Live”, “New”, or similar decorative badges/pills.
11. No generic glassmorphism.
12. No random orb/blob/particle-brain WebGL.
13. No default card grid for the homepage narrative.
14. No bounce/pop entrance motion.
15. No hard scroll snap.
16. No theatrical blocking loader.
17. No invented user testimonials or metrics.
18. Do not imply photographed people used the assessment or received a specific personality/career result.
19. Do not put every technique on every page. Cinematic motion belongs to storytelling; auth/forms remain direct.

# 4. Final color system

**DESIGN LOCK**

```css
--pa-ink: #0B0C0D;
--pa-graphite: #17191A;
--pa-paper: #FFFFFF;
--pa-cool-1: #E6EAE8;
--pa-cool-2: #D9DEDC;
--pa-muted: #5D6461;
--pa-accent: #C84A2D;
--pa-accent-hover: #A63820;
--pa-accent-on-dark: #F07A59;
--pa-success: #147A5B;
--pa-warning: #9A6700;
--pa-danger: #B42318;
```

### Usage rules

- Main light background = pure white `#FFFFFF`.
- Supporting light chapter = visibly cool gray `#E6EAE8`, never warm off-white.
- Dark chapter = `#0B0C0D` or `#17191A`.
- Accent = vermilion `#C84A2D`; use sparingly for active state, action, current evidence, focus emphasis and small identity gestures.
- Do **not** make the site “orange.” Aim for roughly 5–10% accent occupancy in a typical viewport.
- On dark surfaces, small accent text uses `#F07A59`, not `#C84A2D`.
- Semantic success/warning/error colors are separate from brand accent.
- OCEAN/RIASEC are not rendered as a rainbow. Use neutral geometry plus one controlled accent to show active/selected values.

### Contrast intent

- Ink on white and ink on cool gray must be the default reading combination.
- Muted body text `#5D6461` is allowed on white; do not use it as small text on dark.
- White text on `#C84A2D` is permitted for button text.
- Focus rings must remain obvious on both light and dark scenes.

# 5. Final typography system

## 5.1 Families

**DESIGN LOCK**

### Primary: Instrument Sans Variable
Use for:

- brand wordmark
- navigation
- hero/display headings
- section headings
- UI labels
- buttons
- data labels
- numbers

Reason: the existing project already uses Instrument Sans; the variable width axis gives us authorship through proportion rather than fake “premium” ultra-bold weight.

### Secondary: Newsreader Variable
Use only for:

- interpretive pull statements
- human explanatory moments
- one or two reflective sentences per long marketing page

Do not use it for navigation, buttons, forms, data, small labels, or every section heading.

### Font delivery

- Remove Google Fonts `@import` from public CSS.
- Self-host WOFF2 variable font assets in the project, using the upstream OFL-licensed families.
- Preload only the critical Instrument Sans file used above the fold.
- Do not preload Newsreader unless browser profiling proves it is used in the first viewport.
- Set explicit fallback stacks and avoid layout shift from late font replacement.

## 5.2 Type tokens

```css
--pa-font-sans: "Instrument Sans", Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif;
--pa-font-serif: "Newsreader", Georgia, serif;
```

### Hero H1

Desktop ≥ 1280:

- `font-family: var(--pa-font-sans)`
- `font-weight: 500`
- `font-variation-settings: "wdth" 82`
- `font-size: clamp(88px, 10.3vw, 164px)`
- `line-height: 0.82`
- `letter-spacing: -0.072em`
- sentence case
- no terminal punctuation

Tablet 768–1279:

- `font-size: clamp(68px, 10.8vw, 112px)`
- width axis 84
- line-height .84

Mobile < 768:

- `font-size: clamp(54px, 15vw, 78px)`
- width axis 86
- `line-height: .86`
- `letter-spacing: -.055em`

### Major marketing H2

Desktop:

- 72–116 px depending scene
- weight 480–520
- width axis 84–90
- line-height .86–.96
- tracking −.055em to −.07em

Mobile:

- 42–62 px
- line-height .92–1.0
- tracking −.04em

### H3 / state title

- desktop 30–44 px
- mobile 28–36 px
- weight 500
- line-height 1.02–1.12

### Body

- desktop 18 px / 1.55
- large interpretive paragraph 20–22 px / 1.45
- mobile 16–17 px / 1.55
- ideal line length 42–58 characters; hard maximum about 66 characters

### Navigation / controls

- nav 14 px / 1
- buttons 14 px / 1
- weight 500
- no uppercase transformation

### Newsreader pull statement

- desktop 40–56 px / 1.05
- mobile 30–38 px / 1.12
- weight 400
- optional italic only when the copy itself is reflective, never as decoration

### Numerals

Use tabular figures for live data/result examples where alignment matters.

# 6. Layout system

## 6.1 Global grid

**DESIGN LOCK**

- Desktop ≥ 1280: 12-column grid.
- Tablet 768–1279: 8-column grid.
- Mobile < 768: 4-column grid.
- Desktop outer inset: 48 px at 1280–1599; 64 px ≥ 1600.
- Tablet inset: 32 px.
- Mobile inset: 20 px.
- Desktop column gap: 24 px.
- Tablet gap: 18 px.
- Mobile gap: 12 px.
- No generic centered `max-width: 1200px` shell for cinematic scenes; full-width compositions may use the grid directly.
- Reading copy should still use controlled measures.

## 6.2 Spacing rhythm

Base spacing set:

`4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 80, 96, 128, 160`

Do not invent random 37/53/91 px spacing unless optical browser QA justifies it.

## 6.3 Radius

- Marketing buttons and functional surfaces: 2–4 px maximum.
- Inputs: 2 px.
- Do not use 18–32 px “friendly SaaS” radius.
- Circular controls allowed only where their function is intrinsically circular (e.g. previous/next arrow icon button).

2. One long authored “portrait journey” stage driven by vertical scroll, with controlled horizontal media movement and five semantic states.
3. Quiet trust chapter.
4. Final CTA/brand resolution with footer integrated into the same dark world.

The DOM should still contain sensible semantic sections/headings even though the visual experience reads as a continuous transformation.

## Scene H0 — Hero / professional context

### Exact copy

**H1**

`Your work`  
`has a pattern`

**Body**

`Add your CV or enter your background, then answer questions shaped around your field. Personality Assessor turns that evidence into a clearer picture of personality and career direction.`

**Primary CTA**

`Build my profile`

**Secondary CTA**

`See how it works`

### Composition at 1440×900

- hero = 100svh, minimum 680 px
- background image = work-02 full bleed
- H1 x = 48 px; visual baseline in lower-left two-thirds
- H1 max width ≈ 1160 px
- first line begins around 47–52% of viewport height depending optical crop
- body block sits in lower-right quadrant, width 360–410 px
- primary + secondary actions sit below body with 12 px gap; buttons must never cover photographic focal content
- no separate label above H1

### Entry motion

No blocking loader.

On first paint (when reduced motion is off):

- hero image: scale 1.025 → 1.0 over 1.35 s, `power3.out`
- H1 line 1 mask reveal: 0.85 s
- H1 line 2 mask reveal starts 0.10 s after line 1
- body + CTAs: opacity 0 → 1 and y 18 → 0 over 0.70 s, start after 0.22 s
- header: opacity 0 → 1 over 0.55 s

Do not split words into individual characters.

### Scroll handoff

From roughly 58% to 100% of hero scroll progress:

- H1 y: 0 → `-6vh`
- H1 opacity: 1 → 0.14
- body/CTA opacity: 1 → 0
- image scale remains nearly stable (maximum additional scale +1.5%)
- the first work-world image rail begins entering from below/right before hero text is fully gone

The next scene must visibly begin before the hero fully disappears.

# 10. Portrait Journey — one master pinned stage

## 10.1 Engineering geometry

Desktop/pointer-rich only (`min-width: 1024px` and `pointer:fine`):

- stage height in layout: trigger controls approximately `4.8 × viewportHeight` of scroll distance
- inner visual stage pins at 100svh
- no snap
- `scrub: 0.78`
- `anticipatePin: 1`
- `invalidateOnRefresh: true`
- one master GSAP timeline; do not create independent ScrollTriggers for every child
- scroll-driven master timeline uses `ease: "none"`; child transitions may use restrained `power2.inOut` interpolation where it does not break reversible progress logic

Approximate normalized state anchors:

- 0.00 — Work / evidence enters
- 0.18 — CV/profile context resolves
- 0.37 — Adaptive question
- 0.56 — Four analytical lenses
- 0.76 — Career relationship
- 0.91 — Development state
- 1.00 — Trust handoff

Each transition must overlap by approximately 6–10% of total normalized progress. Never allow a blank stage.

## 10.2 Persistent actor: Profile Plane

A single semantic visual object changes function through the sequence.

### State A

Looks like a tall professional evidence/document field — white plane, square-ish corners, real typographic fragments, no fake glass.

### State B

Document fragments reorganize into structured context: field, skills, subjects/interests. The plane becomes less document-like and more analytical.

### State C

A question occupies the same spatial footprint. The prior evidence remains faintly legible behind/around it so the causal relationship is visible.

### State D

The question answer resolves into profile geometry representing distinct analytical lenses.

### State E

Profile geometry becomes career comparison evidence.

### State F

The visible mismatch/gap becomes next-step development content.

No WebGL is required. Build with semantic HTML, SVG where useful, CSS transforms and GSAP.

---

## State A — Work-world rail / context

### Heading

`Start with the work you’ve already done`

### Body

`A CV or manual profile gives the assessment context: your field, experience, subjects, skills and interests.`

### Media behavior

The five-image work-world rail moves behind the Profile Plane from right to left during the first ~20% of the master timeline.

Desktop image geometry:

- each image width 24–30vw
- height 48–66vh, intentionally varied within that range
- gap 16 px
- no card borders
- no rounded containers
- caption sits directly below image, 14 px, muted/ink depending background
- rail translates approximately 120–145vw over its active interval
- translation is linear with scroll; no auto-loop

The rail exists to show that professional context differs, not to show a portfolio gallery.

---

## State B — CV/profile interpretation

### Heading

`Turn background into assessment context`

### Body

`The system identifies useful professional signals before the assessment begins. You stay able to review the detected context before moving on.`

### Profile Plane content demonstration

Use neutral demonstration fields, not the photographed person’s identity:

- `Field` → `Software / systems`
- `Skills` → `Problem solving · JavaScript · Analysis`
- `Interests` → `Learning · Product building · Technology`

Include a visible label `Demonstration profile` in normal text, not a pill or eyebrow.

Do not claim the current marketing demo shows full raw CV text. The protected onboarding currently exposes detected profile data, while a fuller parsed-text experience belongs to the later authenticated-product redesign.

---

## State C — Adaptive question

### Heading

`The questions change with the context`

### Body

`A student, a recent graduate and an experienced professional should not receive an identical assessment. Your profile helps determine what the system asks next.`

### Demo question

`When a project changes direction, what do you do first?`

Visible answer examples:

- `Clarify the changed constraint, then test the revised path.`
- `Gather input before choosing the next step.`

These are demonstration controls. They can be clickable for microinteraction but must not pretend to calculate a real result.

### Interaction motion

- answer hover/focus: 180–220 ms; background/ink change + maximum 1 px y shift
- selected answer: accent indicator through fill/text state, not a pill outline
- question change in scroll sequence: outgoing prompt shifts x `-6vw`, fades to .15; incoming analytical geometry starts before prompt fully leaves

---

## State D — analytical lenses

### Heading

`More than one way to read a profile`

### Body

`Personality, vocational interests, work values and career signals stay distinct so you can see where each reading comes from.`

### Lens controls

Text buttons only:

- `Big Five / OCEAN`
- `RIASEC`
- `Work values`
- `Career signals`

No pills. Active item uses accent color + weight/opacity change. No decorative underline required.

### Exact explanatory copy

**Big Five / OCEAN**  
`Five continuous personality dimensions: Openness, Conscientiousness, Extraversion, Agreeableness and Neuroticism.`

**RIASEC**  
`Six vocational interest dimensions: Realistic, Investigative, Artistic, Social, Enterprising and Conventional.`

**Work values**  
`What matters in the conditions and rewards of work, including growth, independence, security and other value dimensions.`

**Career signals**  
`Professional evidence such as problem solving, learning orientation, technical depth and leadership.`

### Visualization rules

- OCEAN: five horizontal data scales, neutral track + accent value; these are functional data marks, not decorative dividers.
- RIASEC: one six-axis radial/radar-like SVG with neutral structure and accent profile shape; no rainbow.
- Work Values: eight ranked typographic/value rows; no equal card tiles.
- Career Signals: four vector bars/columns with large numeric values from `marketingDemo` demonstration data.
- every visualization includes accessible text equivalents or list content in DOM.

---

## State E — career relationship

### Heading

`A career match should show its reasoning`

### Body

`Compare your current profile with curated career models. See where the relationship is strong, where it differs and what could move you closer.`

### Demo content

Career: `Software Engineer`  
Relationship: `Strong alignment`

`Why it relates`  
`Technical depth, problem solving and learning orientation are close to this curated model.`

`Development difference`  
`Build more evidence of production delivery.`

Footer disclosure inside demo, normal body text:

`This is a product demonstration. Career alignment is guidance for exploration, not a hiring recommendation or employment guarantee.`

### CTA

`Explore career intelligence`

### Visual transition

The profile lens geometry does not disappear and a new card enter. Instead, its same values stretch/reposition into a two-sided relationship/comparison composition. Career title becomes large typographic architecture behind/adjacent to the comparison.

---

## State F — development

### Heading

`A gap is useful when it becomes a next step`

### Body

`Turn a difference into deliberate work, then return later with new evidence and see what changed.`

### Demo roadmap copy

`Evidence gap`  
`Applied research practice`

`Deliberate work`  
`Complete one observed research cycle`

`Carry forward`  
`Record the outcome in your next assessment`

Do not number these steps visually. Let each item replace/recompose the prior state across horizontal space.

### CTA

`See how progress works`

# 15. Global motion system

## 15.1 Motion philosophy

- motion explains state change
- scroll-linked motion is reversible
- stillness is deliberate
- no bounce
- no cheap “everything fades up” system
- no scroll hijacking
- no touch smoothing that disconnects content from the finger

## 15.2 Technology lock

Use current `gsap` dependency. Import/register:

- `ScrollTrigger`
- `ScrollSmoother`

Do not add Lenis, Locomotive Scroll or another global smooth-scroll library.

Framer Motion may remain for existing route/auth transitions where useful; do not orchestrate the same DOM node simultaneously with Framer and GSAP.

Do not introduce Three.js/R3F for the marketing redesign.

## 15.3 Desktop smooth scrolling

Only public marketing routes, not login/signup or protected app:

```js
ScrollSmoother.create({
  wrapper: '#smooth-wrapper',
  content: '#smooth-content',
  smooth: 0.78,
  effects: false,
  smoothTouch: false,
});
```

Rules:

- create smoother before page ScrollTriggers
- preserve native browser scrollbar
- do not use `normalizeScroll` initially
- fixed header stays outside the smoother content wrapper
- kill/recreate appropriately on route lifecycle
- if `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, do not instantiate ScrollSmoother
- if `pointer: coarse`, do not instantiate ScrollSmoother

## 15.4 GSAP React lifecycle

Every scene-level GSAP module must use `gsap.context()` (or official React `useGSAP` if Codex chooses to add that small official package) and revert/kill on unmount.

Never leave stale ScrollTriggers between route transitions.

Call `ScrollTrigger.refresh()` after:

- critical font readiness
- hero image load if dimensions/crop changed
- meaningful responsive layout change

Do not refresh continuously during scroll.

## 15.5 Motion timing tokens

```js
const motion = {
  fast: 0.20,
  ui: 0.26,
  reveal: 0.62,
  scene: 0.90,
  hero: 1.35,
  smoothScrollCatchup: 0.78,
};
```

Eases:

- UI hover/focus: `power2.out`
- ordinary reveal: `power3.out`
- controlled scene interpolation: `power2.inOut`
- master scroll timeline: `none`

No `back`, `bounce`, `elastic` eases in marketing/auth.

## 15.6 Hover

- link/CTA reaction 180–260 ms
- maximum translateY: 1–2 px
- no scale > 1.015 on buttons
- image hover, where used: scale max 1.025 over 650–900 ms
- no cursor-following magnetic button unless later browser testing proves it adds real value; first pass excludes it

---

# 16. Mobile choreography

## 16.1 General

Mobile is not the desktop pinned sequence collapsed into a column.

Below 1024 px:

- remove global ScrollSmoother
- remove pinned 4.8vh journey
- use native scrolling
- transform the five journey states into a continuous vertical story
- each state retains the same persistent Profile Plane concept through shared layout/state transitions, but movement distances are smaller

## 16.2 Hero

- 100svh, min-height 620 px
- H1 in upper/lower composition based on source focal crop; baseline implementation uses lower-left with 20 px inset
- body and CTAs move beneath heading with no overlay collision
- use object-position derived from desktop but allow media query adjustment up to ±12 percentage points
- no automatic image zoom beyond 1.01 on mobile

## 16.3 Work-world rail

Mobile uses native `overflow-x:auto` + `scroll-snap-type:x mandatory` because this is browser-native scrolling, not a custom drag dependency.

Still provide `Previous` and `Next` icon/text controls at ≥44×44 px so the gallery is operable without a dragging gesture.

- image width: 78vw
- max height: 58svh
- gap: 12 px
- scroll padding: 20 px

## 16.4 Lens control

- four text controls wrap into two rows if needed
- min target 44 px high
- selected state communicated by text + color/weight, never color only
- visualization appears below controls

## 16.5 Auth

- no fixed 50/50 split
- 28–34svh media opening
- H1 bridges media/paper world
- form controls min-height 48 px
- bottom padding includes safe-area inset where supported

---

# 17. Reduced-motion composition

When `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`:

1. Disable ScrollSmoother.
2. Disable pinned/horizontal scrub choreography.
3. Render all homepage semantic states in a normal vertical document.
4. Preserve Profile Plane in its resolved/static state for each chapter.
5. Remove large-scale panning, zooming and cross-screen translations.
6. Allow only short opacity/color transitions ≤150 ms where needed to communicate interaction state.
7. No auto-moving image rail. It becomes a native horizontal gallery or static vertical media sequence.
8. Header scene color changes may remain because they are necessary for readability, but use near-instant transitions.

Reduced motion must still feel designed, not like the CSS failed to load.

---

# 18. Accessibility acceptance requirements

Target WCAG 2.2 AA behavior for redesigned public/auth surfaces.

- Skip link remains.
- Every page has one logical H1.
- Heading hierarchy is semantic; typography size does not dictate HTML level.
- Visible labels on all auth fields.
- Errors are textual and use appropriate live regions.
- Do not block paste in password/email fields.
- Preserve browser/password manager autocomplete attributes.
- Focus indicator minimum 3 px visual ring or equivalent, never removed.
- Header/mobile menu restores focus on close.
- All custom interactive controls keyboard operable.
- If any interaction uses drag, provide single-pointer previous/next controls.
- Our own target standard: 44×44 px minimum even though WCAG 2.2’s AA minimum can be smaller in allowed cases.
- Do not use color alone to communicate selected/error/success state.
- Decorative repeated images use empty alt; meaningful images use descriptive alt.
- Data visualizations expose textual equivalents in DOM.
- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- No flashing/flicker effects.

---

# 19. Performance acceptance requirements

Targets for field-quality UX:

- LCP ≤ 2.5 s at 75th percentile
- INP ≤ 200 ms at 75th percentile
- CLS ≤ 0.1 at 75th percentile

Implementation constraints:

- hero/LCP image eager + high priority
- no lazy loading above-the-fold hero
- all below-fold media lazy by default
- preserve width/height
- WebP responsive sources remain
- no WebGL dependency
- no autoplay background video in first pass
- one major GSAP timeline for the long journey, not hundreds of triggers
- transform/opacity as primary animated properties
- avoid animating width/height/top/left continuously during scroll
- `will-change` only on elements actively animated; remove/avoid global blanket use
- font files WOFF2; minimize number of files and preload only critical Instrument Sans
- no route-blocking loader
- defer noncritical marketing visualization code if bundle analysis shows it affects initial load materially

# Personality Assessor — Final Marketing & Authentication Pre‑Production Master Specification

**Status:** DESIGN LOCK / READY FOR CODEX IMPLEMENTATION  
**Scope:** Public marketing site + public authentication entry pages only. Protected dashboard, assessment, results and analytics UI are explicitly deferred to the next design phase.  
**Repository:** `analyticsmath/PersonalityAnalysis`  
**Canonical product name:** Personality Assessor

---

## 0. Authority and operating rule

This document is the design authority for the first implementation pass. Codex is the implementation agent, not the art director. If an instruction conflicts with current code or creates a technical impossibility, Codex must report the conflict rather than silently redesign, rewrite copy, substitute a template pattern, remove behavior, or invent new visual language.

The redesign preserves verified product functionality and public-route behavior while replacing the current public visual architecture. Backend contracts, authentication behavior, protected routes, assessment logic, scoring logic and data models are out of scope for this pass unless a frontend integration bug makes a minimal compatibility change strictly necessary.

### Evidence labels used in this document

- **VERIFIED PRODUCT TRUTH** — directly confirmed in the current repository.
- **DESIGN LOCK** — final creative/UX decision for implementation.
- **LIVE-QA PENDING** — implementation value is specified, but final optical tuning must be checked in the rendered browser because pixel-level source imagery/real font rendering cannot be perfectly judged from repository metadata alone.

---

# 1. Verified product truth that the marketing experience must communicate

## 1.1 Core journey

**VERIFIED PRODUCT TRUTH**

The current product supports this chain:

1. Account creation / sign in.
2. User chooses professional state: Student, Graduate, or Professional.
3. User supplies professional context through CV upload or manual profile entry.
4. CV/profile information is analyzed into structured professional context.
5. The adaptive assessment is built around that context.
6. Normal question target is 22, with extension possible up to 26.
7. Questions can use MCQ, Likert, slider/scale and text interaction forms.
8. Result generation includes Big Five / OCEAN, RIASEC, work values, career signals, confidence/evidence information and career intelligence.
9. Career comparison uses a curated catalog of 17 roles and exposes reasons, differences/gaps and roadmap-oriented development.
10. The product stores assessment history and supports longitudinal analytics/progress.

## 1.2 AI position

**VERIFIED PRODUCT TRUTH**

AI can participate in CV intelligence, adaptive question generation and written/narrative assistance when configured. Core scoring is not a free-form model opinion: structured scoring and deterministic career logic remain foundational. Adaptive question generation includes deterministic/contextual fallbacks when the AI service is unavailable.

**DESIGN LOCK — public wording:**

> AI helps adapt questions to your professional context and can support written interpretation. Core assessment scores are calculated through structured scoring logic.

Do not advertise OpenAI, Groq, a particular model, or “machine learning prediction” in headline marketing. Provider names are infrastructure, not the user proposition. Do not claim clinically validated, scientifically proven career prediction, guaranteed employability, diagnostic validity, or a numerical accuracy percentage.

## 1.3 Scientific framing

**DESIGN LOCK**

Permitted language:

- “Built around established personality and vocational frameworks.”
- “Big Five / OCEAN.”
- “RIASEC vocational interests.”
- “Continuous dimensions rather than a single personality box.”
- “Professional reflection and career exploration.”

Prohibited without a future validation study:

- “Clinically validated.”
- “Scientifically proves your ideal career.”
- “98% accurate.”
- “Predicts career success.”
- “Diagnoses personality or mental health.”

---

# 2. Final brand / experience concept

## 2.1 Creative concept: **The Portrait in Motion**

**DESIGN LOCK**

The persistent protagonist is not a literal face, avatar, brain, neural-network sphere or AI object. It is the user’s **professional evidence becoming legible**.

At the beginning, professional identity is unresolved:

- field
- education
- skills
- projects
- experience
- interests
- work context

As the story progresses, the same evidence changes state:

**work context → structured evidence → adaptive question → multidimensional profile → career relationship → development direction**

The page must feel like one idea transforming, not a collection of independent sections.

## 2.2 Emotional target

The experience should feel:

- intelligent
- composed
- human
- analytical without being clinical
- confident without claiming certainty
- premium without luxury clichés
- technological without looking like an “AI template”

It must not feel:

- mystical
- horoscope-like
- cyberpunk
- HR surveillance-like
- therapy-like
- generic SaaS
- purple/blue AI
- stock-market dashboard-like

## 2.3 Visual ownership test

If “Personality Assessor” is replaced with a random SaaS name and the page still makes complete sense, the design has failed. Every major visual state must derive from one of these product-specific truths:

- professional context
- CV/profile evidence
- adaptive questioning
- multidimensional interpretation
- explainable career relationship
- development over time

---

# 3. Hard visual rules for this implementation

1. No gradients anywhere.
2. No ivory, cream, beige, warm luxury off-white.
3. No purple/blue/cyan AI aesthetic.
4. No eyebrow/kicker text anywhere.
5. No visible editorial scene numbering (`01`, `02`, etc.).
6. No decorative horizontal hairlines/dividers as a visual motif.
7. No split-color hero headline.
8. No left-copy/right-image hero.
9. No floating rounded navbar capsule.
10. No “AI Powered”, “Live”, “New”, or similar decorative badges/pills.
11. No generic glassmorphism.
12. No random orb/blob/particle-brain WebGL.
13. No default card grid for the homepage narrative.
14. No bounce/pop entrance motion.
15. No hard scroll snap.
16. No theatrical blocking loader.
17. No invented user testimonials or metrics.
18. Do not imply photographed people used the assessment or received a specific personality/career result.
19. Do not put every technique on every page. Cinematic motion belongs to storytelling; auth/forms remain direct.

# 4. Final color system

**DESIGN LOCK**

```css
--pa-ink: #0B0C0D;
--pa-graphite: #17191A;
--pa-paper: #FFFFFF;
--pa-cool-1: #E6EAE8;
--pa-cool-2: #D9DEDC;
--pa-muted: #5D6461;
--pa-accent: #C84A2D;
--pa-accent-hover: #A63820;
--pa-accent-on-dark: #F07A59;
--pa-success: #147A5B;
--pa-warning: #9A6700;
--pa-danger: #B42318;
```

### Usage rules

- Main light background = pure white `#FFFFFF`.
- Supporting light chapter = visibly cool gray `#E6EAE8`, never warm off-white.
- Dark chapter = `#0B0C0D` or `#17191A`.
- Accent = vermilion `#C84A2D`; use sparingly for active state, action, current evidence, focus emphasis and small identity gestures.
- Do **not** make the site “orange.” Aim for roughly 5–10% accent occupancy in a typical viewport.
- On dark surfaces, small accent text uses `#F07A59`, not `#C84A2D`.
- Semantic success/warning/error colors are separate from brand accent.
- OCEAN/RIASEC are not rendered as a rainbow. Use neutral geometry plus one controlled accent to show active/selected values.

### Contrast intent

- Ink on white and ink on cool gray must be the default reading combination.
- Muted body text `#5D6461` is allowed on white; do not use it as small text on dark.
- White text on `#C84A2D` is permitted for button text.
- Focus rings must remain obvious on both light and dark scenes.

# 5. Final typography system

## 5.1 Families

**DESIGN LOCK**

### Primary: Instrument Sans Variable
Use for:

- brand wordmark
- navigation
- hero/display headings
- section headings
- UI labels
- buttons
- data labels
- numbers

Reason: the existing project already uses Instrument Sans; the variable width axis gives us authorship through proportion rather than fake “premium” ultra-bold weight.

### Secondary: Newsreader Variable
Use only for:

- interpretive pull statements
- human explanatory moments
- one or two reflective sentences per long marketing page

Do not use it for navigation, buttons, forms, data, small labels, or every section heading.

### Font delivery

- Remove Google Fonts `@import` from public CSS.
- Self-host WOFF2 variable font assets in the project, using the upstream OFL-licensed families.
- Preload only the critical Instrument Sans file used above the fold.
- Do not preload Newsreader unless browser profiling proves it is used in the first viewport.
- Set explicit fallback stacks and avoid layout shift from late font replacement.

- weight 500
- no uppercase transformation

### Newsreader pull statement

- desktop 40–56 px / 1.05
- mobile 30–38 px / 1.12
- weight 400
- optional italic only when the copy itself is reflective, never as decoration

### Numerals

Use tabular figures for live data/result examples where alignment matters.

# 6. Layout system

## 6.1 Global grid

**DESIGN LOCK**

- Desktop ≥ 1280: 12-column grid.
- Tablet 768–1279: 8-column grid.
- Mobile < 768: 4-column grid.
- Desktop outer inset: 48 px at 1280–1599; 64 px ≥ 1600.
- Tablet inset: 32 px.
- Mobile inset: 20 px.
- Desktop column gap: 24 px.
- Tablet gap: 18 px.
- Mobile gap: 12 px.
- No generic centered `max-width: 1200px` shell for cinematic scenes; full-width compositions may use the grid directly.
- Reading copy should still use controlled measures.

## 6.2 Spacing rhythm

Base spacing set:

`4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 80, 96, 128, 160`

Do not invent random 37/53/91 px spacing unless optical browser QA justifies it.

## 6.3 Radius

- Marketing buttons and functional surfaces: 2–4 px maximum.
- Inputs: 2 px.
- Do not use 18–32 px “friendly SaaS” radius.
- Circular controls allowed only where their function is intrinsically circular (e.g. previous/next arrow icon button).

## 7.3 Scene behavior

At top of homepage hero:

- transparent background
- white foreground
- header visually belongs to the hero image

When entering light sequence:

- foreground becomes ink
- transition 240 ms, `power2.out`
- no divider line

When a dark authored scene is active:

- full-width background becomes `#0B0C0D` or transparent if underlying scene is stable and readable
- foreground becomes white

Do not use `mix-blend-mode` for core nav readability.

## 7.4 Mobile menu

- button text: `Menu` / `Close`
- minimum target: 48 × 48 px
- opens a full-viewport solid panel, not a floating card
- background white; ink text; accent used only for primary CTA

- Escape closes and restores focus to trigger
- lock background scroll while menu is open

# 10. Portrait Journey — one master pinned stage

## 10.1 Engineering geometry

Desktop/pointer-rich only (`min-width: 1024px` and `pointer:fine`):

- stage height in layout: trigger controls approximately `4.8 × viewportHeight` of scroll distance
- inner visual stage pins at 100svh
- no snap
- `scrub: 0.78`
- `anticipatePin: 1`
- `invalidateOnRefresh: true`
- one master GSAP timeline; do not create independent ScrollTriggers for every child
- scroll-driven master timeline uses `ease: "none"`; child transitions may use restrained `power2.inOut` interpolation where it does not break reversible progress logic

Approximate normalized state anchors:

- 0.00 — Work / evidence enters
- 0.18 — CV/profile context resolves
- 0.37 — Adaptive question
- 0.56 — Four analytical lenses
- 0.76 — Career relationship
- 0.91 — Development state
- 1.00 — Trust handoff

Each transition must overlap by approximately 6–10% of total normalized progress. Never allow a blank stage.

## 10.2 Persistent actor: Profile Plane

A single semantic visual object changes function through the sequence.

### State A

Looks like a tall professional evidence/document field — white plane, square-ish corners, real typographic fragments, no fake glass.

### State B

Document fragments reorganize into structured context: field, skills, subjects/interests. The plane becomes less document-like and more analytical.

### State C

A question occupies the same spatial footprint. The prior evidence remains faintly legible behind/around it so the causal relationship is visible.

### State D

The question answer resolves into profile geometry representing distinct analytical lenses.

### State E

Profile geometry becomes career comparison evidence.

### State F

The visible mismatch/gap becomes next-step development content.

No WebGL is required. Build with semantic HTML, SVG where useful, CSS transforms and GSAP.

---

## State A — Work-world rail / context

### Heading

`Start with the work you’ve already done`

### Body

`A CV or manual profile gives the assessment context: your field, experience, subjects, skills and interests.`

### Media behavior

The five-image work-world rail moves behind the Profile Plane from right to left during the first ~20% of the master timeline.

Desktop image geometry:

- each image width 24–30vw
- height 48–66vh, intentionally varied within that range
- gap 16 px
- no card borders
- no rounded containers
- caption sits directly below image, 14 px, muted/ink depending background
- rail translates approximately 120–145vw over its active interval
- translation is linear with scroll; no auto-loop

The rail exists to show that professional context differs, not to show a portfolio gallery.

## State B — CV/profile interpretation

### Heading

`Turn background into assessment context`

### Body

`The system identifies useful professional signals before the assessment begins. You stay able to review the detected context before moving on.`

### Profile Plane content demonstration

Use neutral demonstration fields, not the photographed person’s identity:

- `Field` → `Software / systems`
- `Skills` → `Problem solving · JavaScript · Analysis`
- `Interests` → `Learning · Product building · Technology`

Include a visible label `Demonstration profile` in normal text, not a pill or eyebrow.

## State C — Adaptive question

### Heading

`The questions change with the context`

### Body

`A student, a recent graduate and an experienced professional should not receive an identical assessment. Your profile helps determine what the system asks next.`

### Demo question

`When a project changes direction, what do you do first?`

Visible answer examples:

- `Clarify the changed constraint, then test the revised path.`
- `Gather input before choosing the next step.`

These are demonstration controls. They can be clickable for microinteraction but must not pretend to calculate a real result.

### Interaction motion

- answer hover/focus: 180–220 ms; background/ink change + maximum 1 px y shift
- selected answer: accent indicator through fill/text state, not a pill outline
- question change in scroll sequence: outgoing prompt shifts x `-6vw`, fades to .15; incoming analytical geometry starts before prompt fully leaves

## State D — analytical lenses

### Heading

`More than one way to read a profile`

### Body

`Personality, vocational interests, work values and career signals stay distinct so you can see where each reading comes from.`

### Lens controls

Text buttons only:

- `Big Five / OCEAN`
- `RIASEC`
- `Work values`
- `Career signals`

No pills. Active item uses accent color + weight/opacity change. No decorative underline required.

### Exact explanatory copy

**Big Five / OCEAN**  
`Five continuous personality dimensions: Openness, Conscientiousness, Extraversion, Agreeableness and Neuroticism.`

**RIASEC**  
`Six vocational interest dimensions: Realistic, Investigative, Artistic, Social, Enterprising and Conventional.`

**Work values**  
`What matters in the conditions and rewards of work, including growth, independence, security and other value dimensions.`

**Career signals**  
`Professional evidence such as problem solving, learning orientation, technical depth and leadership.`

### Visualization rules

- OCEAN: five horizontal data scales, neutral track + accent value; these are functional data marks, not decorative dividers.
- RIASEC: one six-axis radial/radar-like SVG with neutral structure and accent profile shape; no rainbow.
- Work Values: eight ranked typographic/value rows; no equal card tiles.
- Career Signals: four vector bars/columns with large numeric values from `marketingDemo` demonstration data.
- every visualization includes accessible text equivalents or list content in DOM.

# 15. Global motion system

## 15.1 Motion philosophy

- motion explains state change
- scroll-linked motion is reversible
- stillness is deliberate
- no bounce
- no cheap “everything fades up” system
- no scroll hijacking
- no touch smoothing that disconnects content from the finger

## 15.2 Technology lock

Use current `gsap` dependency. Import/register:

- `ScrollTrigger`
- `ScrollSmoother`

Do not add Lenis, Locomotive Scroll or another global smooth-scroll library.

Framer Motion may remain for existing route/auth transitions where useful; do not orchestrate the same DOM node simultaneously with Framer and GSAP.

Do not introduce Three.js/R3F for the marketing redesign.

## 15.3 Desktop smooth scrolling

Only public marketing routes, not login/signup or protected app:

```js
ScrollSmoother.create({
  wrapper: '#smooth-wrapper',
  content: '#smooth-content',
  smooth: 0.78,
  effects: false,
  smoothTouch: false,
});
```

Rules:

- create smoother before page ScrollTriggers
- preserve native browser scrollbar
- do not use `normalizeScroll` initially
- fixed header stays outside the smoother content wrapper
- kill/recreate appropriately on route lifecycle
- if `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, do not instantiate ScrollSmoother
- if `pointer: coarse`, do not instantiate ScrollSmoother

## 15.4 GSAP React lifecycle

Every scene-level GSAP module must use `gsap.context()` (or official React `useGSAP` if Codex chooses to add that small official package) and revert/kill on unmount.

Never leave stale ScrollTriggers between route transitions.

Call `ScrollTrigger.refresh()` after:

- critical font readiness
- hero image load if dimensions/crop changed
- meaningful responsive layout change

Do not refresh continuously during scroll.

## 15.5 Motion timing tokens

```js
const motion = {
  fast: 0.20,
  ui: 0.26,
  reveal: 0.62,
  scene: 0.90,
  hero: 1.35,
  smoothScrollCatchup: 0.78,
};
```

Eases:

- UI hover/focus: `power2.out`
- ordinary reveal: `power3.out`
- controlled scene interpolation: `power2.inOut`
- master scroll timeline: `none`

No `back`, `bounce`, `elastic` eases in marketing/auth.

## 15.6 Hover

- link/CTA reaction 180–260 ms
- maximum translateY: 1–2 px
- no scale > 1.015 on buttons
- image hover, where used: scale max 1.025 over 650–900 ms
- no cursor-following magnetic button unless later browser testing proves it adds real value; first pass excludes it

---

# 16. Mobile choreography

## 16.1 General

Mobile is not the desktop pinned sequence collapsed into a column.

Below 1024 px:

- remove global ScrollSmoother
- remove pinned 4.8vh journey
- use native scrolling
- transform the five journey states into a continuous vertical story
- each state retains the same persistent Profile Plane concept through shared layout/state transitions, but movement distances are smaller

## 16.2 Hero

- 100svh, min-height 620 px
- H1 in upper/lower composition based on source focal crop; baseline implementation uses lower-left with 20 px inset
- body and CTAs move beneath heading with no overlay collision
- use object-position derived from desktop but allow media query adjustment up to ±12 percentage points
- no automatic image zoom beyond 1.01 on mobile

## 16.3 Work-world rail

Mobile uses native `overflow-x:auto` + `scroll-snap-type:x mandatory` because this is browser-native scrolling, not a custom drag dependency.

Still provide `Previous` and `Next` icon/text controls at ≥44×44 px so the gallery is operable without a dragging gesture.

- image width: 78vw
- max height: 58svh
- gap: 12 px
- scroll padding: 20 px

## 16.4 Lens control

- four text controls wrap into two rows if needed
- min target 44 px high
- selected state communicated by text + color/weight, never color only
- visualization appears below controls

## 16.5 Auth

- no fixed 50/50 split
- 28–34svh media opening
- H1 bridges media/paper world
- form controls min-height 48 px
- bottom padding includes safe-area inset where supported

# 17. Reduced-motion composition

When `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`:

1. Disable ScrollSmoother.
2. Disable pinned/horizontal scrub choreography.
3. Render all homepage semantic states in a normal vertical document.
4. Preserve Profile Plane in its resolved/static state for each chapter.
5. Remove large-scale panning, zooming and cross-screen translations.
6. Allow only short opacity/color transitions ≤150 ms where needed to communicate interaction state.
7. No auto-moving image rail. It becomes a native horizontal gallery or static vertical media sequence.
8. Header scene color changes may remain because they are necessary for readability, but use near-instant transitions.

Reduced motion must still feel designed, not like the CSS failed to load.

---

# 18. Accessibility acceptance requirements

Target WCAG 2.2 AA behavior for redesigned public/auth surfaces.

- Skip link remains.
- Every page has one logical H1.
- Heading hierarchy is semantic; typography size does not dictate HTML level.
- Visible labels on all auth fields.
- Errors are textual and use appropriate live regions.
- Do not block paste in password/email fields.
- Preserve browser/password manager autocomplete attributes.
- Focus indicator minimum 3 px visual ring or equivalent, never removed.
- Header/mobile menu restores focus on close.
- All custom interactive controls keyboard operable.
- If any interaction uses drag, provide single-pointer previous/next controls.
- Our own target standard: 44×44 px minimum even though WCAG 2.2’s AA minimum can be smaller in allowed cases.
- Do not use color alone to communicate selected/error/success state.
- Decorative repeated images use empty alt; meaningful images use descriptive alt.
- Data visualizations expose textual equivalents in DOM.
- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- No flashing/flicker effects.

---

# 19. Performance acceptance requirements

Targets for field-quality UX:

- LCP ≤ 2.5 s at 75th percentile
- INP ≤ 200 ms at 75th percentile
- CLS ≤ 0.1 at 75th percentile

Implementation constraints:

- hero/LCP image eager + high priority
- no lazy loading above-the-fold hero
- all below-fold media lazy by default
- preserve width/height
- WebP responsive sources remain
- no WebGL dependency
- no autoplay background video in first pass
- one major GSAP timeline for the long journey, not hundreds of triggers
- transform/opacity as primary animated properties
- avoid animating width/height/top/left continuously during scroll
- `will-change` only on elements actively animated; remove/avoid global blanket use
- font files WOFF2; minimize number of files and preload only critical Instrument Sans
- no route-blocking loader
- defer noncritical marketing visualization code if bundle analysis shows it affects initial load materially
