# Personality Assessor — ZERO-BASE Phase A/B/C
## Award Intelligence + Product Archaeology + Radical Creative Territories

**Date:** 16 August 2026  
**Status:** Research and concept-generation authority — **NO CODING**  
**Starting judgment:** Current visible frontend is rejected at approximately 1–2/10 against the intended top-tier award benchmark.  
**Goal:** Discover a new visual concept from product truth, not from the existing frontend.

---

# 0. Reset premise

This phase does not repair:
- Evidence Imprint;
- Work Worlds;
- the current hero;
- the current section stack;
- the current typography system;
- the current public-route structures;
- the current dashboard visual system.

Those implementations are used only as negative evidence.

The only inherited authority is:
1. real product behavior;
2. real backend/data contracts;
3. the Valtum anti-template doctrine;
4. user rejection evidence;
5. current elite-studio research.

The next website must be designed as if the current visible frontend never existed.

---

# 1. Award intelligence — what elite teams are actually doing

## 1.1 The score model reinforces the problem

Awwwards score pages expose:
- Design — 40%
- Usability — 30%
- Creativity — 20%
- Content — 10%

Development recognition also evaluates:
- semantics / SEO;
- animations / transitions;
- accessibility;
- web-performance optimization;
- responsive design;
- markup / metadata.

The lesson is not to “game” a jury.

It is that an information-heavy website can be correct and still fail because most of the perceived quality lives outside written content.

---

## 1.2 Lusion / Oryzo — world before UI

Oryzo’s team openly rejected an early concept that already looked like a typical polished award-site direction because it felt lifeless.

Their improvement did not come from:
- more cards;
- a better grid;
- another type scale.

It came from:
- a believable world;
- a protagonist at the center;
- transitions that preserve continuity;
- reducing UI competing with the world.

### Transfer to Personality Assessor

The new site needs a world or behavioral system stronger than its navigation, labels, headings and panels.

If the visitor remembers the UI layout rather than the experience, we have failed.

---

## 1.3 OFF+BRAND / Vizcom — demonstration before explanation

Vizcom’s hero is designed as a short product story:
- sketch;
- transformation;
- iteration.

The experience proves the proposition before long copy is needed.

### Transfer

Personality Assessor should let the visitor *experience one piece of adaptive interpretation* immediately.

The public site should not spend the first half of the page explaining how adaptation works.

---

## 1.4 Podium — abandon page logic when the subject requires continuity

Podium deliberately moved away from a page-based structure because ordinary portfolio pages broke the rhythm of its films.

### Transfer

We must not assume the homepage needs a sequence of conventional sections.

A continuous narrative is allowed if it makes the product easier and more memorable.

---

## 1.5 Naked City Films — the interface behaves like the subject

Naked City treats movement more like editorial cutting than generic web fades.

The site communicates identity through:
- timing;
- pacing;
- decisive transitions;
- visible structure;
- restraint.

### Transfer

Personality Assessor motion should behave like interpretation:
- a question causes a consequence;
- evidence changes a reading;
- missing information creates an unresolved state;
- a new assessment changes history.

Not:
- fade-up;
- line draw;
- parallax because the library makes it easy.

---

## 1.6 Obys — identity and interaction are one system

Obys did not start from web page components. Their identity work began with type and the idea of “space,” then interaction inherited those rules.

### Transfer

Typography, visual material, motion and page structure must originate from one idea.

A font choice cannot carry the identity by itself.

---

## 1.7 San Rita — no two projects should follow one formula

San Rita describes each brief as a different trail and treats constraints as part of the design.

Their GZNA work also demonstrates a useful pattern: a complex industrial ecosystem became tactile through a direct interactive visualizer instead of a static catalog.

### Transfer

Personality Assessor needs a direct experience native to assessment and interpretation, not a studio-wide Awwwards recipe.

---

## 1.8 DashDigital — product complexity should produce the solution

DashDigital describes research and strategy as preceding visual production.

Different client industries lead to different solutions.

### Transfer

The product archaeology below should generate our visual concept.

The concept should not be imported from another award site.

---

## 1.9 Lesse Studio — creativity still needs frictionless use

Lesse’s redesign reduced navigation friction while retaining identity.

### Transfer

We should be visually ambitious on public storytelling and extremely direct when the user is:
- signing up;
- uploading context;
- answering an assessment;
- reading a real result;
- deleting/exporting data.

Award-level is not permission to make operational tasks theatrical.

---

# 2. The elite “designer brain” model

The recurring thinking model across strong studios is:

## 2.1 Find an ownable truth
What is true about this product that competitors cannot simply borrow?

## 2.2 Turn truth into behavior
What does that truth *do* visually?

## 2.3 Pick one protagonist
What persists long enough to create memory and continuity?

## 2.4 Compose keyframes
Before motion, create still states worth photographing.

## 2.5 Build rhythm, not sections
Alternate:
- compression;
- release;
- scale;
- detail;
- silence;
- interaction;
- narrative consequence.

## 2.6 Let media carry meaning
Photography, type, data, texture, soundless movement and UI should each have a job.

## 2.7 Remove copy the visual system already explains
Elite work edits aggressively.

## 2.8 Select technology after the idea
GSAP, Anime.js, WebGL, Rive, Three.js, Canvas, CSS and native APIs are implementation consequences.

## 2.9 Design mobile as a different choreography
The concept stays.
The composition changes.

## 2.10 Refine in browser
Development and art direction iterate together.

The browser is not just QA.
It is the final design surface.

---

# 3. Product archaeology — what the real Personality Assessor actually contains

The current source-of-truth audit describes Personality Assessor as an end-to-end system combining:
- adaptive psychometric questions;
- CV/profile context;
- deterministic multi-dimensional scoring;
- career matching;
- personal analytics;
- optional AI narrative/coaching.

The important visual opportunity is that the product is *not one score*.

It is a chain of changing states.

---

# 4. The real journey

At a high level:

```text
professional context / CV
        ↓
question coverage state
        ↓
adaptive question
        ↓
answer
        ↓
evidence contributions
        ↓
Big Five / RIASEC / Work Values / Career Signals
        ↓
valid / partial / insufficient states
        ↓
career relationship layers
        ↓
skill gaps
        ↓
roadmap
        ↓
new assessment / history / change
```

That is far more visually interesting than the current landing-page information architecture.

---

# 5. Native product materials discovered in source

## 5.1 Context is not just text

Question generation can use:
- domain;
- skills;
- tools;
- interests;
- previous questions;
- missing traits;
- missing facets;
- CV relevance;
- expected difficulty.

Therefore “context” is a live set of forces influencing the next question.

This is much richer than rendering a CV paragraph inside a white box.

---

## 5.2 The questionnaire is coverage-seeking

The current question-coverage service tracks:
- trait coverage;
- facet coverage;
- missing traits;
- missing facets;
- CV coverage;
- whether more CV-focused questions are needed;
- easy → medium → advanced progression.

This means the assessment has an actual *unfinished shape* at every moment.

The next question is partly chosen because something is not sufficiently covered.

### Visual opportunity
**Absence can become a protagonist.**

Instead of only visualizing what is known, we can visualize:
- what is unresolved;
- what the next question is trying to clarify;
- which parts remain open.

---

## 5.3 One answer can affect multiple dimensions

The evidence builder can map one answer into:
- Big Five;
- RIASEC;
- Work Values;
- Career Signals.

The contribution can have:
- direction;
- source;
- dimension;
- key;
- signal;
- weight.

### Visual opportunity
A response is not a one-to-one “answer → score.”

It can be shown as one event being interpreted through several different systems.

That is a major product-native visual idea.

---

## 5.4 The system explicitly knows uncertainty

The scoring orchestrator produces:
- `valid`;
- `partial`;
- `insufficient_data`;
- evidence count;
- evidence sources;
- missing evidence;
- missing dimensions;
- contradictions;
- global confidence;
- per-layer confidence;
- final/not-final state.

### Visual opportunity
The strongest visual language may come from **resolution vs uncertainty**, not from bars and cards.

Incomplete information should remain visibly incomplete.

Contradiction can be designed as tension, not error.

---

## 5.5 Career fit is layered

The current career-matching service computes distinct layers:
- RIASEC;
- skill readiness;
- work values;
- personality;
- education;
- goal/domain;

and separately tracks signal fit and confidence.

### Visual opportunity
Career fit can become a composite relationship rather than a single percentage.

A role can be:
- close in one dimension;
- stretched in another;
- missing evidence in a third.

That relationship can become spatial, cinematic or tactile.

---

## 5.6 Skill gaps produce action

The product distinguishes:
- matched skills;
- missing critical skills;
- recommended skills;
- evidence sources;
- readiness.

The roadmap then turns gaps into:
- 0–30 days;
- 1–3 months;
- 3–6 months;
- 6–12 months;
- portfolio proof;
- role preparation;
- stretch impact.

### Visual opportunity
The product is not simply “know yourself.”

It is:
**interpret → compare → act → produce new proof → reassess.**

---

## 5.7 History matters

The analytics domain contains:
- assessment history;
- trait trends;
- insight timeline;
- career readiness;
- skill progress;
- roadmap progress.

### Visual opportunity
Identity is temporal.

The product can show:
**you are not a fixed result.**

That is emotionally and visually stronger than a static personality dashboard.

---

# 6. Product-specific creative truths

From the source, five unusually strong truths emerge:

1. **The system asks because something is unresolved.**
2. **One decision can be interpreted in several different ways.**
3. **A profile can be partial, contradictory and still useful.**
4. **A career is a layered relationship, not a label.**
5. **A later assessment can change the story.**

These five truths are stronger creative material than “professional evidence as material.”

They should drive the next concepts.

---

# 7. Territory A — THE DECISION PORTRAIT
## Provisional score: 9.3/10 potential

### One-sentence concept

> **You are revealed through decisions, not through labels.**

The website behaves like a cinematic sequence of professional situations.

The visitor makes one or two real illustrative choices.

Each choice changes the visual world and creates a new fragment of a non-literal “portrait.”

The portrait is not a face.
It is a changing composition made from:
- environment;
- gesture;
- typography;
- fragments of work;
- data;
- contrast.

### Why it belongs to Personality Assessor

The product is fundamentally question/decision-driven.

Question generation is contextual and coverage-seeking.

One response contributes to several readings.

Therefore the homepage can demonstrate the actual product mechanic instead of explaining it.

### First ten seconds

No conventional hero section.

The browser opens *inside a professional situation*.

Example:
a project room under delivery pressure.

A concise prompt enters the scene:

`The deadline moves forward. What do you protect first?`

Three actions exist physically within the composition.

The user chooses.

The scene cuts.

A new visual portrait begins to assemble from the decision.

Brand/title appears only after the user has experienced the idea.

### Desktop visual language

- full-screen editorial/cinematic photography or directed video;
- split frames;
- film cuts;
- cropped gestures/hands/work artifacts;
- oversized type used only when it behaves like part of the edit;
- one decision can create multiple visual consequences;
- no section containers.

Think:
**interactive short film + data portrait**, not SaaS landing page.

### Homepage rhythm

```text
SCENE
decision
CUT
interpretation begins

SCENE
same decision seen four different ways

REVEAL
what is still unresolved

SCENE
career environments appear as alternate futures

ACTION
build your real profile
```

No requirement for “Work Worlds,” “Trust,” “Methodology” sections.

### Signature behavior

**Decision Cut**

A choice changes:
- crop;
- scene;
- typography;
- data composition;
- next visual question.

The website feels responsive to intention.

### Profile reveal

The same selected decision is replayed through four readings:
- personality;
- vocational interest;
- values;
- career signal.

Not four cards.

Four *edits* of the same event.

### Career

A chosen decision opens alternate role-world edits.

The user sees why a role feels:
- natural;
- stretched;
- under-supported.

### Mobile

Excellent translation.

390×844 becomes a vertical interactive film:
- full-viewport scene;
- thumb-zone decisions;
- direct cut;
- portrait fragments;
- swipe or tap to inspect alternate readings.

No desktop stacking.

### Product-app translation

Assessment:
- perfect fit;
- one decision per screen;
- clean operational UI.

Results:
- a “decision reel” can show which answers shaped each reading.

Analytics:
- compare two portrait cuts from different assessments.

### Assets required

This concept **cannot reach 9/10 with random Pexels imagery**.

Needs:
- a tightly art-directed photographic/video set;
- 5–8 professional scenarios;
- consistent lens/light/grade;
- macro detail crops;
- human gestures;
- real workplace materials.

Could be:
- commissioned;
- carefully generated as a coherent editorial series;
- or licensed from one consistent production set.

### Technology

Likely:
- DOM/CSS for type and controls;
- GSAP or native timeline for scene cuts;
- optional WebGL only for high-quality image-transition treatment;
- no generic 3D object.

### Anti-copy proof

The experience only works because Personality Assessor asks contextual questions and interprets responses.

It would not transfer cleanly to a courier, booking, fintech or agency site.

### Main risk

Could become overly cinematic and hide the actual product.

Mitigation:
the decision itself must be real, immediate and legible.

---

# 8. Territory B — THE UNFINISHED MAP
## Provisional score: 9.0/10 potential

### One-sentence concept

> **Your profile is not a result. It is a map with resolved and unresolved territory.**

The entire experience is organized around a changing topographic / cartographic field.

But this is **not** a generic data orb.

### Product truth behind it

The scoring system explicitly knows:
- missing dimensions;
- missing evidence;
- contradictions;
- partial validity;
- confidence;
- coverage.

This gives us a native “known / unknown / contradictory” landscape.

### First ten seconds

A nearly empty field appears.

Not a loading state.

A real current professional context is introduced.

As context enters, some regions become defined while others remain blank.

The headline can be minimal:

`Not everything about you is known yet.`

Then:

`That is the point.`

A question appears where the map is least resolved.

### Visual world

- editorial cartography;
- contour surfaces;
- voids;
- boundaries;
- pressure/tension;
- layered translucent data;
- photographic fragments embedded into terrain;
- no dashboards.

The map is not claimed to be scientific geography.

It is a visual metaphor for evidence coverage.

### Signature behavior

**Resolution**

Questions physically resolve previously unclear territory.

Contradictory evidence can create:
- overlapping boundaries;
- competing contours;
- unstable regions.

Missing evidence remains blank.

### Four readings

Instead of four tabs:
the same map changes projection.

Personality = one projection.
RIASEC = another.
Values = another.
Career Signals = another.

Like changing map layers, not changing cards.

### Career

Role profiles become alternate territories.

The user's map overlays a role map.

The overlap and mismatch become visible.

Career fit becomes spatially intelligible.

### Progress

Two assessment maps can be compared through time:
- changed terrain;
- stable regions;
- newly resolved areas.

### Mobile

A full-screen map with direct pan/inspect.

But mobile must have fixed, accessible “next insight” controls so the user is never forced to pan precisely.

### Technology

Potentially:
- Canvas/SVG;
- optional WebGL if a truly tactile topology needs it;
- GSAP for projection transitions;
- direct reduced-motion 2D fallback.

### Assets

Less dependent on photography than Territory A.

Requires:
- custom map/art direction;
- strong data-design system;
- subtle selected photographic context.

### Anti-copy proof

The unresolved/partial/contradictory profile state is native to this product.

### Main risk

Could look pseudo-scientific or like AI generative visualization.

Mitigation:
- clearly metaphorical;
- editorial;
- no fake technical labels;
- no brain/biometric aesthetics;
- no “precision” claims.

---

# 9. Territory C — THE PROFESSIONAL CONTACT SHEET
## Provisional score: 8.8/10 potential

### One-sentence concept

> **A person is not one professional image. They are a sequence of moments.**

The website behaves like a living editorial contact sheet / film archive of work moments.

### Product truth behind it

The platform uses:
- context;
- projects;
- CV;
- questions;
- answers;
- skills;
- history;
- later reassessment.

Identity emerges from multiple moments rather than one label.

### First ten seconds

The opening is a wall/field of professional moments:
- presenting;
- reviewing;
- building;
- resolving conflict;
- writing;
- researching;
- making;
- learning.

No text-heavy hero.

The viewer scrolls or moves through them.

One moment expands.

A question appears inside that moment.

The answer causes the entire contact sheet to reorder.

### Signature behavior

**Re-edit**

The same material is re-edited depending on the analytical lens.

Personality does not add a chart panel.

It changes which moments become prominent.

RIASEC reorders the sheet differently.
Work Values highlights different moments.
Career Signals create another edit.

### Visual language

- editorial film;
- contact sheets;
- variable image scale;
- off-grid crops;
- contact marks;
- marginal type;
- full-bleed interruptions;
- occasional moving image.

Crucially, it must avoid becoming a grid of image cards.

The contact sheet should flow, overlap, crop and expand.

### Career

Select a role and the contact sheet re-edits around moments relevant to that role.

The role comparison becomes:
`Which parts of your existing work story are already present, and what is missing?`

### Progress

New work adds new frames.
Old frames remain.
The professional story visibly evolves.

### Mobile

Very strong:
- vertically sequenced filmstrip;
- tap frame to expand;
- swipe through related moments;
- no tiny grid.

### Technology

- CSS grid/absolute editorial composition;
- GSAP Flip potentially useful because the same media actors reorder;
- video where available;
- no WebGL needed.

### Assets

Requires the strongest media library of all concepts:
- coherent professional stills/video;
- enough variation to sustain sequencing;
- actual project artifacts if possible.

### Anti-copy proof

The re-editing concept comes from multi-dimensional interpretation and temporal work history.

### Main risk

Can look like a creative-agency portfolio instead of a product.

Mitigation:
interactive questions and analytical re-editing must remain central.

---

# 10. Territory D — THE PARALLEL SELF
## Provisional score: 8.9/10 potential

### One-sentence concept

> **The same evidence can tell four different truths about one person.**

The central design idea is simultaneous interpretation.

Instead of treating Personality, RIASEC, Work Values and Career Signals as separate modules, one source event exists in the center while four visual readings diverge around it.

### Product truth behind it

One answer can contribute into multiple dimensions.

That is real system behavior.

### First ten seconds

A single professional moment occupies the whole screen.

The user chooses a response.

The scene fractures into four simultaneous interpretations.

Each interpretation has its own visual language.

No “Four Readings” tab control.

The visitor sees one event being read four ways.

### Signature behavior

**Refraction**

Not lens/magnifier cliché.

The same content is transformed into:
- typographic tension;
- spatial direction;
- color/material;
- visual sequence.

The four readings can temporarily coexist before recombining.

### Visual language

Potentially very distinctive:
- split screens;
- stacked exposures;
- printmaking/registration;
- multiple synchronized crops;
- shared moving actor crossing separate visual systems.

### Career

A role can pull more strongly on some interpretations than others.

The screen rearranges based on which layers matter most.

### Progress

Later assessments create a second “version” of the self.

Old/new interpretations can synchronize or diverge.

### Mobile

Mobile cannot show four equal quadrants.

Instead:
- one source moment;
- quick vertical “turn” through four interpretations;
- persistent source actor;
- gesture between lenses.

### Technology

- GSAP / Flip;
- clip paths;
- SVG;
- optional canvas compositing;
- no need for WebGL.

### Assets

Requires:
- a custom graphic-design system;
- highly controlled photography;
- four genuinely distinct but coherent interpretation languages.

### Anti-copy proof

The four-system interpretation is specific to this product.

### Main risk

Could become visually busy and difficult to understand.

Mitigation:
one source moment always remains visually identifiable.

---

# 11. Territory E — THE CAREER STAGE
## Provisional score: 8.5/10 potential

### One-sentence concept

> **A professional identity changes depending on the situation and the role around it.**

The website becomes a sequence of theatrical “work stages.”

The same human subject enters different professional environments.

The environment changes the decisions, emphasis and career relationship.

### Product truth behind it

Questions adapt to:
- domain;
- skills;
- context;
- coverage.

Career fit is layered rather than universal.

### First ten seconds

A quiet human figure / work object exists in an empty stage.

The stage transforms:
- research room;
- workshop;
- strategy room;
- technical environment;
- collaborative setting.

The same person behaves differently in each.

The site asks:
`Which version of work feels most like you?`

### Signature behavior

**Set Change**

The environment transforms around the persistent subject.

Unlike old Work Worlds, these are not six image swaps.

The subject and spatial composition persist while the *world* changes.

### Visual language

- theatrical lighting;
- set design;
- strong physical objects;
- moving walls/surfaces;
- selective 3D or composited photography;
- sparse type.

### Career

This concept naturally grows into career exploration:
roles become worlds the user can enter.

### Mobile

Each stage becomes a full-height scene.
Swipe or scroll transitions between worlds.

### Technology

Potentially:
- WebGL / Three.js becomes justified if actual scene continuity requires it;
- or layered DOM/video if sufficient.

### Assets

Highest production burden:
- bespoke 3D/set assets or coherent composited scenes;
- human subject consistency;
- art direction.

### Anti-copy proof

Context-sensitive assessment and career worlds justify the set transformations.

### Main risk

High production cost and could drift toward spectacle.

Mitigation:
keep the actual question/decision as the narrative trigger.

---

# 12. Territory comparison

| Territory | Design Potential | Creativity | Product Specificity | Usability | Mobile | Asset Cost | Technical Risk |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Decision Portrait | 9.4 | 9.5 | 9.6 | 9.0 | 9.4 | High | Medium |
| Unfinished Map | 9.2 | 9.3 | 9.3 | 8.4 | 8.5 | Medium | Medium-High |
| Professional Contact Sheet | 9.1 | 9.0 | 8.9 | 9.0 | 9.2 | High | Low-Medium |
| Parallel Self | 9.2 | 9.4 | 9.5 | 8.5 | 8.4 | High | Medium |
| Career Stage | 9.4 | 9.3 | 8.8 | 8.5 | 8.7 | Very High | High |

These are concept-potential scores, not implementation scores.

---

# 13. Provisional winner

## **THE DECISION PORTRAIT**

This is currently the strongest territory.

Why:

1. It makes the product understandable within seconds.
2. It starts from a real native mechanic: contextual questions and decisions.
3. It drastically reduces marketing copy.
4. It is inherently interactive.
5. It can be visually cinematic without fake science.
6. It translates unusually well to mobile.
7. It can create a memorable first interaction.
8. It gives Valtum a strong portfolio story:
   **“We designed the website to behave like the product.”**
9. It allows the same response to unfold through multiple reading systems.
10. It avoids the previous obsession with panels, score cards and explanatory sections.

---

# 14. Strong secondary direction

## **THE PARALLEL SELF**

This is the strongest visual-system alternative.

It takes the real one-answer → multiple-dimensions behavior and turns it into an authored graphic experience.

It is more abstract than Decision Portrait and slightly riskier for usability, but it could produce extraordinarily distinctive static keyframes.

---

# 15. A possible future synthesis — NOT YET LOCKED

Do not merge territories prematurely.

But the most promising future synthesis would be:

**Decision Portrait as the public narrative engine**
+
**Parallel Self as the result/interpretation visual language**

That would create:

```text
professional situation
↓
decision
↓
same moment splits into multiple readings
↓
unresolved dimensions invite further questions
↓
career futures become explainable
```

This is far stronger than:

```text
hero
↓
features
↓
four readings
↓
career section
↓
trust
```

However, the synthesis must be validated through static keyframes before it becomes final direction.

---

# 16. What we should now remove from the old design vocabulary

The next concept phase should not automatically carry:

- `Your work leaves evidence.`
- `Work changes the evidence.`
- `Context changes the question.`
- `Four readings. Kept separate.`
- `A fit score should explain itself.`
- `New work changes the profile.`
- `See what shaped the result.`
- `Build a profile you can return to.`

Some may return later if they earn their place.

None is currently locked.

Likewise:
- Source Serif 4;
- Source Sans 3;
- white/black neutral palette;
- Pexels images;
- current navigation;
- current footer;
- current image crops;
- current Work World taxonomy

are all unlocked.

---

# 17. Media conclusion

The current generic stock-photography library is not enough to produce the recommended 9/10 concept.

A top-tier public experience will likely require one of:

### Option 1 — commissioned/controlled photography
Best quality and authenticity.

### Option 2 — one cohesive licensed editorial series
Lower production effort, still coherent.

### Option 3 — deliberately generated editorial scenario set
Viable if art-directed tightly and not recognizably “AI stock.”

### Option 4 — hybrid
Real/stock professional macro material + generated controlled hero/decision scenes.

The media system must be approved as a single art direction, not image-by-image stock substitutions.

---

# 18. Typography conclusion

Do not select the final typeface before the concept keyframes.

The old mistake was asking typography to supply “premium.”

For Decision Portrait, likely needs:
- a strong cinematic/editorial display voice;
- a quiet highly legible interaction/UI face;
- possibly variable-width behavior;
- minimal type families.

But final font selection belongs after keyframe research.

---

# 19. Color conclusion

No palette is locked.

Color should emerge from:
- scenario photography;
- lighting;
- mood;
- product emotional objective.

Potentially:
- largely neutral UI;
- strong scene-specific color;
- graphic accent arising from the portrait system.

Do not preselect “premium green,” purple AI, beige luxury or black-tech.

---

# 20. Technology conclusion

Do not install or remove libraries yet.

For Decision Portrait:
- GSAP may be useful for cinematic continuity;
- Flip may be useful for actor identity across edits;
- WebGL may be useful for high-quality image transitions;
- Rive may not be needed;
- Anime.js may not be needed;
- Framer Motion can remain useful inside the operational product.

Technology will be locked only after static and motion storyboards.

---

# 21. Mobile concept for the provisional winner

390×844 should begin as a full-screen professional moment.

No desktop navigation compressed across the top.

Possible opening:

```text
minimal brand / menu

[full-height professional situation]

The deadline moves forward.

What do you protect first?

[decision]
[decision]
[decision]
```

After tap:

```text
CUT

same scene reframed

A visual portrait fragment appears.

“Your choice protected reliability.”

Continue
```

Then:
- interpretation;
- another unresolved question;
- career direction.

This would feel like an app.

Not a website shrunk to a phone.

---

The next step is **not coding**.

The next step is:

Required deliverables before motion or Codex:

2. first decision keyframe;

# Personality Assessor — ZERO-BASE Visual Reset Charter
## Total Frontend Art-Direction Restart — No Repair, No Legacy Visual Authority

**Date:** 16 August 2026  
**Status:** Active reset authority  
**Purpose:** Remove all visual/design inheritance from the rejected Personality Assessor frontend and restart the complete visible experience from product truth.

## Final judgment

Against a serious top-tier interactive-design benchmark, the current browser is approximately:

- Visual design: 1.5–2/10
- Creativity: 1–1.5/10
- Composition: 1.5–2/10
- Product-specific art direction: 1/10
- Mobile art direction: 0.5–1/10
- Award-readiness: 1/10

The implementation is technically competent but visually generic, container-led, over-explanatory, repetitive, and strongly AI/template-coded.

This reset treats the entire current visible design as rejected evidence.

## What is now unlocked

Nothing from the current visible frontend is visually sacred.

Reopened:
- creative concept
- homepage story
- section count
- route story
- content amount and copy
- hero and header
- typography and palette
- photography and protagonist
- data-viz language
- motion and scroll model
- route transitions
- dashboard, assessment, result, mobile and footer systems
- Evidence Imprint
- Source Serif / Source Sans pairing
- current neutral palette
- current Work Worlds, Context → Question, Career and route silhouettes

Past work remains only as rejection evidence and technical history.

## What survives

Only product and engineering truth:
- backend APIs
- auth/session contracts
- assessment persistence, recovery and drafts
- real question types
- scoring data contracts
- Big Five / RIASEC / Work Values / Career Signals semantics
- career recommendation contracts
- analytics/history contracts
- privacy/account actions actually supported
- API clients, services and real domain hooks
- URLs unless product strategy changes
- tests that protect real functionality rather than rejected styling

## Visual code considered disposable

Replace rather than patch:

```text
frontend/src/components/public/imprint/**
frontend/src/pages/public/**
frontend/src/styles/imprint/**
frontend/src/pages/PublicHomePage.jsx
frontend/src/content/personalityImprintMedia.js
frontend/src/imprint-guardrails.test.jsx
```

Visually rebuild while preserving functional logic where embedded:

```text
frontend/src/components/product/**
frontend/src/styles/product-shell.css
frontend/src/pages/Dashboard/**
frontend/src/pages/AnalyticsPage.jsx
frontend/src/components/analytics/**
frontend/src/styles/analytics-product.css
frontend/src/components/assessment-start/**
frontend/src/pages/AssessmentFlow/**
frontend/src/components/assessment/**
frontend/src/pages/Result/**
frontend/src/components/career/**
frontend/src/pages/Auth/**
frontend/src/pages/PrivacyControlsPage*
```

Do not delete business/session/data logic blindly; extract it before replacing the visual layer.

## New process

Do not begin with Hero / Work Worlds / Context / Profile / Career / Trust.

Use:

```text
PRODUCT TRUTH
↓
ONE MEMORABLE EXPERIENCE IDEA
↓
VISITOR EMOTION / MEMORY
↓
PROTAGONIST
↓
STORY RHYTHM
↓
VISUAL WORLD
↓
STATIC KEYFRAMES
↓
MOTION / INTERACTION
↓
CONTENT REDUCTION
↓
MOBILE RECOMPOSITION
↓
APPLICATION TRANSLATION
↓
IMPLEMENTATION ARCHITECTURE
```

The homepage may end up with four acts, eight acts, or no recognizable sections at all.

## Elite-studio research lessons

**Lusion / Oryzo**  
A clean typical award-style early concept was rejected because it felt lifeless. The breakthrough came from building a believable world around the protagonist and reducing UI around it.

**Podium**  
The team moved away from a page-based structure toward one continuous sequence; media itself carries transitions.

**Naked City Films**  
Movement behaves like editorial cutting and brand rhythm rather than default fade-up motion.

**Unseen Studio**  
Abstract ideas and hidden stories are translated into experiences users can explore and remember.

**Bisous / Beaucoup**  
An invisible structural grid maintains coherence while visible compositions vary dramatically in scale and media treatment.

**Lesse Studio**  
Creative identity and clarity coexist; expressive art direction is not an excuse for difficult navigation.

## Creative target

Not:
> “a beautiful personality-assessment SaaS website.”

Target:
> **a digital experience whose central visual behavior could only make sense for a system that interprets a human being from professional evidence and evolving work.**

Before writing content architecture, answer:
1. What single visual event should the visitor remember?
2. What can exist continuously for 20–40 seconds?
3. What changes meaning as the experience progresses?
4. What is physically/manipulably different from ordinary SaaS?
5. What product truth can become image, space, typography, data or interaction?
6. What can be understood without explanation copy?
7. Why could this experience not be moved unchanged to another AI/HR/SaaS product?

Until these are answered visually, do not code.

## Content rule

Visual system first. Content only where needed to orient, clarify or act.

The homepage should not explain every methodology, trust boundary, data category, score, career dimension or development stage.

Detailed information belongs in deeper routes and inspection layers.

## Anti-AI-template test

Reject any keyframe that resembles:
- heading + paragraph + card
- heading + tabs + content panel
- heading + image + three text columns
- four equal numbered items
- giant white rounded container
- three-card product explanation
- three-column privacy grid
- generic dark chapter with list/image/detail
- vertical stepper
- horizontal cards
- bento
- “serif title = premium”
- SVG lines added to make static layout look conceptual
- decorative labels such as ALIGN / TRANSLATE
- giant stock image used as protagonist without transformation

If the page can be described by component names rather than by what happens, reject it.

## Technology doctrine

No library is visually locked.

Anime.js, GSAP, Framer Motion, Rive, WebGL, Three.js, WAAPI, CSS and View Transitions are tools only.

Choose them after the concept.

## Mobile restart

The current 390×844 design is rejected completely.

Mobile must be designed as its own sequence, independently deciding:
- navigation
- hero
- protagonist
- crops
- gestures
- typography
- persistent controls
- content omissions
- assessment interaction
- dashboard interaction

It must not be the desktop DOM stacked vertically.

## Gates before implementation

**Gate A — Award intelligence**  
Deep-study current top-tier sites and studio process.

**Gate B — Product archaeology**  
Audit the real Personality Assessor journey and discover visual material in product truth.

**Gate C — 3–5 radically different creative territories**  
Each with concept, protagonist, spatial behavior, mobile translation and anti-copy proof.

**Gate D — One concept lock**

**Gate E — Static keyframes**  
Opening, first transition, core reveal, interactive state, final resolution, mobile opening, mobile product moment.

If still images are not 9/10, motion does not start.

**Gate F — Motion storyboard**

**Gate G — Product visual system**  
Assessment, results, analytics, career, dashboard, privacy.

**Gate H — Implementation**

## Definition of success

The next browser is judged against top-tier creative work, not the previous frontend.

The visual story must remain understandable with paragraphs hidden.

The homepage should not have a countable card system.

Mobile should not resemble desktop.

Typography should not carry all creative weight.

Images should transform meaning.

Motion should carry continuity rather than reveal containers.

## Current directive

**Do not issue another repair prompt to Codex.**

The current visible frontend has **zero design authority**.

Start new creative research and concept development from a blank visual canvas while preserving the real product logic underneath.

Only after a 9/10 static concept is approved should the old visual frontend be replaced in code.


### Supersession

For Math Intellect frontend decisions:

# 1. Mission

Reconstruct the entire visible Math Intellect frontend so it is credible as:

- a top-tier Valtum portfolio case study;
- a premium product suitable for serious high-value client scrutiny;
- an award-submission-caliber digital experience in visual design, usability, mobile craft, motion, performance and product specificity;
- a real mathematical workbench rather than an AI/SaaS template.

The redesign is a **complete frontend rebuild**, not a patch and not a reskin.

The visual frontend that exists today is negative evidence. Do not preserve its composition simply because components already exist.

Preserve product logic where it is correct. Re-author the visible experience.

---

# 2. Core product thesis

Math Intellect is a mathematical simulation and decision workbench with adaptive interpretation/progression layers.

Its native transformation is:

```text
real system
→ structure
→ assumptions
→ mathematical model
→ simulation
→ evidence
→ interpretation
→ comparison / decision
→ changed assumptions
→ rerun
```

The visual north star is:

> **Scientific Editorial × Real Systems × Living Mathematics**

The experience must feel intelligent because the mathematics is legible and manipulable — not because the interface uses blue/purple light, neural imagery, glass panels, fake telemetry or “intelligence” language.

---

# 3. Non-negotiable complete-rebuild boundary

## 3.1 Do not preserve the old visual frontend

The following are **not** design foundations:

- old hero;
- `IntelligenceSurfaceScene` / neural orb;

- global gradients and glows;

- hard-coded community theatre;

## 3.2 What may survive

Preserve or refactor, where technically correct:

Do **not** rewrite backend or database to fit the new UI.

## 5.1 TEXT–CONTAINER–CARD LOOP

# 6. New frontend visual foundation

## 6.1 Identity palette

Replace the current dark/gradient token system with this high-luminance neutral foundation:

```css
--mi-canvas: #F4F6F5;
--mi-paper: #FFFFFF;
--mi-ink: #111412;
--mi-ink-2: #2D3330;
--mi-text: #505753;
--mi-muted: #78807C;
--mi-rule: #D8DDDA;
--mi-rule-strong: #BAC1BD;
--mi-surface-soft: #ECEFEE;

--mi-change: #E35A35;
--mi-focus: #2457E6;
--mi-success: #23755B;
--mi-warning: #9D6814;
--mi-danger: #B64049;
```

Rules:

- no gradients anywhere as identity treatment;
- no permanent cyan/violet/green/lime brand accent;
- `--mi-change` is a state/data-change signal, **not** decorative brand paint;
- charts have an independent accessible data-color system;
- success/warning/danger are semantic only;
- default public and app world is high-luminance neutral;
- do not introduce a default full-site dark mode in this reconstruction. If existing user settings contain theme data, do not break those contracts, but do not let legacy dark visuals dictate the new design. A future fully designed dark mode is separate work.

## 6.2 Surfaces

Do not define a universal “premium surface”.

Use boundaries only when information is truly independent/selectable/actionable.

Allowed bounded-object examples:

- a saved-model row/item;
- a discrete feed entry;
- a popover;
- a sheet/dialog;
- a selected input editor;
- a mobile bottom sheet;
- a table row group;
- a genuine data comparison object.

Public narrative chapters should mostly use open composition, media, mathematical fields, typography and whitespace rather than card shells.

## 6.3 Radius

No universal 24–28px radius system.

Recommended functional scale:

```css
--mi-radius-xs: 4px;
--mi-radius-sm: 8px;
--mi-radius-md: 12px;
--mi-radius-lg: 18px;
```

Use `0` for major photography when editorial composition is stronger without rounding.

Avoid pill-shaped containers unless the control semantically benefits from pill geometry (rare).

## 6.4 Shadows

Default major composition uses **little to no shadow**.

Use shadow only for real elevation: floating sheet, menu, dialog, transient overlay.

No cyan/brand glow.

# 7. Typography system

## 7.1 Intended family

**Primary:** ABC Diatype family  
**Mathematical notation:** STIX2 via MathJax 4 where equation rendering is required.

### Licensing rule

Codex must **not scrape, download or embed unlicensed commercial font files**.

If licensed ABC Diatype webfont files are already available locally in the repository or supplied by the user, integrate them with correct `@font-face`, preload only critical cuts, and use WOFF2.

If the files are not available:

- implement the complete type-token system using a neutral fallback stack during engineering;
- keep the intended family names/tokens ready for substitution;
- explicitly report `ABC Diatype licensed files required for final visual acceptance`;
- do not silently replace Diatype with Sora, Inter, Mona Sans, Poppins, Space Grotesk or another trendy font and call the design final.

Suggested fallback during implementation only:

```css
font-family: Arial, "Helvetica Neue", sans-serif;
```

This fallback is not final art approval.

## 7.2 Roles

- Diatype Regular: body, controls, navigation, reading.
- Diatype Medium: selective hierarchy/emphasis.
- Diatype Semi Mono: sparse technical metadata only — simulation IDs, exact compact parameter fingerprints, timestamps where alignment benefits.
- STIX2: actual mathematical expressions/formulas, not decorative labels.

No decorative programmer mono.

## 7.3 Type scale

Target ranges:

| Role | 1440/large | 1366×768 | 390 mobile |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Hero display | 82–92px | 72–78px | 50–56px |
| Major chapter | 54–64px | 48–56px | 36–42px |
| Public subhead | 26–32px | 24–28px | 24–28px |
| Public body | 17–18px | 16–17px | 16px |
| App page title | 30–34px | 28–32px | 24–28px |
| App section | 20–24px | 20–22px | 19–22px |
| Task/body | 15–16px | 15–16px | 16px |
| Parameter labels | 13–14px | 13–14px | 13–14px |
| Metadata | 12–13px | 12–13px | 12px |
| Major numeric result | 48–64px | 42–56px | 36–46px |

Use fluid `clamp()` only where it preserves deliberate line breaks and viewport budgets.

Avoid 700/800/900 as default hierarchy. Most hierarchy should be regular/medium plus scale/spacing/position.

No tiny uppercase eyebrow system.

# 8. Mathematical typography and MathJax

Add MathJax only for pages/components that require formal mathematical typesetting.

Official package: `mathjax@4`.

Implementation rules:

- do not load MathJax globally into the initial homepage bundle if no formula is visible above the fold;
- lazy-load it for Method / Explain / formula-rich states;
- use accessible MathJax output/exploration where practical;
- do not render formulas as PNG/SVG screenshots;
- do not use formulas decoratively to make the site look mathematical.

If integration complexity risks the core reconstruction, keep simple inline equations as semantic text temporarily and isolate MathJax behind a `MathExpression` component so it can be finalized without touching app logic.

# 9. Motion technology ownership

## 9.1 Add Anime.js

Install from the official `animejs` npm package.

Use Anime.js only for local/product-native mathematical interactions:

- direct draggable assumption controls where enhancement is needed;
- SVG path drawing/morphing;
- deterministic trajectory/field transitions;
- parameter-to-visual propagation;
- local compare transitions.

Do not create a second global animation architecture.

## 9.2 GSAP + ScrollTrigger

Retain GSAP.

Use ScrollTrigger only for:

1. desktop `World → Structure` handoff if it genuinely benefits from an owned sequence;
2. desktop Model Worlds persistent-stage progression;
3. Evidence transformation if a persistent owned timeline is materially better than native scrolling.

Do not pin every chapter.

No global ScrollSmoother.

## 9.3 Three.js

Retain Three.js only for real returned 3D data:

- surface;
- scatter 3D;
- multi-trace state space.

Delete the decorative marketing intelligence sphere when no legitimate consumer remains.

## 9.4 React / CSS

React owns real state.

CSS owns ordinary focus/hover/pressed/disabled feedback.

Scroll never chooses a user's simulation parameter or answer.

## 9.5 Motion verbs

All branded motion must map to one of:

- **Propagate** — input changes linked representations;
- **Accumulate** — paths/samples build evidence;
- **Resolve** — running/noisy state settles to result;
- **Compare** — A/B states align and differences become visible;
- **Inspect** — exact evidence appears on user intent;
- **Carry** — one actor persists across scene/state/route;
- **Explain** — formula/annotation connects to evidence.

If a proposed animation cannot be justified by one of these verbs or ordinary UI feedback, remove it.

# 12. Deterministic public model demos

The public experience may demonstrate mathematics, but it may not fabricate authority or random intelligence.

All illustrative public models must:

- be explicitly identified as illustrative/demo;
- use deterministic fixed seeds where pseudo-random sequences are required;
- produce stable results across reloads/builds;
- have formulas/parameters that match the visual behavior;
- never be presented as a forecast, customer result or actual user simulation.

## 12.1 Uncertainty / Monte Carlo

Use a seeded discrete stochastic process:

```text
x_t = x_(t-1) + μ·Δt + σ·sqrt(Δt)·ε_t
```

Fixed defaults:

- start = 0;
- μ = small fixed drift or 0;
- Δt = fixed;
- deterministic PRNG seed;
- N paths chosen for performance and clarity;
- primary user control: `σ`.

Visual outputs:

- path ensemble;
- endpoint density/distribution;
- threshold/tail selection;
- exact probability derived from the deterministic sample.

No random values on render.

## 12.2 Strategy / Game Theory

Use an explicitly defined 2×2 zero-sum matrix whose mixed equilibrium can be calculated deterministically.

User changes one payoff term or controlled scalar.

Visual outputs:

- payoff relationship;
- best-response/equilibrium position;
- mixed-strategy probability change;
- one concise annotation.

Avoid decorative chess imagery.

## 12.3 Dynamics / Market

Use a deterministic seeded AR(1)-style illustrative process:

```text
x_t = ρ·x_(t-1) + ε_t
```

Primary user control: `ρ` persistence.

Visual outputs:

- time-series state;
- range/variation;
- persistence/regime visual behavior.

Label as illustrative process, not market forecast.

## 12.4 Interaction / Conflict

Use a deterministic seeded agent-alignment / neighborhood interaction illustration.

Primary user control: interaction radius `r` or coupling strength.

Visual outputs:

- agent trajectories;
- local interactions;
- global order/coherence metric if correctly derived from the model.

Do not invent “success probability”.

## 12.5 Build / Custom

Do not invent another demo model.

This world transitions to the real Product Model Builder.

- global `useMicroInteractions(location.pathname)`;
- legacy public page imports after redirects/replacements;
- visual hard-coding in `PageLoader` / `ApiErrorToast` based on removed tokens.

Do not implement arbitrary global route zoom/fade for every route. Route transitions should be minimal and contextual.

---

# 14. Public header

## 14.1 Opening state

Header belongs to the Systems Atlas world.

Desktop target:

```text
Math Intellect                      Models   Method   Workbench   Sign in
```

Rules:

- no floating capsule;
- no separate nav slab;
- no decorative divider line;
- no gradient logo mark;
- no tiny tagline;
- no “Live”; no system status;
- wordmark may be text-first until a separately authored brand mark exists.

## 14.2 Released state

After hero release, header may become sticky with opaque/high-luminance background when needed for readability.

Transition ownership should be tied to the hero's actual release state, not an arbitrary global `scrollY > 20` aesthetic threshold.

## 14.3 Mobile

Approx. 58–62px visual zone.

Wordmark left, menu right; workbench action may be visible if geometry allows.

Menu uses accessible dialog/drawer behavior; no glass/neon.

---

# 15. Homepage — seven authored chapters

The homepage is not built from a repeated `<SectionHeader /> + <CardGrid />` primitive.

Each chapter has a different silhouette and information behavior.

## Chapter 01 — Systems Atlas

### Purpose

Establish Math Intellect through real systems and editorial spatial composition.

### Copy

**Headline:** `Model what changes.`

**Support:** `Build simulations for uncertainty, strategy, markets and interacting systems. Inspect the mathematics behind every result.`

**Primary CTA:** `Open workbench`

**Secondary CTA:** `Explore models`

### Desktop 1440×900

- `min-height: 100svh`;
- outer gutters around 48–56px;
- integrated header;
- MI-01 dominant image around 48–54vw visual width and 58–68svh height;
- MI-03 close detail actor around 13–17vw visual width;
- one structural/diagrammatic actor foreshadowing the next transformation;
- typography uses open negative space — no fixed 50/50 grid;
- major image may leave right/top edge;
- no default rounded card framing;
- no metrics strip;
- no hero model/graph as protagonist;
- no old Three.js marketing scene.

### 1366×768

- hero must fit as a composed field without requiring the user to scroll simply to see the headline/CTA;
- title target 72–78px;
- reduce secondary-image pressure before shrinking the dominant image too far;
- all essential controls visible in the opening viewport.

### 390×844

- 18–20px gutters;
- portrait art-directed MI-01 crop;
- title 50–56px;
- third desktop actor may be removed;
- CTA remains reachable without awkward overlap;
- no forced absolute-position collage that clips at 375/360/320.

### Motion

Entry is restrained: media establishes, typography establishes, then stops.

No perpetual floating.

---

## Chapter 02 — World → Structure

### Purpose

Show the conceptual transition from physical system to modelable structure.

### Rule

This is **editorial analogy**, not computer vision or a claimed product feature.

### States

```text
world
→ attention
→ structure
→ model language
→ release
```

Photography decreases in dominance while selected authored lines/relationships gain hierarchy.

Never show scanner lines, object-detection boxes, HUD grids or fake inference labels.

### Desktop motion

May use a short owned ScrollTrigger sequence.

The final structural actor becomes the first visual material of Model Worlds.

### Mobile

Short natural-scroll handoff; no long pin.

### Reduced motion

Static world image followed by resolved structural illustration.

---

## Chapter 03 — Model Worlds

### Purpose

Demonstrate the five real engine families without feature cards.

### Worlds

1. Uncertainty — Monte Carlo
2. Strategy — Game Theory
3. Dynamics — Market
4. Interaction — Conflict
5. Build — Custom/product handoff

### Desktop stage

One viewport-height persistent stage.

Active world receives 55–65% of visual pressure.

Neighboring worlds remain partial context at unequal scales.

Never use same-sized rail cards.

### Required state labels

Implement semantic labels/states, e.g.:

```text
uncertainty-establish
uncertainty-dwell
strategy-transition
strategy-establish
strategy-dwell
dynamics-transition
dynamics-establish
dynamics-dwell
interaction-transition
interaction-establish
interaction-dwell
build-transition
build-establish
build-dwell
release
```

A stable dwell exists after each establish state.

Direct world controls map to the same states/timeline rather than creating a second state machine.

### Uncertainty

Media: MI-05 / MI-01-compatible system imagery.  
Math: deterministic path ensemble → distribution → tail.  
Verb: **Accumulate / Resolve**.  
Copy: `Vary uncertainty. Inspect the spread.`

### Strategy

Media: MI-02.  
Math: defined payoff relationship/equilibrium.  
Verb: **Rebalance** (implemented through Compare/Propagate grammar; do not add a new global motion brand).  
Copy: `Change a payoff. Watch equilibrium move.`

### Dynamics

Media: MI-06.  
Math: deterministic time/process state.  
Verb: **Propagate/Evolve**.  
Copy: `Change persistence. Follow the state through time.`

### Interaction

Media: MI-07.  
Math: deterministic agent interaction/trajectory field.  
Verb: **Propagate**.  
Copy: `Change the rule. See the system reorganize.`

### Build

Photography retreats. Real product Model Builder language enters.  
Copy: `Define the assumptions. Build your own model.`

### Mobile

No desktop pin timeline.

Use one world at a time with:

- large portrait media where applicable;
- mathematical representation;
- direct manipulation;
- direct world selector;
- optional native horizontal snap/swipe, but never swipe-only navigation.

---

## Chapter 04 — Evidence

### Purpose

Show that simulation output becomes inspectable evidence.

### Headline

`From run to evidence.`

### Persistent transformation

Use one stable illustrative result whose representations transform relationally:

```text
samples / paths
→ density
→ distribution
→ selected region
→ exact probability / statistic
→ mathematical explanation
```

Do not create six cards.

The user should understand these are multiple views of the **same result**.

AI/generated interpretation does not appear until mathematical evidence is established.

Desktop may use a compact owned narrative sequence if needed; mobile should remain normal readable vertical flow.

---

## Chapter 05 — Compare

### Purpose

Demonstrate iteration/decision reasoning.

### Headline

`Change one thing. Read the difference.`

### Representation

A and B occupy the same coordinate field.

Do not create `Scenario A` and `Scenario B` cards.

Baseline is quieter.

Changed scenario receives the change signal.

Differences attach to the exact region they describe.

Provide a deterministic input control and an accessible textual summary of the delta.

---

## Chapter 06 — Workbench

### Purpose

Bridge authored public narrative into the actual product.

### Headline

`Build the model yourself.`

### Representation

Do not display a fake browser/device frame.

Use real Product Model Builder DOM/components or a production-faithful non-interactive projection sourced from the same design primitives.

The public visitor should recognize continuity in typography, spacing, mathematical geometry, control design and motion.

Provide direct CTA into signup/login/workbench depending auth state.

---

## Chapter 07 — Resolve

### Purpose

Establish method/epistemic boundaries and end the website intentionally.

### Headline

`Know what came from the model.`

### Support

`Calculated evidence, uncertainty and generated interpretation stay distinct.`

### Visual structure

Simplify the mathematical actor.

Optionally bring MI-08 / MI-03 as a restrained human/physical detail after the dense analytical/product chapters.

Make visible distinctions between:

- calculated result;
- model uncertainty/limits;
- generated interpretation.

Then integrate final workbench action + utility footer into the same composition.

No giant CTA card. No generic black footer slab.

---

# 16. `/models` — engine atlas

Purpose: deeper reference for real simulation families.

Do not make a five-card features page.

Recommended composition:

- compact integrated public header;
- model index that stays available;
- each engine gets its own native visual representation and concise explanation;
- input → behavior → output → what user can inspect;
- illustrative data clearly labeled;
- links to actual Workbench engine selection.

Engine areas:

### Monte Carlo

Show distribution/path logic, uncertainty controls and real result families supported by frontend contracts.

### Game Theory

Show payoff/matrix/equilibrium logic.

### Market

Show time/process state, risk/variation, not fake candles.

### Conflict

Show agents/interaction/outcome logic only where the actual product contract supports it.

### Custom

Show actual build/edit flexibility, not another fabricated visualization.

Avoid repeating one hero pattern five times.

---

# 17. `/workbench` — public product walkthrough

Purpose: prove the actual product, not describe features.

Sequence:

1. choose model/engine;
2. set assumptions;
3. validate;
4. run;
5. inspect result;
6. compare;
7. explain.

Use real product UI primitives.

Do not show fake user data or hard-coded authority metrics.

Do not create device mockups around the UI.

Provide explicit links into signup/login or `/app/simulations/new` depending auth.

---

# 18. `/method` — mathematical method, limits and AI boundary

This route can contain more reading, but it still must not become cards of text.

Use:

- equations;
- diagrams;
- deterministic illustrative plots;
- annotated examples;
- source/provenance distinctions;
- method flow.

Suggested major territories:

1. `What the simulation calculates`
2. `Deterministic vs stochastic`
3. `How uncertainty is represented`
4. `What generated interpretation does`
5. `What generated interpretation does not prove`
6. `Model assumptions and limits`

Only make claims supported by current product/backend behavior.

No invented scientific certification, accuracy percentage, security/compliance claim or retention policy.

`frontend/src/marketing/components/MarketingLayout.tsx` should be substantially rebuilt.

Retain only useful routing/accessibility behavior.

Create a public layout that supports:

- opening integrated header;
- released header state;
- route-level compact header on secondary routes;
- authored footer;
- mobile menu;
- accessibility skip link;
- sensible scroll restoration.

`MarketingCard.tsx` must no longer be the macro composition engine. Delete it if it has no legitimate bounded-object use after reconstruction.

`ProductVisualization.tsx` may be replaced or decomposed; do not preserve invented schematic visuals merely because the component exists.

Replace current radial-gradient fixed-sidebar world.

The rail is calm and functional.

No `Engine Fleet`, fake system health or ambient glow.


# 23. Model Builder — `/app/simulations/new`

This is the core product screen.

`SimulationPage.tsx`, `SimulationForm.tsx` and engine form components should be treated as behavior/data sources, not immutable layout architecture.

## 23.1 Desktop composition

Three functional territories, not three decorative cards:

### Assumptions

Approx. 280–320px at 1440+.

Contains:

- engine selection;
- name/context where required;
- grouped parameters;
- constraints;
- saved model/template behavior where supported;
- validation.

### Model field

Flexible and visually dominant, ideally 680px+ at large desktop.

Shows the mathematical structure relevant to the selected engine.

If a live pre-run preview cannot be truthfully calculated from current client/product logic, show a structural/parameter representation rather than inventing output.

### Inspector

Approx. 280–320px when open.

Contextual/collapsible.

Shows selected parameter definition, units, assumptions, constraints, help and validation.

Do not keep it permanently visible if it has no useful content.

## 23.2 Engine selection

Do not use five large marketing cards.

Use a compact selectable list/index with concise description and relevant preview.

## 23.3 Parameters

- sentence-case labels;
- units visible where known;
- numeric input paired with slider only when continuous manipulation is meaningful;
- no rainbow engine colors;
- no tinted selected card edge;
- validation next to the relevant control;
- preserve accessible labels and keyboard behavior.

## 23.4 Primary actions

Use plain task language:

- `Run simulation`
- `Save model` where supported
- `Reset` where appropriate

Remove:

- Mission Launch;
- Strategic Win;
- predicted skill gain;
- fake estimated duration;
- decorative pre-launch mission card;
- tunnel/rings.

## 23.5 Mobile

The mathematical/model area owns roughly 45–55% of useful viewport height where feasible.

Assumptions use a safe-area-aware bottom sheet / focused edit mode.

Sheet states can be:

- collapsed context;
- half-height edit;
- expanded/full edit.

The model remains visible at collapsed/half states.

Run action remains thumb reachable.

Do not render desktop columns as vertically stacked full-width cards.

---

# 24. Model Builder state matrix

Implement coherent states:

## M0 — engine/new state

Useful engine structure visible immediately.

## M1 — editing

Selected parameter clearly associated with its model representation.

## M2 — valid/ready

Primary run action enabled; no fake celebratory state.

## M3 — invalid

Inline/local errors; preserve user inputs.

## M4 — running

Same workspace remains; truthful real/indeterminate progress.

## M5 — completed

Model/result resolves into result transition; link/route to result workbench.

## M6 — failed

Error attached to run state, retry available, inputs retained.

No full-screen failure theatre.

---

# 25. Running simulation truth contract

Never synthesize progress.

If `useRealtimeSimulation` / API provides real progress:

- show actual progress;
- show actual stage only if backend provides stage semantics.

If only status exists:

- display `Running simulation`;
- optional elapsed time calculated locally;
- indeterminate progress affordance;
- stable assumptions/model context.

Do not infer “Sampling probability space”, “AI interpreting”, etc. unless backend explicitly reports those phases.

---

# 26. Result Workbench — `/app/analytics/:id`

Replace `Overview / Charts / 3D` as primary user IA.

New information architecture:

1. **Result** — What happened?
2. **Uncertainty** — How variable is it?
3. **Drivers** — What influenced it?
4. **Compare** — What changed?
5. **Explain** — Why?
6. **Surface** — conditional, only when meaningful 3D data exists

Use actual available result contracts. Hide a view if required data does not exist.

Do not show an empty “Drivers” tab just because the design lists one.

## 26.1 Result

Show:

- run/model identity;
- execution status/metadata;
- primary real result;
- strongest engine-appropriate representation;
- exact metrics near evidence.

Do not start with four KPI cards.

## 26.2 Uncertainty

Use histogram/CDF/box/ranges/quantiles where available and meaningful.

Missing data is explicitly absent, not zero.

## 26.3 Drivers

Only show real sensitivity/influence/engine-supported evidence.

Never invent feature importance.

## 26.4 Compare

If compare data/history is not available directly, allow the user to select another compatible run if the existing product APIs make that feasible without backend redesign.

Otherwise provide only existing comparison behavior.

Use shared-coordinate representations, not A-card/B-card.

## 26.5 Explain

Separate:

- computed mathematical explanation;
- formula/method;
- generated AI interpretation;
- recommendation/alternatives where actually returned.

Make generated content visibly identified as generated interpretation.

## 26.6 Surface

Render only if real 3D data exists.

Provide a 2D/textual summary/fallback.

---

# 27. Engine-specific visualization grammar

## Monte Carlo

Primary:

- endpoint distribution;
- selected region/tail;
- key exact metric.

Secondary:

- path ensemble;
- CDF;
- box/quantile view.

## Game Theory

Primary:

- payoff relationship/matrix;
- equilibrium/strategy state.

Secondary:

- response or comparison representation where contract supports it.

## Market

Primary:

- time-series state + range/context.

Secondary:

- distribution/risk/regime representation backed by actual result.

Do not generate fake candlesticks from random values.

## Conflict

Primary:

- agent/outcome relationship or returned engine-native result.

Secondary:

- trajectories/heat/state distribution when the backend data supports them.

Do not show meaningless network lines.

## Custom

Representation follows returned data.

Do not force a universal chart merely for consistency.

`ChartRenderer.tsx` is large and may contain useful geometry/data handling. Audit before deleting.

## 28.1 Preserve if correct

- parsing of current chart contracts;
- responsive measurement;
- ResizeObserver;
- value formatting;
- keyboard/touch behavior if already robust;
- low-power/reduced-motion branches;
- 3D data adaptation.

## 28.2 Replace art direction

Remove/rebuild:

- dark glass shell;
- chart glow;
- gradient overlays;
- brand rainbow palette;
- inner glow;
- decorative spring tooltip behavior;
- generic chart-card container.

## 28.3 New chart rules

Default field:

- paper/canvas neutral;
- graphite labels;
- subtle structural grid only when useful;
- exact-value inspection;
- annotation near evidence;
- active selection uses semantic/data color;
- non-color distinction where needed;
- touch equivalent of hover;
- textual summary/table when exact comparison requires it.

## 28.4 Data colors

Create separate accessible utilities for:

- categorical;
- sequential;
- diverging;
- semantic state.

Do not tie all chart colors to product brand.

# 29. 3D result system

`ThreeDTabPanel.tsx` may retain useful renderer/performance logic.

Rules:

- no auto-orbit merely to show 3D.

Delete `frontend/src/marketing/three/IntelligenceSurfaceScene.tsx` if it has no remaining nondecorative consumer after reconstruction.

# 30. AI interpretation design

AI is a secondary interpretive layer.

Correct visual hierarchy:

```text
model
→ calculated output
→ uncertainty/evidence
→ generated interpretation
→ recommendation / alternatives
```

Generated text must be clearly labeled as interpretation when appropriate.

Never use AI as:

- hero icon;
- palette rationale;
- ambient visual field;
- badge system;
- glowing state;
- fake confidence authority.

Do not claim generated confidence is scientific certainty unless backend semantics explicitly define it.

---

# 31. Feed/community reconstruction

`FeedPage.tsx` should preserve real `useSocialFeed` / service behavior, but remove seeded/fabricated community theatre.

Do not show hard-coded:

- active simulator count;
- missions today;
- XP community total;
- fake Top 10 usernames;
- fake trending states.

A real feed item should emphasize:

- author;
- model/scenario;
- small deterministic/real result thumbnail if available;
- time;
- real actions supported by current product (inspect/fork/share/etc.).

Visualize an activity item as content-first editorial object, not a generic social glass card.

If an item needs a boundary because it is independently actionable/selectable, a restrained boundary is valid.

---

# 32. Profile reconstruction

Separate three concerns:

## Identity

- avatar;
- name;
- bio;
- timezone;
- account fields.

## Analytical progression

- actual skill profile/progression values;
- learning/behavior data if truly available;
- calm evidence-based representation.

## Settings

- user preferences;
- notification/theme controls that actually exist.

Remove gamified language as default identity.

XP/badges may remain secondary if backed by product truth.

Prefer precise horizontal measures / lists over decorative radar if comparison/readability is better.

---

# 33. Empty/loading/error-state constitution

Every major protected route needs explicit states.

## Loading

Use task-specific skeleton/placeholder or concise status.

Do not use fake animated data.

## Empty

Explain what is missing and provide one meaningful next action.

Do not fill emptiness with fake charts.

## Error

Preserve user context and retry ability.

Do not clear unsaved Model Builder input because analytics fetch failed.

## Partial

If one AI endpoint fails but mathematical result exists, show result and a local interpretation failure state instead of failing the entire page.

This separation is especially important because AI is not the calculation layer.

---

# 34. Accessibility contract

Target WCAG 2.2 AA as baseline.

Implementation requirements:

- semantic headings with logical hierarchy;
- skip link;
- keyboard access to all controls;
- visible focus;
- no hover-only critical information;
- touch equivalents;
- no color-only state distinction;
- accessible names for icon controls;
- math controls support keyboard increments;
- charts have accessible summary/value alternative;
- 3D has non-3D alternative;
- reduced-motion composition;
- dialogs/sheets trap/restore focus correctly;
- sticky/fixed UI does not obscure focused elements;
- validation programmatically associated with fields;
- route/page title changes sensible;
- loading/status announcements use ARIA live only where useful, not noisy;
- target size appropriate for mobile;
- dragging always has an alternative control method.

### Mathematical accessibility

Where MathJax is used, configure it in a way that retains accessible expression behavior rather than rendering inaccessible decorative output.

---

# 35. Reduced-motion contract

`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` is an alternate understandable composition, not `duration: 0` on a giant pinned story.

Public:

- Systems Atlas becomes static layered editorial composition;
- World → Structure becomes direct state handoff;
- Model Worlds becomes direct selectable worlds without long scrub travel;
- Evidence uses discrete representation changes;
- Compare updates immediately/briefly;
- no parallax.

App:

- all tasks remain functional;
- no auto-animated chart transitions required for comprehension;
- no auto-orbit 3D;
- no decorative pulses.

---

# 36. Performance contract

Performance is part of visual quality.

## 36.1 General

- route-level code split stays;
- do not load Three.js marketing code on homepage if it is not used;
- lazy-load heavy 3D result code;
- lazy-load MathJax where needed;
- only load Anime.js modules/features actually used;
- remove dead old marketing visual code from production bundles;
- avoid giant client-side object arrays when Canvas can render efficiently;
- avoid excessive DOM nodes for path ensembles;
- avoid forced layout loops during scroll.

## 36.2 Images

- local optimized derivatives;
- correct `srcset` / `sizes`;
- hero LCP discoverable early;
- below-fold media lazy loaded;
- Model World neighbors may preload strategically, not all at once;
- explicit width/height/aspect metadata to control CLS;
- do not ship 4K master to 390px phone.

## 36.3 Core quality targets

Aim for good Core Web Vitals in field conditions. Do not sacrifice the first meaningful state for decorative enhancement.

## 36.4 Slow connection

The interface must remain understandable if HD media or 3D is delayed.

Text/navigation/core controls appear independently of optional enhancement.

---

# 37. SEO and metadata

Update `frontend/index.html` and route-level metadata approach as available in the current SPA architecture.

At minimum:

- product title/description no longer use generic “AI intelligence” language;
- meaningful OpenGraph/social title/description;
- accessible favicon/logo treatment;
- canonical path behavior if already supported/deployment appropriate;
- preserve `robots.txt` unless product requirements change;
- no fake structured-data claims/ratings/reviews.

Do not invent schema.org ratings, customers or pricing.

# 40. Copy constitution

Use concrete mathematical verbs/nouns.

Prefer:

```text
model
change
vary
inspect
compare
simulate
sample
estimate
constrain
rerun
explain
isolate
distribution
variance
payoff
equilibrium
scenario
parameter
outcome
uncertainty
```

Avoid repeated identity claims:

```text
premium
powerful
strategic intelligence
cutting-edge
next-generation
high-trust
decision-ready
mission
command
engine fleet
intelligence core
```

No em-dash-heavy AI-copy cadence as a default style.

No section-kicker grammar.

No claim that is not backed by product truth.

---

# 41. State/data truth rules

Hard requirements:

- no `Math.random()` for user-facing prediction/intelligence/progress;
- no hardcoded authority metrics presented as real;
- no fake user/community counts;
- no fake leaderboard;
- no fake “Live” status;
- no fake health status;
- no fake ROI;
- no fabricated confidence;
- no invented progress stage;
- no invented retention/privacy/security/compliance claim;
- no demo data represented as production customer/user data;
- missing data shown as missing/unknown, not zero;
- AI failure does not erase deterministic result if deterministic result is available.

Search the frontend for current violations and remove them from production presentation.

---

# 42. Public/protected visual continuity

The marketing and application worlds must visibly belong to the same product through:

- same typography system;
- same neutral/graphite foundation;
- same mathematical color semantics;
- same annotation style;
- same direct-manipulation philosophy;
- same motion verbs;
- same chart language;
- same spacing discipline.

Do **not** carry marketing cinematic scroll behavior into operational app screens.

Marketing is expressive. Workbench is direct.

---

# 43. Interaction principles

1. Direct manipulation beats decorative explanation.
2. Mathematical changes should update linked representations.
3. User intent controls parameters; scroll does not choose parameter values.
4. Every sticky/pinned actor must arrive, settle, dwell and release coherently.
5. Reverse scroll must be coherent.
6. Fast scroll must not create impossible intermediate states.
7. Mobile never depends on hover.
8. Dragging always has numeric/keyboard alternative.
9. Charts support inspect/select rather than merely animate.
10. Do not delay repeated work with cinematic transitions.

---

# 44. Visual acceptance tests — mandatory

Before declaring completion, run these design tests against actual rendered production routes.

## Blur / silhouette test

Blur/zoom out the public page.

Reject if silhouette becomes:

```text
rectangle
rectangle
rectangle
big rectangle
three rectangles
CTA rectangle
```

## Paragraph-hide test

Temporarily hide body paragraphs.

Core public experience should still communicate:

- real systems;
- model families;
- evidence;
- comparison;
- workbench.

## Swap-logo test

Ask whether the homepage could become another AI SaaS by changing only logo/copy.

If yes, reject.

## Card-count test

Count prominent bounded rectangles on public routes.

If they dominate the silhouette, reject unless semantics require boundaries.

## Typography test

Remove photography. Typography + math should still look authored, not generic AI startup.

## Motion test

Test slow scroll, fast scroll, reverse and micro-oscillation.

Owned actors must establish → dwell → transition coherently.

## Sticky test

Pinned actor reaches intended optical position and stops. If it continuously drifts or swaps before settlement, reject.

## Artifact test

Immediate rejection for:

- duplicate text;
- debug labels;
- transition ghosts;
- accidental guide bars;
- z-index collision;
- clipping;
- broken overlays;
- unintentional giant empty region;
- temporary placeholder copy/asset visible in production.

## Core representation test

If a route can be described as `heading + paragraph + cards + image beside it`, redesign the representation.

---

# 45. Viewport acceptance matrix

## 1440×900

Verify:

- Systems Atlas visual pressure;
- image crops;
- headline/CTA;
- World → Structure continuity;
- Model Worlds dwell;
- Evidence/Compare readability;
- Workbench bridge;
- app workspace widths;
- analytics labels/legends.

## 1366×768

Critical:

- no hero overflow;
- no chapter requiring two scrolls just to see title + active actor;
- Model Worlds active media + title + interaction fit together;
- app top bar/nav do not steal work area;
- Model Builder fields usable without excessive vertical compression.

## 1024×768 / 768×1024

- transition out of desktop rail layout deliberately;
- no “almost desktop” broken composition;
- media crops authored;
- app inspector behavior sensible.

## 430×932 / 390×844

Primary mobile quality gate:

- feels like an app;
- hero art direction intentional;
- Model Worlds touch-native;
- model field remains primary;
- bottom sheet usable;
- chart inspect works on touch;
- bottom nav safe area correct.

## 375 / 360 / 320

- no clipped CTA;
- no hidden form field;
- no horizontal layout concealment;
- no tiny chart labels masquerading as responsiveness;
- no modal/sheet overflow.

# 46. Browser/reduced-motion/failure acceptance

At minimum manually verify current Chrome/Chromium-class desktop and mobile responsive mode.

Also verify:

- `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`;
- keyboard-only navigation;
- touch-like interaction for drag/inspect;
- media request failure/fallback;
- 3D unavailable/low-power fallback;
- API loading/error states;
- unauthenticated public-only redirects;
- authenticated redirect from login/signup;
- protected route behavior;
- browser back/forward scroll behavior.

Do not install a huge E2E framework solely for this visual pass unless one already exists or a focused defect cannot be verified otherwise.
