# 47. Dependency policy

Current dependencies are already sufficient for most work.

Expected additions:

```text
animejs
mathjax@4   (only if/when formal math typesetting implementation is included)
```

Do not add:

- Lenis;
- Barba;
- Framer Motion/Motion just because it is familiar;
- another chart library without a concrete gap;
- Rive without a real authored state-machine need;
- Lottie as a default animation solution;
- another 3D abstraction library;
- component frameworks that impose generic SaaS styling.

If MathJax is deferred behind a clear `MathExpression` adapter because formula pages can ship semantically without it, report that explicitly; do not block the whole reconstruction on ornamental math typesetting.

# 48. Implementation order

Implement in this exact high-level order to minimize regressions.

## Stage 1 — Baseline and safety

1. inspect local git status/HEAD;
2. record current changed/untracked files;
3. do not overwrite unrelated user work;
4. read Brain + Phase 3 spec fully;
5. inspect API/types/hooks/services used by each route;
6. identify backend-coupled frontend behavior.

## Stage 2 — Foundation

1. replace token/type/reset foundation;
2. remove global old background/glow/ripple/microinteraction architecture;
3. create media registry/responsive media primitive;
4. install/import Anime.js only after foundation is clean;
5. add/lazy-isolate math typesetting adapter if used;
6. rebuild public/app shared primitives.

## Stage 3 — Public shell/routes

1. new public layout/header/footer;
2. route map `/models`, `/workbench`, `/method`;
3. redirects;
4. auth restyling can wait until public/product foundation established.

## Stage 4 — Homepage

1. Systems Atlas static composition first;
2. responsive/mobile art direction;
3. World → Structure static states;
4. Model Worlds static/dwell states;
5. Evidence;
6. Compare;
7. Workbench bridge;
8. Resolve;
9. only then add motion.

Do not animate a weak static composition.

## Stage 5 — Secondary public routes

Models → Workbench → Method.

## Stage 6 — App shell/auth

Rebuild navigation, top bar, mobile bottom nav, login/signup.

## Stage 7 — Dashboard

Rebuild around real recent work and empty states.

## Stage 8 — Model Builder

Recompose existing simulation forms/behavior into Assumptions / Model / Inspector.

Remove mission/pre-launch/synthetic state theatre.

## Stage 9 — Running/result

Truthful running states, result IA, charts, compare/explain.

## Stage 10 — Feed/profile

Remove synthetic social theater; rebuild hierarchy.

## Stage 11 — Motion/enhancement

Anime local math interactions; GSAP selected public story sequences; Three conditional 3D.

## Stage 12 — Cleanup

Delete dead old visual code/assets/classes, update imports, remove old fonts/tokens.

## Stage 13 — Validation

Lint/build + focused browser acceptance + final source search for banned artifacts.

# 57. Final implementation quality statement

The reconstruction is successful only if Math Intellect no longer looks like a website decorated to communicate intelligence.

It should feel like an authored system in which:

- high-resolution real-world media establishes the system;
- structure emerges from the world;
- mathematics explains behavior;
- the workbench lets the user change assumptions;
- analytical evidence is inspectable;
- comparison reveals consequence;
- AI interprets rather than visually dominates;
- mobile feels like a purpose-built mathematical application;
- the product remains truthful about what is calculated, unknown, illustrative or generated.

If the final public page can be summarized as:

> “large heading, some explanatory copy, cards, a product screenshot, more cards”

then Phase 3 has failed even if all tests pass.

The intended quality bar is a highly authored, product-specific, award-submission-caliber frontend — not an imitation of award websites, but a Math Intellect experience that derives its visual and interaction grammar from the product itself.

# Personality Assessor — Phase 3 C52 Integrated Product Visual System Board
## Evidence Imprint — Award-Level Pre-Implementation Synthesis

**Date:** 15 August 2026  
**Status:** **PRE-IMPLEMENTATION VISUAL SYSTEM BOARD — NO PRODUCTION CODING YET**  
**Creative thesis:** **Professional evidence as material**  
**Concept:** **The Evidence Imprint**  
**Signature transformation:** **Evidence Lift**  
**Motion verbs:** **Locate → Lift → Resolve → Translate → Align → Return**  
**Primary mobile acceptance canvas:** **390×844**  
**Primary desktop acceptance canvases:** **1440×900 and 1366×768**

---

# 0. What this board is

This is the C52 Integrated Product Visual System Board required by the Valtum Master Brain before a final Codex production contract.

It exists to stop the implementation agent from receiving abstract words such as:

- premium;
- editorial;
- immersive;
- award-level;
- creative;
- smooth;

and resolving them into:

> heading → paragraph → bordered rectangle → cards → image → repeat.

The board therefore turns Phase 1 research and Phase 2 creative-direction thinking into **specific visual states**.

This document is **not** permission for Codex to improvise.

It is also not a coding prototype.

The next production contract must translate these locked frames into exact files, assets, responsive rules and motion code.

---

# 1. External research synthesis applied to this board

This board was refined after another research pass through award-winning and highly recognized interactive work.

## 1.1 Awwwards score structure

Awwwards score pages continue to expose the weighting:

- Design — 40%;
- Usability — 30%;
- Creativity — 20%;
- Content — 10%.

That weighting is useful internally because it demonstrates why a site cannot win primarily through copy.

The visual/interactive system has to carry far more of the experience.

## 1.2 Tracing Art — Resn + Getty

Tracing Art is particularly relevant to Personality Assessor because it faces a similar conceptual challenge:

- a complex evidence domain;
- incomplete and ambiguous records;
- substantial data;
- a need to remain understandable for non-experts;
- a need to preserve rigor.

The project turns archival provenance records into a continuous visual narrative rather than exposing the database as a dashboard of cards.

The important transfer is:

> **complex evidence can remain complex while becoming visually navigable.**

Tracing Art uses:
- narrative chapters;
- timelines;
- archival records;
- data visualization;
- scroll-linked transitions;
- a visual language derived from the source domain.

Personality Assessor should do the same with:
- professional work;
- evidence;
- adaptive questions;
- profile instruments;
- career relationships.

We do not copy Tracing Art’s archival aesthetic or Three.js sphere.

## 1.3 Telescope

Telescope’s team built the identity around a product-native metaphor: zooming in to focus on what matters.

The relevant transfer is not the literal zoom effect.

It is:

> **one metaphor governs brand identity, imagery, typography, interaction and motion.**

Our equivalent is Evidence Imprint / Evidence Lift.

## 1.4 Data Disappeared

This project derived its design core directly from subject matter:
- “visual information decay”;
- outdated governmental data technology;
- punch-card motifs.

The team explicitly researched subject artifacts and converted them into design material.

That reinforces our decision to use:
- actual professional documents;
- plans;
- work surfaces;
- evidence fragments;

rather than generic abstract shapes.

## 1.5 Data visualization studios

Research into data-storytelling practice repeatedly reinforces that a chart should not be treated as a neutral content widget.

The best work asks:
- what pattern matters;
- what story exists inside the data;
- what human relationship must become obvious.

For Personality Assessor:

- Big Five should answer “where are these tendencies positioned?”;
- RIASEC should answer “which vocational territories dominate relative to one another?”;
- Work Values should answer “what is the hierarchy?”;
- Career Signals should answer “which professional evidence relationships are stronger or weaker?”;
- longitudinal analytics should answer “what changed and when?”

The visualization should embody the question.

---

# 2. Board-level success definition

The final system succeeds when:

1. a homepage screenshot is recognizable without logo;
2. paragraphs are not required to understand the story;
3. different routes have distinct silhouettes;
4. professional evidence is a persistent material language;
5. motion visually explains evidence transformation;
6. data visualizations are native representations, not dashboard filler;
7. mobile feels authored separately;
8. operational product UX remains direct;
9. no scene can be described primarily as “heading + paragraph + cards”;
10. no technology appears merely to signal technical sophistication.

---

# 3. Board A — Product visual DNA

## 3.1 Core visual equation

```text
REAL WORK
   ↓
PHOTOGRAPHIC ENVIRONMENT
   ↓
MATERIAL EVIDENCE
   ↓
TRACE / ANNOTATION
   ↓
STRUCTURED INSTRUMENT
   ↓
RELATIONSHIP
   ↓
NEW WORK RETURNS
```

The site does not need a new decorative motif for each section.

These six material states are sufficient.

## 3.2 Protagonist hierarchy

### Level 1 — Environment
Large professional photography.

### Level 2 — Evidence material
Plans, documents, tool/desk fragments, notes, artifact crops.

### Level 3 — Trace
Sparse SVG line/outline/measurement.

### Level 4 — Instrument
Charts and structured interpretation.

The material progresses through these levels.

## 3.3 Visual prohibitions

Never introduce:
- blank floating rectangles pretending to be “artifacts”;
- pills;
- fake scores;
- abstract AI brains;
- personality orbs;
- generic mesh gradients;
- generic corporate vector characters;
- sticky-note decoration with no semantic role;
- random circles/lines merely because the composition is empty.

---

# 4. Board B — Hero final system

## 4.1 Hero message

### H1
**Your work leaves evidence.**

### Support
**See how professional context becomes questions, readings and career direction you can inspect.**

### Actions
**Build my profile**  
**See how it works**

Total visible marketing prose before interaction:
approximately **20–30 words**.

## 4.2 Approved photographic actors

### Actor H1 — Dominant environment
Pexels 9618456  
Role: **source world / professional work**

### Actor H2 — Human proximity
Pexels 5940721  
Role: **professional human presence**

### Actor H3 — Evidence source
Pexels 9617376  
Role: **plan/document material source**

All three remain.

## 4.3 Missing asset family that must be produced before implementation

The existing CSS blank fragments are rejected.

Required local evidence fragment assets:

1. `hero-blueprint-fragment`
2. `hero-document-edge`
3. `hero-tool-fragment`
4. optional `hero-laptop-surface-fragment`
5. mobile-specific `hero-evidence-fragment-mobile`

Preferred creation method:
- crop/extract from approved photo sources;
- use transparent WebP/PNG where actual alpha extraction works;
- otherwise use SVG/CSS mask around real pixels;
- preserve photographic texture.

CSS `mask-image`, SVG `<mask>` and `clip-path` are now broadly available enough to support this kind of non-rectangular media treatment in modern browsers, while still requiring a simple rectangular fallback when necessary.

## 4.4 Desktop 1440×900 composition

```text
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ brand            nav                              sign in    primary      │
│                                                                          │
│                         [evidence source — partial]                       │
│                                                                          │
│ Your work                 ╲                                              │
│ leaves evidence.        [lifted imprint]     [dominant work environment] │
│                ───────────────╲───────────────────────────────────────     │
│ support copy                    ╲                                         │
│ CTA   text action                [human/professional crop]                │
│                                                                          │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Key rule:
the dominant photo must cross the invisible text/media boundary.

The composition must not resolve into two columns.

## 4.5 Optical geometry

### Header
- integrated over hero;
- 64–72px visual height;
- transparent;
- no horizontal divider.

### H1
- x: 4–5vw;
- top: ~29–34svh;
- width: 47–54vw;
- Source Serif 4;
- ~82–96px depending viewport;
- line height ~0.9–0.95.

### Dominant image
- x: 44–49vw;
- y: ~23–26svh;
- width: 47–53vw;
- height: 48–54svh.

### Evidence source
- upper right / behind;
- width 14–20vw;
- intentionally partially cropped.

### Human crop
- lower right / foreground;
- width 18–23vw;
- overlap dominant image.

### Lifted imprint
- 9–15vw;
- crosses type/media seam;
- no UI border/shadow.

## 4.6 1366×768

Hero should feel compressed, not cropped.

Targets:
- H1 ~76–84px;

# 24. Board V — Performance contract

## Images
- local derivatives;
- AVIF/WebP/JPG fallback;
- `<picture>` for art-directed crops;
- proper `srcset` / `sizes`;
- explicit dimensions.

Responsive image guidance consistently shows that serving desktop-size media to mobile wastes substantial bandwidth and can delay LCP.

## Hero
Only the true LCP actor receives high priority.

Do not eagerly load every overlapping hero image at maximum priority.

## Motion
Prefer transform/opacity for large DOM movement.

Mask/clip effects should be tested on target devices because paint-heavy operations can become expensive.

Use `will-change` temporarily and sparingly.

## WebGL
Not required.

## Target
- LCP <= 2.5s where practical;
- CLS <= 0.1;
- INP <= 200ms where practical.

- no autoplay sound;
- direct next/back alternatives for scroll storytelling;
- touch target comfort;
- no color-only encoding;
- headings remain logical despite visual interlock.

SVG/animation must avoid flashing and respect motion preferences.

# 29. Award-level judge simulation

This is an internal critique exercise, not a prediction.

## Design — target 9/10
Questions:
- is the hero recognizable?
- does the composition feel authored?
- are imagery and typography interlocked?
- are all scenes visually resolved?

## Usability — target 8.5–9/10
Questions:
- can users still navigate without scroll tricks?
- are controls obvious?
- is mobile direct?
- does reduced motion work?
- does product UX remain fast?

## Creativity — target 9/10
Questions:
- is Evidence Imprint specific to this product?
- does the site demonstrate rather than decorate?
- are route silhouettes meaningfully different?
- could a template builder plausibly generate the same thing?

## Content — target 8+/10
Questions:
- is the copy concise?
- is methodology truthful?
- are demo values clearly labeled?
- is AI/scoring separation accurate?

# Personality Assessor — Phase 1 Award-Level Creative Intelligence Research
**Date:** 15 August 2026  
**Status:** Research / Creative Direction Foundation — **DO NOT IMPLEMENT YET**  
**Purpose:** Rebuild the creative decision-making model before another line of redesign code is written.

---

# 0. Executive conclusion

The current Personality Assessor is not failing because it needs another spacing patch, another set of rounded corners, another scroll library, or another pass of “make this section premium.”

It is failing because the design process has repeatedly started from **content units** instead of a **creative concept**.

The current thinking pattern has been:

> What content do we need?  
> Put that content in a section.  
> Put the section in a rectangle.  
> Add an image.  
> Add motion to the rectangle.  
> Repeat.

That process can produce a competent SaaS website. It cannot reliably produce an award-level authored digital experience.

The new process must reverse the order:

> What single idea can this product uniquely own?  
> What visual behavior embodies that idea?  
> What is the persistent protagonist?  
> What should the user *experience* instead of read?  
> What content can therefore disappear?  
> What technology is actually necessary to make that experience real?  
> How does the same idea become native on mobile?

This report establishes that new mental model.

---

# 1. The screenshots: what is objectively wrong

The latest screenshots are valuable because they make the failure visible without looking at source code.

## 1.1 Hero

What improved:
- Source Serif 4 gives the opening more humanity than the previous all-grotesk system.
- The three approved images are directionally useful.
- The opening statement is concise.

What still fails:
- the media still reads as large rectangles layered over each other;
- the small white/gray “material fragments” look like blank cards/placeholders;
- the header is still a separate white horizontal slab rather than part of the hero world;
- the composition still resolves into “large copy zone + media zone”;
- the hero does not yet contain a unique behavior that belongs to Personality Assessor;
- a visible horizontal scrollbar indicates unresolved viewport composition.

The hero is aesthetically improved, but it is still a **layout** rather than an **idea**.

## 1.2 Work Worlds

The section is:
- heading;
- paragraph;
- six text navigation items;
- one giant rectangular image;
- one label;
- one large sentence.

This is cleaner than the previous card carousel, but still not creatively authored.

The main problem is not card radius. It is that **the world itself does not transform**. We are simply replacing a large media rectangle and changing text.

A truly authored Work Worlds scene should make the same evidence protagonist behave differently in each professional environment.

## 1.3 Context → Question

This screenshot demonstrates the recurring failure most clearly:

- heading;
- explanatory paragraph;
- uppercase “Illustrative Interaction” label;
- white document card;
- uppercase “Professional Context Document” label;
- uppercase “Adaptive Prompt” label;
- question text;
- three large horizontal answer cards.

This is still the TEXT–CONTAINER–CARD LOOP.

The page tells the visitor that evidence becomes a question, but visually it shows **a document card beside a form**.

The visual behavior does not embody the proposition.

## 1.4 Career relationship

The route is:
- a vertical role list;
- percentages;
- one large rectangular image;
- three explanatory text blocks below.

Again, the information is valid enough as demo content, but the representation is not authored enough.

“Career relationship” should feel like a relationship map / tension / alignment field, not a directory beside a photograph.

## 1.5 Development loop

This is currently:
- one large image on the left;
- five stacked rows on the right:
  - Gap
  - Work
  - Artifact
  - Evidence
  - Return

This is exactly the anti-pattern in another form:

> five horizontal cards stacked vertically.

The content is describing a loop while the composition is linear and static.

## 1.6 Trust

The dark background changed, but the information architecture did not.

It is still:
- heading;
- paragraph;
- four equal text columns;
- dot;
- heading;
- paragraph;
- divider;
- links.

Changing the canvas to black does not create a new design idea.

---

# 2. The award-scoring reality

A useful correction: “design and creativity are 75%” is not the visible Awwwards formula.

Awwwards score pages expose:

- **Design: 40%**
- **Usability: 30%**
- **Creativity: 20%**
- **Content: 10%**

That is an extremely important framing for this project.

It means:

> Design + Usability + Creativity = **90%**  
> Content = **10%**

The current Personality Assessor has repeatedly optimized the 10% category — written explanation — while underinvesting in the other 90%.

This does **not** mean text is unimportant. It means content must become part of a designed experience rather than being the experience itself.

CSS Design Awards evaluates:
- UI;
- UX;
- Innovation.

Its published FAQ says WOTD consideration generally requires an average judge score above approximately 8.0, subject to the quality of the submission pool.

The Webby Awards judge Websites and Mobile Sites on:
- content;
- structure/navigation;
- visual design;
- functionality;
- interactivity;
- innovation;
- overall experience.

Therefore the correct internal target is not:
> “Does the homepage look stylish?”

It is:
> “Does every layer — visual system, interaction, mobile usability, performance, structure, content and technology — reinforce one authored idea?”

---

# 3. The “designer brain” behind top-tier work

Award-winning studios do not start with components.

They work through a sequence closer to this:

## Step 1 — Find an ownable truth

Not:
> What is our hero layout?

But:
> What idea is genuinely native to this brand/product?

Examples:
- Vizcom: **sketch becomes product**.
- Zoox: the **physical form of the vehicle** becomes the visual grammar.
- MindMarket: **human connection / listening** becomes a persistent visual thread.
- Obys: **Obys as a space**; identity, logo, type and layout become one system.
- Oryzo: an ordinary physical product is treated with absurd premium seriousness, inside a believable desk world.
- Bruno Simon: a portfolio becomes a world you literally drive through.

The best concept is not a decoration.
It explains why the site looks and behaves the way it does.

## Step 2 — Define the protagonist

The strongest experiences usually have something that survives longer than one section:

- a product;
- a character;
- a line/thread;
- a vehicle form;
- a logo;
- an object;
- a camera/world;
- a material;
- a transformation.

A persistent protagonist creates continuity. Without one, each section becomes a new template.

## Step 3 — Storyboard behavior before components

Dogstudio describes beginning Zoox with many low-fidelity sketches for:
- motion;
- transitions;
- content.

Only after the motion/story thinking did they resolve the wireframe and final system.

The key implication:

**We should sketch what happens, not just where boxes go.**

## Step 4 — Turn the concept into a grammar

A good concept affects:
- crop;
- shape;
- typography;
- motion;
- navigation;
- data representation;
- image behavior;
- transitions;
- even error/empty states.

Zoox is a strong example: the rounded vehicle shape influences frames, borders, buttons and art direction.

## Step 5 — Remove anything the experience already explains

OFF+BRAND’s Vizcom case study is explicit: the hero is a short story — sketch → transform → iterate — so visitors understand the product without long explanation.

Lusion’s Oryzo team reached a similar conclusion from a different direction:
- fewer typefaces;
- fewer colors;
- fewer UI ideas;
- UI supports the visual world.

Award-level restraint is not “minimalism.”
It is **removing redundant explanation because the design already communicates it.**

## Step 6 — Choose technology after the concept

Lusion states this directly: the pipeline follows the idea, not the other way around.

Obys used:
- Bun;
- React only for server-side templating;
- TypeScript interactions;
- an in-house RAF + WAAPI animation system;
- native WebGL;
- Strapi;
- plain CSS.

Vizcom used:
- Webflow;
- WebGL/3D;
- Rive;
- GSAP.

Zoox used WebGL because it solved the fidelity/asset-weight experience problem.

The lesson is not “copy their stack.”

The lesson is:
> **technology is an implementation consequence of the creative idea.**

## Step 7 — Refine in browser

Obys explains that much of the time was spent refining:
- timing;
- spacing;
- behavior;
- micro-interactions

during development.

The effortless feeling is not produced by a one-shot design file.
It is tuned in the real medium.

---

# 4. Seven case-study lessons we should internalize

## 4.1 Oryzo / Lusion — believable world + controlled UI

Why it matters:
Personality Assessor has also become too sterile and “designed by UI components.”

Key lesson:
Oryzo’s early clean studio-style concept looked polished but felt lifeless. The team improved it by placing the protagonist inside a believable work desk environment.

Their principles:
- realistic image;
- product at the center;
- seamless transitions;
- humor.

They then intentionally reduced:
- typefaces;
- colors;
- UI styles.

**Personality translation:**
We need believable professional evidence worlds — real work, real material, real artifacts — not more informational panels.

## 4.2 MindMarket / KOKI-KIKO — make an intangible service visible

This is one of the closest conceptual references to our problem.

MindMarket is a qualitative research company. Their business value is intangible: human understanding.

Instead of explaining research through business cards and service paragraphs, they created:
- a persistent connecting visual thread;
- custom hand-drawn illustrations;
- animation as narrative structure;
- depth through layered scenes.

The design expresses **how the company thinks**.

**Personality translation:**
Psychological/professional interpretation is also intangible.
We need a visual mechanism that makes interpretation *feel physical*.

## 4.3 Vizcom / OFF+BRAND — the experience is the explanation

Objective:
make Vizcom understandable within seconds.

Solution:
the hero literally demonstrates:
- sketch;
- transformation;
- iteration.

The visual proves the headline.

**Personality translation:**
A visitor should see:
> work evidence → interpretation → adaptive question → profile relationship

before reading a methodology paragraph.

## 4.4 Zoox / Dogstudio — product-native geometry

Dogstudio did not invent random “premium shapes.”
They used the actual rounded geometry of the Zoox vehicle throughout the visual language.

**Personality translation:**
We need a native material/behavior from professional evidence itself — not arbitrary circles, rounded cards or abstract AI geometry.

## 4.5 Obys — identity system before website layout

The new Obys did not begin with page wireframes.
It began with a custom typeface.

That typeface then influenced:
- rhythm;
- hierarchy;
- spacing;
- identity.

The logo became an active interface participant and persisted across layouts.

The team also intentionally excluded non-essential content.

**Personality translation:**
We should stop treating typography as a token choice made after the page structure.
Type, image material, movement and product concept should be designed together.

## 4.6 Anime.js — documentation as product demonstration

The Anime.js website is powerful because the website **behaves like the product it is selling**.

It does not merely claim:
> “We support SVG morphing.”

The site demonstrates:
- SVG morphing;
- line drawing;
- motion paths;
- timelines;
- draggable interactions;
- staggering;
- scroll synchronization;
- responsive animation behavior.

The interface becomes proof.

**Personality translation:**
The Personality Assessor site should demonstrate interpretation rather than explain interpretation.

## 4.7 GQ × Audemars Piguet / Immersive Garden — coherence over excess

The important lesson from high-end cinematic projects is not “use 3D.”

It is:
- continuous pacing;
- precise transitions;
- attention to material;
- camera restraint;
- timing;
- scene coherence.

The strongest immersive sites often hold the camera still long enough for the subject to matter.

**Personality translation:**
Our current long scrubs are not premium simply because they move.
The user needs complete, composed dwell states.

---

# 5. What creativity actually means in our project

Creativity is not:
- another layout;
- more offset grids;
- a bigger serif;
- rounded image collage;
- horizontal cards instead of vertical cards;
- parallax;
- pinning;
- a WebGL orb;
- adding Anime.js.

Creativity is:

> **finding a product-native visual rule that can generate many coherent moments.**

A creative rule should answer:
- Why are the images cropped this way?
- Why does this object move?
- Why does this chart use this representation?
- Why does the hero transition into the next chapter?
- Why does mobile behave differently?
- Why does the page feel like this product and no other one?

If we cannot answer those questions from one central idea, the site is still a collection of layouts.

---

# 6. Recommended creative territory for Personality Assessor

## Working concept: **THE IMPRINT / PROFESSIONAL EVIDENCE AS MATERIAL**

This is a research recommendation, not yet the final visual lock.

Core idea:

> Work leaves an imprint.  
> Personality Assessor reveals, separates and reconnects those imprints.

The website should treat professional evidence as **material**, not content cards.

### The protagonist

Not a line copied from MindMarket.

Not a 3D sphere.

Not a card.

The protagonist is a **changing evidence surface / imprint** derived from real work:
- a crop of a plan;
- a document layer;
- a work photograph;
- a hand-made annotation;
- an extracted contour;
- a trace;
- a structured measurement.

The same material changes form as the visitor progresses.

### Hero

Real work environments overlap like a physical analysis table.

The title is not beside the world; it participates in it.

A real evidence fragment crosses the typographic field.

One visual “imprint” is extracted from the environment.

### Work Worlds

Do not swap giant photos.

The evidence imprint enters six environments.

Each environment changes:
- crop;
- scale;
- movement;
- texture;
- evidence behavior.

The world demonstrates a different professional mode.

### Evidence → Question

The extracted material is isolated.

Unimportant context physically falls away.

The remaining evidence reshapes/repositions into the origin of the adaptive question.

The question is born from the visual evidence, not rendered in a form card beside it.

### Profile

The same evidence separates into four analytical grammars:
- Big Five;
- RIASEC;
- Work Values;
- Career Signals.

They should not all look like bars inside containers.
Each becomes its own spatial representation.

### Career

Multiple profile/evidence traces converge around a role environment.

“Fit” is shown as a relationship:
- aligned;
- stretched;
- unsupported;
- developable.

Not simply a percent beside a role name.

### Development

A new work artifact re-enters the system.

The visual literally returns to the earlier evidence material, closing the loop.

This is much closer to an ownable concept than “professional site with images and charts.”

---

# 7. A new content rule: copy must earn screen space

Homepage content should be treated as part of composition.

Recommended target:
- H1: 3–7 words;
- scene statement: 3–8 words;
- support line: 8–20 words;
- detailed methodology lives deeper;
- visual labels only when interaction genuinely needs them.

New test:

> If we hide all body paragraphs, can a visitor still understand the product’s central story?

If no, the visual system is not doing enough work.

For an award-level public homepage, the goal should be that **most understanding is carried by image, interaction, data relationship and motion**.

---

# 8. Typography research direction

Typography must not be selected as a fashionable afterthought.

The Obys case is useful because type was foundational, not decorative.

For Personality Assessor:

## Current direction worth preserving
- Source Serif 4 has improved the hero.
- Source Sans 3 remains suitable for product/UI readability.

## What still needs improvement
The type system is currently used conventionally:
- big H1;
- standard H2;
- paragraph;
- uppercase label.

The next stage needs typography to behave spatially:
- type behind/through image;
- cropped scale transitions;
- variable optical hierarchy;
- large quiet editorial statements;
- product UI typography that is operational rather than decorative;
- very few uppercase micro-labels.

Do not solve personality through “fancy font.”
Solve it through:
- scale;
- rhythm;
- line break;
- alignment;
- relationship to media;
- motion;
- silence.

---

# 9. Color research direction

Award-level color is usually concept-dependent.

There is no requirement to have a permanent “brand accent.”

The current neutral white / black foundation is useful because it allows:
- professional photography;
- evidence material;
- illustration;
- data semantics

to supply color.

But neutral must not become sterile.

We should introduce color through **evidence worlds**, not through UI chrome:
- real blueprints;
- highlighter marks;
- natural work materials;
- professional environments;
- chart semantics;
- custom illustration if commissioned.

No arbitrary colored borders.

No “AI purple.”

No generic premium olive.

No gradient identity.

---

# 10. Technology intelligence

The current app already includes:
- React 19;
- Vite;
- GSAP;
- Framer Motion;
- Three / React Three Fiber / Drei;
- Recharts;
- Barba;
- Lottie.

The problem is not a lack of libraries.

The problem is that our creative concept has not been strong enough to justify how they are used.

## 10.1 GSAP

Keep for **macro narrative ownership**:
- long scroll-linked transformations;
- true pinning;
- scene-to-scene carry;
- complex cross-actor sequencing.

Use sparingly.

One scene = one clear owner.

## 10.2 Anime.js v4

Anime.js is highly relevant, but **not as a replacement badge**.

Current official Anime.js capabilities include:
- `createTimeline()`;
- timeline labels;
- ScrollObserver / `onScroll()`;
- advanced staggering;
- SVG morphing;
- SVG line drawing;
- motion paths;
- draggable + springs;
- Scope/media-query handling;
- WAAPI-powered lightweight animations.

The official site itself won Awwwards Site of the Month in May 2025 and a Developer Award.

### Where Anime.js could be valuable for Personality Assessor

Use it for **local, crafted kinetic systems**:

1. evidence lines drawing/retracting;
2. SVG contour morphing;
3. evidence fragments converging;
4. profile relationships;
5. chart/micro-diagram transformations;
6. draggable/inspectable career relationship surfaces;
7. text/character micro-choreography;
8. local responsive animation scopes.

### Where NOT to use Anime.js

Do not use Anime.js:
- to duplicate a GSAP ScrollTrigger scene;
- simply because its website looks good;
- for a second global smooth-scroll owner;
- to animate every section;
- as a reason to increase motion density.

### Ownership model if both libraries are used

**GSAP**
- macro scroll story;
- pinning;
- large cross-section transitions.

**Anime.js**
- local DOM/SVG choreography;
- path drawing;
- morphing;
- staggered evidence/data behavior;
- draggable micro-experiences.

**Framer Motion**
- authenticated application state;
- React layout transitions;
- sheets/panels/list-detail.

**CSS / WAAPI**
- basic hover/focus/press;
- cheap single-element transitions.

Never let two libraries own the same transform on the same actor.

## 10.3 Anime.js module strategy

Do not import the full toolbox by habit.

Anime.js documents a modular architecture.

Potential imports:
- timeline;
- animation;
- SVG;
- stagger;
- Scope;
- WAAPI where appropriate.

Use WAAPI for simple compositor-friendly micro-motion.
Use Anime.js JS animation for:
- SVG attributes;
- complex timelines;
- high target counts;
- richer callbacks/control.

## 10.4 Rive

Rive is useful only if we create original illustration/motion assets.

Possible use:
- one custom evidence character/object;
- responsive illustration system;
- controlled state-machine visual.

Do not use:
- marketplace stock illustrations;
- generic corporate characters.

## 10.5 WebGL / Three / R3F

Not mandatory.

Use only if the concept gains something impossible or significantly weaker in DOM/SVG.

Possible justified use:
- a real spatial evidence world;
- one persistent material object that transforms continuously;
- highly tactile 3D data/evidence surface.

Not justified:
- a floating personality sphere;
- random particles;
- “3D because awards.”

A strong 2.5D DOM/SVG experience can be more original and faster.

## 10.6 Theater.js

Interesting only if we commit to a cinematic 3D/visual timeline that requires designer/developer tuning in-context.

Do not add for this product unless the selected concept clearly requires it.

## 10.7 Native Web Animations API

Worth using for:
- small performant visual states;
- simple load/hover/transition;
- compositor-friendly movement.

Anime.js WAAPI is useful when we want a consistent interface around WAAPI.

---

# 11. Mobile-first at award level

“Responsive” is not enough.

Desktop award sites often fail on mobile because the cinematic desktop idea is merely collapsed.

Our mobile rule:

> **same concept, different choreography.**

At 390×844:

- one primary actor at a time;
- touch is direct;
- no hover dependency;
- no long desktop pin;
- no tiny landscape image;
- portrait crops are independently directed;
- bottom navigation for authenticated product;
- safe-area-aware actions;
- less text than desktop when necessary;
- transitions are shorter and more tactile;
- scroll does not fight the browser;
- 44px+ frequent touch targets;
- no horizontal overflow.

Mobile should feel like a deliberate companion application.

For the public story, this may mean:
- vertical evidence transformations rather than horizontal rails;
- direct swipes/taps;
- full-screen inspection scenes;
- native sheets for detail;
- persistent but compact evidence protagonist.

---

# 12. Performance is part of creativity

Award-level does not excuse slow interaction.

A creative effect that destroys mobile responsiveness is not premium.

Internal targets:
- LCP <= 2.5s where practical;
- CLS <= 0.1;
- INP <= 200ms where practical;
- no long main-thread animation loops without need;
- responsive AVIF/WebP;
- explicit image sizing;
- lazy below-fold media;
- no unnecessary high-priority preloads;
- reduced-motion alternative;
- no global WebGL if only one small scene needs it.

The creative team must design within the performance budget from the beginning.

---

# 13. New award-level internal scorecard

This is an **internal target**, not a promise of an award.

## Awwwards-style target
- Design: **9.0**
- Usability: **8.5**
- Creativity: **9.0**
- Content: **8.0**

The goal is not to game scoring.
It is to force us to ask why the experience deserves a 9.

## CSSDA-style target
- UI: **8.7+**
- UX: **8.5+**
- Innovation: **8.7+**

## Internal extra categories
- Concept ownership: 9/10
- Mobile authorship: 9/10
- Performance: 8.5+/10
- Accessibility: 8.5+/10
- Motion coherence: 9/10
- Template distance: 9.5/10

If any scene is obviously reproducible by a generic AI builder, it fails regardless of average score.

---

# 14. New creative acceptance tests

## 14.1 No-copy test
Hide paragraphs.

If the idea disappears, fail.

## 14.2 Grey-box test
Replace all media with grey boxes.

If the site becomes the same template as any SaaS product, fail.

## 14.3 Screenshot silhouette test
Blur the page.

If it becomes a stack of rectangles, fail.

## 14.4 Swap-brand test
Replace “Personality Assessor” with another SaaS company.

If composition still makes sense unchanged, fail.

## 14.5 Motion mute test
Disable animation.

The static composition must still be strong.

## 14.6 Motion purpose test
For every animation ask:
> What relationship does this explain?

No answer = remove it.

## 14.7 Mobile-only test
Review the entire product without looking at desktop.

If it feels like a derivative version, fail.

## 14.8 3D deletion test
If deleting WebGL changes nothing about the concept, WebGL was unnecessary.

## 14.9 Card count test
If public narrative is visually dominated by bounded rectangles, fail.

## 14.10 Design-to-content ratio test
Estimate what percentage of understanding is carried by:
- interaction;
- image;
- visual relationship;
- motion;
- spatial hierarchy

versus paragraphs.

If text still carries most of the meaning, the creative system is underdeveloped.

---

Do not:

- create another 50-page implementation spec while the creative idea is still weak.

# 18. Final Phase 1 thesis

The current site is not missing “better cards.”

It is missing a **creative thesis**.

Award-level digital work is not created by arranging content more elegantly.
It is created by turning the brand/product truth into a visual and interactive system that could not belong to anyone else.

For Personality Assessor, the next successful design must make **professional evidence physically and visually transform into interpretation**.

The site should become understandable through:
- material;
- movement;
- photography;
- data;
- spatial relationship;
- interaction.

Text becomes supporting evidence.

Not the website itself.

**Do not code Phase 2 until this creative direction is locked.**

# Personality Assessor — Phase 2 Creative Concept Lock
## Award-Level Creative Direction, Storyboard, Interaction Grammar & Technology Ownership

**Date:** 15 August 2026  
**Status:** **CREATIVE DIRECTION LOCK — DO NOT IMPLEMENT YET**  
**Prerequisites:** Phase 1 Award-Level Creative Intelligence Research + Valtum Master Brain C52/C53 + latest screenshot-forensic rejection evidence  
**Next gate after this document:** C52 Integrated Product Visual System Board  
**Implementation agent status:** Codex must not receive a new redesign instruction until the visual system board is approved.

---

# 0. Why this phase exists

Phase 1 established that the Personality Assessor problem is not a lack of styling, animation libraries, cards with better spacing, or cleaner CSS.

The failure is upstream:

> the website has repeatedly been designed as information containers instead of a single authored digital idea.

Phase 2 therefore does not ask:
- what section should come next;
- what card style should replace the old card;
- what animation can be added to an existing layout.

It asks:

> **What creative idea is native enough to Personality Assessor that it can generate the hero, motion, imagery, typography, data visualization, secondary routes, mobile choreography and product interface without falling back to a template?**

The answer locked by this phase is:

# **THE EVIDENCE IMPRINT**

---

# 1. Research basis used for this lock

This concept was selected after another research pass through:

- Awwwards scoring and Site-of-the-Month examples;
- OFF+BRAND / Vizcom;
- OFF+BRAND / Lando Norris;
- Lusion / Oryzo BTS;
- Dogstudio / Zoox;
- Obys identity and studio process;
- Obys Design Books;
- KOKI-KIKO / MindMarket;
- Adrien Vanderpotte’s creative-development process;
- Akaru studio methodology;
- Anime.js v4 documentation and current release;
- Apple HIG mobile layout/navigation/safe-area guidance;
- the current Personality Assessor source;
- the latest rejected browser screenshots;
- Valtum Master Brain C52/C53.

The strongest repeated principle was not a particular technology.

It was:

> **Find one product-native behavior, make it physically legible, then let the whole experience inherit that behavior.**

Obys describes storytelling as the invisible structure holding the experience together and explicitly treats websites like editorial compositions with tension, contrast and silence rather than collections of paragraphs. Their current identity work also begins from a central system — type and the “Obys as a space” concept — before page composition.

Dogstudio’s Zoox case study follows the same logic through product form: the rounded vehicle geometry became an art-direction rule across the interface.

Vizcom demonstrates the product workflow instead of explaining it through long copy.

MindMarket translates an intangible B2B value into a visible narrative device.

Adrien Vanderpotte describes the search for a project-specific “feeling” or digital signature and repeatedly ties motion language to the literal character of the brand.

The concept below is our product-specific translation of those principles.

---

# 2. Creative territories considered

A serious creative process should demonstrate that the chosen idea survived alternatives rather than simply being the first metaphor found.

## Territory A — “The Evidence Thread”

**Idea:** a continuous line connects work, questions, profile and career.

### Strengths
- easy continuity;
- strong SVG motion opportunity;
- excellent mobile translation;
- understandable metaphor.

### Rejection
Too close in spirit to MindMarket’s award-winning connecting-thread mechanism.

Even if executed differently, a persistent line as the dominant identity creates unnecessary anti-copy risk and weakens authorship.

**Status:** REJECTED AS PRIMARY CONCEPT.

A line may exist as a subordinate measurement/annotation device, but it cannot be the central brand metaphor.

---

## Territory B — “The Interpretation Lens”

**Idea:** work is inspected through changing optical lenses.

### Strengths
- excellent for zoom/focus transitions;
- useful for methodology;
- natural connection to investigation/analysis.

### Rejection
Too easy to become:
- magnifying-glass UI;
- microscope cliché;
- circular-mask gimmick;
- generic “AI lens” visual language.

The metaphor also explains inspection better than it explains development and returning evidence.

**Status:** REJECTED.

---

## Territory C — “The Career Atlas”

**Idea:** profile dimensions form an explorable territory/map.

### Strengths
- strong career route;
- strong data-viz potential;
- spatially rich;
- useful for master-detail.

### Rejection
It explains only the output side of the product.

It does not naturally explain:
- CV/context;
- adaptive question formation;
- evidence extraction;
- profile change after new work.

**Status:** RETAIN AS SECONDARY CAREER REPRESENTATION ONLY.

---

## Territory D — **“The Evidence Imprint”**

**Idea:** professional work leaves material traces. The product lifts those traces from real work, separates them, interprets them, maps relationships, and accepts new evidence back into the profile.

### Why this is stronger
It explains the entire product loop:

`WORK → IMPRINT → ISOLATE → INTERPRET → RELATE → RETURN`

It naturally combines:
- professional photography;
- paper/documents;
- annotation;
- data;
- motion;
- tactile interaction;
- transparent/irregular crops;
- charts;
- responsive app states.

It does not require WebGL.

It can use sophisticated SVG/DOM motion.

It is not dependent on one stylistic trend.

It remains meaningful with motion disabled.

**Status: SELECTED / LOCKED CREATIVE TERRITORY.**

---

# 3. The one-sentence creative thesis

> **Your work leaves an imprint. Personality Assessor lifts that evidence out of the work itself, separates what it can support, and turns it into an inspectable professional profile.**

This sentence is the conceptual source of the entire site.

If a visual decision cannot plausibly be traced back to this thesis, it is probably decoration.

---

# 4. The persistent protagonist

The persistent protagonist is:

# **THE EVIDENCE IMPRINT**

It is **not one literal object** repeated identically.

It is a coherent family of physical/digital states derived from the same evidence material.

The imprint can appear as:

- an irregular crop lifted from real professional photography;
- a blueprint/document fragment;
- a contour generated from the edge of a real artifact;
- an annotation trace;
- a clipped phrase;
- a measured line;
- a set of separated signals;
- a data visualization;
- a relationship path;
- a returned artifact.

## 4.1 Four material layers

### A. Environment
Real professional photography.

This establishes where evidence came from.

### B. Material
Paper, plans, notebook edges, code/work surfaces, documents, physical project artifacts.

This makes “evidence” tangible.

### C. Trace
Sparse SVG contour/measurement/annotation behavior.

This reveals what the product is noticing.

### D. Instrument
Charts/data representations.

This reveals how evidence becomes a structured reading.

These four layers create the visual system.

Cards do not.

---

# 5. The signature behavior

The site's digital signature is:

# **THE EVIDENCE LIFT**

A meaningful part of a source environment appears to detach from that environment and become the material for the next interpretation.

The behavior has five phases:

1. **Locate** — evidence exists inside the real work.
2. **Lift** — a meaningful fragment separates from its source.
3. **Resolve** — noise drops away; the fragment becomes legible.
4. **Translate** — the same material changes into question/data/relationship.
5. **Return** — new work becomes new evidence and rejoins the system.

This behavior is the equivalent of:
- Vizcom’s sketch → render transformation;
- Zoox’s vehicle-derived geometry;
- MindMarket’s human connection system;

but is product-specific to Personality Assessor.

---

# 6. Static design principle

A crucial rule:

> **The page must remain excellent when all motion is disabled.**

Motion connects strong frames.

Motion cannot rescue weak frames.

Every dwell state must therefore be composed as if it were:
- a campaign still;
- an editorial spread;
- a portfolio screenshot.

The user should be able to stop scrolling anywhere important and see a finished frame.

---

# 7. Homepage story — seven authored acts

The homepage is no longer a set of “sections.”

It is a seven-act narrative.

## ACT I — WORK / THE IMPRINT EXISTS
Hero

## ACT II — DIFFERENT WORK / DIFFERENT IMPRINTS
Work Worlds

## ACT III — EVIDENCE BECOMES A QUESTION
Adaptive transformation

## ACT IV — ONE PERSON / FOUR INSTRUMENTS
Living profile

## ACT V — PROFILE MEETS A ROLE
Career relationship

## ACT VI — NEW WORK RETURNS
Development loop

## ACT VII — WHAT SHAPED THE RESULT
Trust + resolution + footer

Each act must have a different silhouette.

---

# 8. ACT I — Hero storyboard

## 8.1 Goal

Within the first 3–5 seconds, the visitor should understand:

- this product starts from real professional work;
- it extracts meaningful evidence from that work;
- the site itself is authored, not templated.

The hero should be strong enough that Valtum could use a screenshot of it as a portfolio cover.

## 8.2 Copy

### H1
**Your work leaves evidence.**

This remains strong.

### Support
One line only, approximately:

**See how professional context becomes questions, readings and career direction you can inspect.**

### Actions
- `Build my profile`
- `See how it works`

No eyebrow.
No metadata.
No fake score.
No decorative label.

## 8.3 Desktop visual composition

Do not use left column / right image.

Use one shared canvas.

### Typography
The H1 occupies roughly 48–55% of visual width but is allowed to cross the media boundary.

The word `evidence` should have a deliberate relationship with the evidence wall / lifted material.

### Photography
Keep the three approved images:
- architecture/workspace;
- professional/laptop context;
- evidence/plans wall.

But their roles become:

**dominant environment**  
**human proximity**  
**evidence source**

not “large photo / small photo / third photo.”

### Material imprint
A real irregular fragment is visually extracted from the plans/evidence source.

No blank CSS rectangle.

Preferred production:
- generate a local transparent PNG/WebP cutout from an approved photograph;
- or use a tight image fragment with SVG mask/clipPath;
- retain authentic texture.

The imprint should visibly originate from the source image.

## 8.4 Arrival motion

On load:

1. headline establishes;
2. environment establishes;
3. human plane enters;
4. evidence source settles;
5. a contour quietly appears around one material fragment;
6. the fragment lifts 8–18px in perceived depth and stops.

No looping hover.
No perpetual floating.

## 8.5 First scroll

The environment does not instantly disappear.

The imprint becomes the transition actor.

It moves toward the centre/next scene while the source world recedes.

This is the first proof that the site is one continuous experience.

---

# 9. ACT II — Work Worlds as transformations, not slides

## 9.1 Core idea

The same evidence material behaves differently depending on the work environment.

The user is not browsing a gallery.

They are observing **six modes of professional evidence**.

## 9.2 Six visual behaviors

### Build
Visual grammar:
- rectilinear construction;
- alignment;
- measured edges;
- grid/blueprint logic.

The imprint snaps into structural alignment.

### Investigate
Visual grammar:
- isolate;
- compare;
- reveal;
- inspect.

Unrelated information recedes while one trace becomes precise.

### Make
Visual grammar:
- iteration;
- repetition;
- accumulated versions.

The imprint leaves 2–3 controlled historical echoes before settling.

### Shape
Visual grammar:
- responsive contour;
- ambiguity becoming form.

The imprint morphs between two related silhouettes.

### Structure
Visual grammar:
- hierarchy;
- grouping;
- nested system.

The imprint separates into organized layers.

### Collaborate
Visual grammar:
- convergence;
- overlap;
- shared boundaries.

Two or three evidence fragments align into one shared state.

These behaviors are not decorative.
They illustrate different professional modes.

## 9.3 Media composition

One persistent environment stage.

Not six equal cards.

Not one huge 56svh generic rectangle.

Preferred desktop protagonist height:
**approximately 42–46svh**.

Surrounding visual context:
- previous world fragment;
- next world fragment;
- evidence imprint;
- current mode statement.

## 9.4 Copy

Scene title:
**Work changes the evidence.**

World copy remains extremely short.

No long detail descriptions.

## 9.5 Motion ownership

**GSAP ScrollTrigger** owns macro world transitions and scroll state.

**Anime.js** may own the local SVG/material transformation inside each settled world.

GSAP does not animate the same SVG property that Anime.js owns.

---

# 10. ACT III — Evidence becomes the question

This is the most important product-demonstration scene.

## 10.1 Current anti-pattern to eliminate completely

Do not show:

`document card | question form`

The user must watch one become the other.

## 10.2 Initial frame

A professional evidence field occupies the viewport.

It should look more like:
- a real document surface;
- an editorial analysis table;
- a crop from actual work;

than a UI panel.

No white card outline is required.

## 10.3 Scroll choreography

### State 1 — Source
Full context visible.

### State 2 — Noise recedes
Less relevant text/material physically loses contrast.

### State 3 — Evidence remains
One meaningful phrase/fragment stays in focus.

### State 4 — Lift
The phrase/material detaches from the document coordinate system.

### State 5 — Translate
The fragment travels toward the question origin.

The question begins from the same spatial coordinate.

### State 6 — Question established
Document is now context in the background.

### State 7 — Response controls establish
Actual task controls appear.

Then scrolling stops changing personalization.

## 10.4 Response control design

Responses are real controls, so boundaries are allowed.

But avoid card syntax.

Preferred:
- open rows;
- hairline separators;
- one circular/neutral selection marker;
- generous vertical spacing;
- no tinted fill;
- no shadow;
- no colored side edge.

## 10.5 User action

Only click/tap/keyboard selection creates the next micro-transition.

The chosen response compresses into a **qualitative evidence trace**.

Public demo result example:

**Reliability first under delivery pressure**

Not:
- +22;
- 88%;
- “feeds Conscientiousness”;
- fake confidence.

A small note can say:
`Illustrative interaction`

only once, away from the main composition.

---

# 11. ACT IV — Four instruments, one profile

## 11.1 Creative idea

The evidence imprint does not become one magic personality score.

It passes through **four different instruments**.

This gives us a powerful anti-card structure.

The four readings are not four cards.

They are four ways of looking at the same material.

## 11.2 Navigation

Desktop:
- short text index;
- no pills;
- no card tab bar;
- active instrument communicated by position, weight and moving line.

Mobile:
- compact direct segmented navigation or swipe + explicit labels;
- native touch;
- one instrument owns the screen.

## 11.3 Instrument A — Big Five

Visual:
- five strong horizontal lollipops;
- no container;
- generous negative space;
- labels + exact illustrative values only where explicitly marked as demo.

Motion:
- evidence trace resolves into five axes.

## 11.4 Instrument B — RIASEC

Visual:
- true radar geometry;
- ranked textual list;
- one shape, not six cards.

Motion:
- the five-axis field collapses/repositions into six radial directions.

## 11.5 Instrument C — Work Values

Visual:
- ordered vertical/horizontal hierarchy;
- physical ranking;
- bar lengths or typographic order.

Motion:
- radial structure straightens into ordered priorities.

## 11.6 Instrument D — Career Signals

Visual:
- sparse evidence-linked lollipops/relationship measures;
- selected evidence examples may appear as small material fragments.

Motion:
- hierarchy reconnects to source evidence.

## 11.7 Technology

**Anime.js SVG**
- `createDrawable()` for line construction;
- `morphTo()` for controlled shape changes;
- `createTimeline()` for instrument transformations.

Framer Motion may manage React selection/layout if easier, but do not let two systems own the same actor.

---

# 12. ACT V — Career relationship, not career cards

## 12.1 Core idea

A career is a **relationship field**, not a tile with a percentage.

Public marketing should not make demo percentages the protagonist.

## 12.2 Visual structure

Desktop:

### Left / edge
Editorial role index, open type.

### Centre
Dominant active work environment.

### Around/over environment
Three profile-to-role relationships:
- `aligned`;
- `stretch`;
- `evidence to build`.

These appear as spatial traces/measurements.

### Lower/side
Short explanation for the currently inspected relationship.

No three boxes.

## 12.3 Interaction

Hover can preview on fine pointer.

Click establishes.

On touch:
- role list → focused full-screen detail;
- back preserves list position.

## 12.4 Optional draggable R&D

A small relationship marker could be draggable on desktop/tablet to inspect one dimension.

If used:
- it must clarify the relationship;
- keyboard alternative required;
- mobile does not depend on dragging.

Anime.js `createDraggable()` is a viable implementation tool.

This remains optional until the visual board proves value.

---

# 13. ACT VI — The return loop must actually loop

## 13.1 Core idea

Current UI says:

Gap → Work → Artifact → Evidence → Return

but visually renders five stacked rows.

The new composition must behave circularly.

## 13.2 Desktop storyboard

A professional artifact travels through one continuous loop:

1. **Gap** — a missing/weak trace is visible in the profile.
2. **Work** — environment/media expands around it.
3. **Artifact** — a real output fragment forms.
4. **Evidence** — the artifact is outlined/lifted.
5. **Return** — it physically re-enters the profile/instrument field.

The same object should be visually recognizable at stages 3–5.

## 13.3 Composition

Use:
- one dominant image/media;
- one artifact fragment;
- one profile visualization;
- a controlled curved path/sequence.

No five stacked cards.

No five equal paragraphs.

No numbered steps.

## 13.4 Mobile

Natural vertical sequence.

The artifact remains sticky for a limited distance while the context changes around it.

No long desktop pin.

---

# 14. ACT VII — Trust as a cutaway, not a list

## 14.1 Creative idea

Trust means the system can be **opened and inspected**.

Represent the product as a cutaway / provenance stack.

## 14.2 Visual structure

One evidence imprint enters from the left/top.

It passes through:

**Context**  
→ **Structured scoring**  
→ **Narrative assistance**  
→ **Your controls**

But these are layers of one system, not four equal columns/cards.

Each layer should reveal only the minimum necessary copy.

## 14.3 AI/scoring truth

Public copy must preserve actual nuance:

- deterministic logic produces structured numeric profile/career outputs;
- AI may assist context/free-text interpretation and narrative explanation when configured;
- AI prose must not fabricate or override stored deterministic outputs.

Never claim that AI is “air-gapped” from every scoring input if free-text/context interpretation can use AI upstream.

## 14.4 Footer transition

The provenance structure resolves into the footer.

The footer feels like the same world reaching its conclusion.

No separate generic footer slab.

---

# 15. Header creative lock

The header must be part of the opening visual field.

## Desktop hero state
- transparent;
- no bottom divider;
- no white slab;
- no blur pill;
- dark text over light hero.

When hero releases:
- compact neutral navigation surface may appear;
- transition tied to hero state, not arbitrary scrollY.

## Mobile
- brand;
- menu;
- optionally one primary action;
- ~60px plus safe area;
- opens into an intentionally composed navigation view.

The header should not visually divide the page before the hero has started.

---

# 16. Typography behavior lock

## 16.1 Families

Continue the stronger current direction:

### Source Serif 4 Variable
Narrative / reflective voice.

Use for:
- hero;
- 2–3 major statements;
- final resolution.

### Source Sans 3 Variable
Operational / analytical voice.

Use for:
- navigation;
- controls;
- body;
- data;
- app;
- assessment.

## 16.2 New behavior

The improvement now comes from **behavior and composition**, not another font switch.

### Serif behavior
- large optical sizing;
- restrained weight;
- strong line breaks;
- image overlap where safe;
- occasional italic only when editorial meaning supports it.

### Sans behavior
- compact;
- calm;
- no constant uppercase;
- no decorative eyebrows;
- tabular figures for data.

## 16.3 Ban

No:
- giant centered H2 every scene;
- uppercase helper text as design decoration;
- tiny gray label before every heading;
- 600 weight everywhere;
- paragraph blocks over ~55–65 characters per line on public story pages.

---

# 17. Color behavior lock

## 17.1 Base

Keep:
- true white;
- true near-black;
- cool neutral grays.

## 17.2 Scene chroma inheritance

Public storytelling gains color from the media itself.

Each Work World can define a restrained `sceneChroma` value sampled from its approved photography.

That color may affect:
- one SVG trace;
- one small annotation;
- a subtle material state.

It may **not** become:
- a full UI accent system;
- colored card edges;
- selected backgrounds;
- gradient scenes.

This creates visual variation without inventing a generic brand accent.

## 17.3 Analytical scenes

Return mostly to monochrome.

Semantic data colors remain separate and truthful.

---

# 18. Media / artifact language

## 18.1 Photography

Use real professional environments.

Photographs must be:
- spatial actors;
- sources of evidence;
- scene environments;
- transition material.

Not content illustrations beside text.

## 18.2 Transparent / masked material

The user specifically values background-removed material.

Phase 2 therefore locks a **real evidence-fragment asset family**.

Required categories:
- blueprint/plan fragment;
- document/paper edge;
- notebook/tool fragment;
- laptop/work surface fragment;
- one human/material close crop.

These should be extracted from approved photography or sourced/shot with consistent visual quality.

Do not fake them with empty CSS rectangles.

## 18.3 Texture

Subtle real material texture is allowed.

No artificial paper-grain overlay sprayed across the entire site.

---

# 19. Secondary route creative silhouettes

The six public routes must demonstrate the same creative thesis without becoming the same page.

## 19.1 How It Works — **Exploded Evidence Engine**

One persistent evidence artifact moves through:
- context;
- question;
- four instruments;
- career relationship.

This is a continuous transformation stage.

No text rail + image swap.

## 19.2 Career Intelligence — **Relationship Field**

Dark or neutral immersive field.

Roles exist as an index around one active professional environment.

Profile traces converge/diverge around the role.

No role cards.

## 19.3 Progress — **Return Loop**

The development loop becomes the entire page logic.

Mixed-scale work images and artifacts sit around a returning evidence trajectory.

No numbered chronology.

## 19.4 Methodology — **Instrument Bench**

Four full analytical instruments.

The user chooses an instrument and the entire field changes representation.

Longer methodological detail is progressively disclosed below/inside the instrument.

No framework cards.

## 19.5 Trust — **System Cutaway**

Show product layers and boundaries in one provenance composition.

No numbered flow boxes.

## 19.6 Privacy — **Ownership Map**

Represent:
- what enters;
- what is stored;
- what can be exported;
- what can be deleted.

Actual destructive actions remain conventional/clear in the authenticated product.

Public page remains visual and factual.

---

# 20. Auth creative direction

Auth must be calmer than marketing.

It should still belong to the evidence world.

## Desktop
- form is protagonist;
- one evidence imprint or approved photo fragment inhabits the surrounding field;
- narrative serif phrase optional;
- no 50/50 SaaS split;
- no stock rectangle.

## Mobile
Form first.

No user should scroll through an award-showcase scene before creating an account.

---

# 21. Authenticated product translation

Award-level marketing does not justify turning the application into a cinematic experiment.

The product adopts the **instrument** side of the creative language.

## Dashboard
Open analytical fields.

Cards only for genuinely independent records/actions.

## Assessment
Task-first.

One question owns the screen.

## Results
Four instruments.

## Analytics
Questions + visual answers.

## Career Explorer
Relationship field.

## Privacy
Ownership/actions.

The evidence imprint may appear subtly as:
- selected-source marker;
- chart trace;
- empty-state graphic;
- evidence provenance.

It should not become decorative noise in operational UI.

---

# 22. Mobile creative lock — “app-native companion”

390×844 is a primary canvas.

## 22.1 Public hero
- full-screen authored composition;
- portrait crops;
- one dominant environment;
- one human/support plane;
- one evidence fragment;
- title interlock;
- no desktop collage shrink.

## 22.2 Work Worlds
Natural vertical/touch story.

One world at a time.

Optional horizontal gesture only as an enhancement.

## 22.3 Evidence → Question
Vertical transformation.

No pin longer than feels native.

Question/action remains reachable.

## 22.4 Profile
One instrument per screen.

Direct swipe/tap.

## 22.5 Career
List → full-screen detail.

## 22.6 Protected app
Persistent bottom tab navigation for top-level destinations.

Apple’s current HIG supports tab bars as persistent top-level navigation and recommends keeping them visible to preserve orientation/state.

## 22.7 Safe areas
Respect:
- Dynamic Island/camera housing;
- browser chrome;
- bottom safe area;
- tab bar.

## 22.8 Touch
Frequent controls target ~44px minimum.

No hover-only behavior.

---

# 23. Technology ownership lock

This is the first phase where adding Anime.js becomes justified by the concept.

## 23.1 GSAP 3.15 + ScrollTrigger

**Macro narrative owner**

Use for:
- hero → Work Worlds carry;
- desktop Work Worlds state transitions;
- Evidence → Question scroll choreography;
- How It Works persistent process;
- limited cross-scene scroll ownership.

Do not use for:
- every hover;
- every metric;
- every app state.

## 23.2 Anime.js v4

**Local material / SVG choreography owner**

Recommended version at the time of research:
`animejs@4.5.0`

Official current v4 capabilities relevant here:
- `createTimeline()`;
- timeline labels;
- `svg.createDrawable()`;
- `svg.morphTo()`;
- SVG motion paths;
- `createDraggable()`;
- `createScope()` for React roots/media queries/cleanup;
- WAAPI wrapper for lightweight compositor motion.

### Exact expected use
- draw evidence contours;
- morph evidence imprint shapes;
- animate measurement traces;
- instrument-to-instrument SVG transforms;
- local staggered material construction;
- optional career relationship drag/inspect.

### React discipline
Create one Anime.js `Scope` per owned scene/component.

Revert on cleanup.

## 23.3 Anime.js WAAPI mode

Use `waapi.animate()` for:
- simple transform;
- opacity;
- lightweight local motion.

Anime.js documentation notes WAAPI can be smaller/lighter and can run supported compositor properties efficiently.

Use JS Anime `animate()` when:
- SVG attributes;
- complex timeline;
- many targets;
- advanced callbacks/control.

## 23.4 Framer Motion

**Application state owner**

Use for:
- dashboard layout state;
- master-detail;
- sheets;
- tabs/lenses;
- mobile screen transitions;
- route/state relationships inside protected app.

## 23.5 CSS

Use for:
- hover;
- focus;
- press;
- basic transitions.

## 23.6 Three / R3F

**Not part of the locked core concept.**

Do not use WebGL merely to chase awards.

The Evidence Imprint can be executed more uniquely and efficiently in:
- DOM;
- SVG;
- responsive photography.

A future isolated R&D prototype may test one spatial scene, but Phase 2 does not authorize WebGL production usage.

## 23.7 Rive

Not required unless a genuinely custom illustration system is commissioned.

## 23.8 Scroll source

Native browser scroll remains the source of truth.

No Lenis.

No global ScrollSmoother.

---

# 24. Motion vocabulary

The site gets a limited vocabulary.

## Locate
Subtle contour/attention.

## Lift
Evidence separates from source.

## Resolve
Noise fades; important material becomes legible.

## Translate
One material changes representational form.

## Align
Relationships snap/settle into meaningful structure.

## Return
New evidence rejoins profile.

These six verbs replace generic:
- fade up;
- float;
- parallax;
- slide in.

For every motion, name which verb it belongs to.

If it belongs to none, remove it.

---

# 25. Timing character

The site should feel:
- intelligent;
- physical;
- responsive;
- calm.

Not:
- bouncy;
- game-like;
- over-eased;
- lethargic.

## Micro
160–240ms.

## Local material
320–650ms.

## Major settle
600–900ms.

## Scroll scrub catch-up
small, generally ~0.2–0.4 where GSAP scrub is used.

## Dwell
Every important state rests long enough to inspect.

No endless movement.

---

# 26. Content deletion map

The current site is still over-written.

Phase 2 locks an aggressive reduction.

## Homepage target

The public homepage should normally contain approximately **140–220 words of non-navigation explanatory prose**, excluding:
- control labels;
- alt/accessibility text;
- legal footer;
- data labels.

This is an art-direction target, not an SEO law.

## Remove / compress

### Work Worlds
No long section explanation + long world detail.

### Evidence Question
No paragraph explaining what the animation itself shows.

### Living Profile
No paragraph under every trait.

### Career
No long why/stretch/strengthen wall on homepage.

### Development
No five explanatory paragraphs.

### Trust
No four feature paragraphs.

Detailed explanation moves to dedicated routes.

---

# 27. The anti-copy rules

Our references teach principles.

Do not copy their signatures.

## Do not copy MindMarket
- no single persistent thread as the whole identity;
- no custom character looking at cursor CTA;
- no three-layer thread narrative.

## Do not copy Vizcom
- no sketch-to-render car/product transformation;
- no workstation scene imitation.

## Do not copy Oryzo
- no coaster;
- no ironic startup satire;
- no olive/cream/orange desk aesthetic.

## Do not copy Zoox
- no rounded-product-derived border system;
- no autonomous vehicle camera language.

## Do not copy Obys
- no persistent logo-in-corner system as our main trick;
- no direct imitation of their custom grotesk/modernist identity.

We borrow **thinking discipline**.

Not surfaces.

- can the evidence fragment carry between two static scene compositions without clipping?
- can a 390px mobile instrument transition remain readable?

These experiments must:
- test one unknown;
- not become a hidden redesign site;
- not ask Codex to invent visual direction.

# 31. Phase 2 hard lock

The following are now fixed for the next visual-board stage:

### Creative thesis
**Professional evidence as material.**

### Concept name
**The Evidence Imprint.**

### Signature behavior
**Evidence Lift.**

### Transformation verbs
**Locate → Lift → Resolve → Translate → Align → Return.**

### Persistent protagonist
A real professional evidence imprint that changes representation across the experience.

### Copy role
Supporting actor, not protagonist.

### Hero
Three approved professional images + real material fragment extraction.

### Public composition
Open editorial/spatial scenes; no card-led narrative.

### Profile
Four visual instruments, not four cards.

### Career
Relationship field, not role cards.

### Development
True return loop.

### Trust
System cutaway/provenance.

### Mobile
Independent app-native choreography.

### Macro motion
GSAP ScrollTrigger.

### Local SVG/material motion
Anime.js v4.

### Protected React state motion
Framer Motion.

### WebGL
Not part of the core production concept.

### Scroll engine
Native browser scroll.

### Typography
Source Serif 4 + Source Sans 3, improved through composition rather than another fashion-driven font replacement.

### Core palette
Neutral gallery with chroma borrowed sparingly from real media.

If the scene could belong unchanged to:
- an AI startup;
- a courier service;
- a design agency;
- a fintech dashboard;
- an HR SaaS;

stop.

The representation is not specific enough.

# 1. THE NON-NEGOTIABLE CREATIVE IDEA

# THE EVIDENCE IMPRINT

Creative thesis:

> **Your work leaves an imprint. Personality Assessor lifts evidence out of the work itself, separates what it can support, and turns it into an inspectable professional profile.**

Signature behavior:

# EVIDENCE LIFT

Motion/meaning verbs:

**Locate → Lift → Resolve → Translate → Align → Return**

The complete public experience must feel generated by those six verbs.

If an implementation detail cannot be connected to this thesis, it is probably decoration and should be removed.

# 4. VERIFIED PRODUCT TRUTH — BINDING COPY RULES

## 4.1 Adaptive assessment

Current backend truth:
- base questionnaire target: **22 questions**;
- possible maximum: **26**;
- supplemental extension step: **4**;
- extension logic uses confidence/coverage conditions;
- first questions may cycle through MCQ, Likert, slider and text formats;
- AI-assisted CV/context extraction and adaptive question generation are part of the current pipeline.

Therefore public copy may say:
- questions adapt to professional context and assessment coverage;
- additional questions may be used when more evidence is needed.

Do **not** promise:
- that every user gets fewer questions;
- that “AI chooses the perfect question in real time” unless that specific behavior is verified;
- exact completion-time claims unless measured.

## 4.2 Scoring

The structured scoring orchestrator produces:
- Big Five;
- RIASEC;
- Work Values;
- Career Signals;
- score validity;
- evidence counts/sources;
- missing evidence/dimensions;
- warnings;
- confidence metadata.

It marks structured score source as:
`deterministic`.

Correct public framing:

> Structured score outputs are computed by versioned scoring logic from captured evidence. AI may assist with context/free-text interpretation and narrative explanation when configured; generated narrative must not fabricate or override stored structured outputs.

Do not say:
- “AI never touches scoring inputs”;
- “AI is fully air-gapped from scoring”;
- “AI determines your personality score”;
- “scientifically 98% accurate”;
- “clinical”;
- “diagnostic.”

## 4.3 Missing data

Missing = unknown.

Never present missing as:
- 0;
- 50;
- 80%;
- average;
- midpoint;
- default fit.

Use:
- `Not available`
- `Not enough evidence`
- `Not enough history`
- no plotted point.

## 4.4 Public demo data

`personalityMarketingDemo.js` contains illustrative values.

All public numerical demo fields must have one nearby field-level disclosure:

`Illustrative example`

Do not repeat disclaimers beside every number.

Do not let demo career percentages read like real personal recommendations.

## 4.5 Privacy

Only claim controls/contracts actually supported by source.

Do not invent:
- exact retention periods;
- one-click permanent purge;
- model-training policies;
- advertising/data-sale policies;
- printable export formats;
- guaranteed deletion timing;

unless verified directly in current backend/product policy.

# 6. MOTION OWNERSHIP — HARD BOUNDARIES

## GSAP + ScrollTrigger = macro scroll narrative

Owns:
- hero → Work Worlds handoff;
- Work Worlds desktop;
- Evidence → Question desktop scroll choreography;
- How It Works desktop exploded engine;
- any one clearly justified cross-scene carry.

One flagship scene should normally have:
- one GSAP timeline;
- one ScrollTrigger.

Use semantic timeline labels.

Do not animate a ScrollTrigger’s pinned element itself; animate descendants.

## Anime.js = local Evidence Imprint / SVG material

Owns:
- SVG contour draw;
- contour morph;
- evidence trace construction;
- local instrument transformation;
- local evidence-return animation;
- optional career inspection drag if included.

Each React owner creates an Anime `createScope({ root })` and reverts it on cleanup.

## Framer Motion = protected application state

Owns:
- list ↔ detail;
- sheets;
- dashboard maturity layout transitions;
- instrument selection inside protected app;
- mobile UI state;
- panel reflow.

## CSS / WAAPI = microfeedback

Owns:
- hover;
- focus;
- press;
- simple opacity/transform transitions.

## Double-ownership prohibition

GSAP and Anime.js may not write the same animated property on the same element.

Define ownership in code comments near each complex scene.

# 41. PERFORMANCE CONTRACT

- high fetch priority.

Do not mark all layered images high priority.

## Below-fold
Lazy load.

## Fragments
Keep small.

## SVG
Inline/local.

## Anime.js
Import only needed APIs or allow bundler tree-shaking.

## GSAP
No per-pixel React state updates.

Avoid:
- `setState()` every ScrollTrigger tick unless unavoidable;
- state derived from raw progress where semantic labels work.

## Resize
Refresh ScrollTrigger after fonts/media stabilize where needed.
